 403: #### 1.5.1.5 The Canon
 404: *Upon the exclamation 'By the mercy and compassions,' the Priest anoints, and the choirs sing the Canon. If there was no All-Night Vigil, then the choirs sing the Canon, and the Priest does not anoint.*
 405: 
 406: *The Canon, not in the Great Forty Days, usually consists of eight odes, and in the Forty Days - of nine. The eight odes of the canon, outside the Forty Days, are designated by numbers: 1st, 3rd, 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th and 9th. Although the canon consists only of eight odes, nevertheless, its heirmoi reach in number to the 9th ode; the second ode is not taken. The reason for this lies in the fact that the number of heirmoi is different than the number of odes of Holy Scripture, the content of which they contain in an abbreviated form. However, because the content of the second ode of Holy Scripture corresponds only to the penitential season, the heirmoi of the canon, except for the Lenten canon, do not include this ode, but only the eight aforementioned, without the second.*
 407: 
 408: *Of such canons at Matins, Great or Small, there can be either one, or two, or three, or four. One or two (usually two) occur on Feasts of the Lord and of the Theotokos; whether there are two canons, or only one, their troparia are taken together to [make] 12, excluding the heirmoi, and the heirmoi twice. In other cases it is necessary to distinguish: for there can be a service of a Saint in the middle of a Feast, that is in the Fore- or Afterfeast of a Feast of the Lord or of the Theotokos, or the service of a Saint may fall outside a Feast, then either alone, or with the Octoechos service.*
 409: 
 410: *In the first case, the troparia of each ode are taken to [make] 12 together with the heirmos of the first canon*[^30]*, the heirmoi of the other canons are not taken; for although they are presented at the beginning of their odes, they serve only as a model, or for the form of singing for their subsequent troparia. Only, if two Saints with their own services fall in the middle of a Feast, then the troparia of each ode are taken to [make] 14, together with the heirmos of the first canon. In the second case, the troparia of each ode are taken to [make] 14, together with the heirmos of the first: one heirmos and 13 troparia*[^31]*.*
 411: 
 412: *Upon the conclusion of the last troparion of each ode, the current Katavasia*[^32]* is sung, if the heirmos of some of the canons of the Feasts of the Lord or of the Theotokos is presented, or the general heirmos of the Theotokos service of Tone 4 'I shall open my mouth.' These heirmoi of the aforementioned Feasts are used not only at Great Matins on the day of the Feasts themselves, but also at all Great Matins throughout the whole year within the limits defined by the Typikon.*
 413: 
 414: *Refrains to the odes of the canon are now not taken from the odes placed at the end of the Psalter (for we limit them to the penitential days of the Great Forty Days), but are used in the following manner:*
 415: 1. *If it is a canon of a Feast of the Lord, we say: 'Glory, O Lord, to Thy holy Transfiguration (or Nativity, or other, depending on the Feast).' In the Cross canon: 'Glory, O Lord, to Thy Cross and Crucifixion'*[^33]*.* *In the Resurrection canon on Sunday: 'Glory, O Lord, to Thy holy Resurrection.'* *In the Resurrection and Cross [canon]: 'Glory, O Lord, to Thy Cross and Resurrection.'* *In the Paschal canon: 'Christ is risen from the dead.'* *In the Triadic canon: 'O Most Holy Trinity, our God, glory to Thee.'* *In the canon of the Descent of the Holy Spirit and in the canon of all other services of the Lord, Feasts and Penitential [services]: 'Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee.'*
 416: 2. *If it is a canon of a service to the Theotokos: 'O Most Holy Theotokos, save us.'*
 417: 3. *If it is a canon of a service to a Saint, then His rank is named, as indicated in the Menaion, and the name is added: 'Pray to God for us.' E. g.: 'Holy Hieromartyr Josaphat, pray to God for us.'* *On the Feast of All Saints: 'All Saints, pray to God for us.'*
 418: 4. *In the canon for the Dead: 'Rest, O Lord, the soul of Thy departed servant' or in the plural: 'The souls of Thy departed servants.'*
 419: 
 420: *Because at Matins usually there are several canons, each ode of which ends with a Theotokion, to the Theotokia of all canons, except the last, we add the aforementioned refrain to the Theotokos: 'O Most Holy Theotokos, save us,' and before the Theotokion of the last - we add 'Both now,' and before the last troparion of the last canon we add 'Glory,' regardless of whether it will be a Theotokion, or some other.*
 421: 
 422: *In a mixed canon, that is such a one where some troparia will be of one kind of Saints, and others - of another, as happens in the weekday service of the Octoechos, before each troparion a verse is added, according to its rank or content.*
 423: 
 424: *Before the heirmoi we add nothing, but if there is one service of a Feast of the Lord or of the Theotokos, then at the 9th Ode, instead of the general refrains, we sing refrains proper (given at the 9th Ode of the canon of the Feast) to all its troparia, including to the penultimate and last, instead of 'Glory, Both now,' and also to its heirmoi and Katavasia.*
 425: 
 426: *Although now we do not use the Odes of Holy Scripture presented at the end of the Psalter, excluding the Forty Days, nevertheless, we leave something from them, that is at the 8th Ode, instead of Glory - the refrain 'Let us bless the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit, the Lord,' and the refrain to the Katavasia of the 8th Ode: 'We praise, we bless, we worship the Lord, praising and magnifying Him unto all ages,' which is sung according to the tone of the Katavasia; also the Song of the Theotokos 'My soul magnifies' before the heirmos of the 9th Ode of the canon, which we take also in the time of the Forty Days, and outside of it, with the exception of Feasts of the Lord and of the Theotokos, on which, according to ancient typikons, it is not proper to take [it].*
 427: 
 428: *Before the Song of the Theotokos the Deacon, or instead of him the Priest, exclaims:*
 429: > **Deacon**: "The Theotokos and Mother of the Light let us magnify in songs."
 430: 
 431: *...which with us is used also on the aforementioned Great Feasts, when instead of 'My soul magnifies,' the heirmos of the ode is sung*[^34]*.* *The Typikon orders the Deacon or priest during the Song of the Theotokos to cense the Holy Table, iconostasis and the rest, as at the beginning.*
 432: 
 433: *After the 3rd, 6th and 9th Ode of the canon, immediately after the Katavasia, the Small Litany is taken (according to the model given at the first Kathisma of Matins), each with its own exclamation, and after the litany at the 3rd Ode the Sessional Hymn is sung, at the 6th - Kontakion and Ikos, and at the 9th - the Exapostilarion (Hymn of Light) is read. Both the Kontakion and Ikos are taken once each, the Sessional Hymn on Feasts of the Lord and of the Theotokos - twice, that is once - simply the Sessional Hymn, and the second time - with the refrain Glory, Both now. And the Exapostilarion on Feasts of the Lord and of the Theotokos is taken three times, that is twice - simply, and the third time - with the refrain Glory, Both now. On the Feast of a Polyeleos or non-Polyeleos Saint, which is celebrated, according to the Slavonic Typikon, on 6, the Sessional Hymn and His Exapostilarion are taken twice*[^35]*, then Both now: His Theotokion. If the Saint has two Sessional Hymns or Exapostilaria, then they are taken once each, that is the first - simply, the second - with the refrain Glory, then Both now: His Theotokion*[^36]*.* *When several services coincide, each with its own Sessional Hymn, Kontakion-Ikos and Exapostilarion, then they are taken one after another, according to the order of services; however, the Kontakion-Ikos of the first service is taken at the 6th Ode in its place, and the Kontakion-Ikos of the second, according to the Slavonic typikons*[^37]*, is transferred to the 3rd Ode and goes immediately before the Sessional Hymn. The sequence of Sessional Hymns and Exapostilaria in the middle of a Feast of the Lord and of the Theotokos ends with the Sessional Hymn or Exapostilarion of the Feast. After the Katavasia of the 9th Ode, according to the Slavonic Typikon, 'It is truly meet' is taken, if it is not Sunday. If it is Sunday, 'It is truly meet' is not taken, but then, between the Small Litany and the Exapostilarion (Exapostolarion) we sing, according to the tone of the Prokeimenon of the Liturgy, the troparion 'Holy is the Lord our God' (3)"*[^38]*.*

 194: Note: The Synod of Lviv permits on all days of Great Lent, except Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays, meat, on the condition of [reciting] 5 "Our Father" and 5 "Virgin Theotokos" for the laity, and Psalm 50 - for the clergy; on the other three days - dairy products.
 195: 
 196: GENERAL RUBRICS
 197: FOR THE FIVE FIRST LENTEN DAYS OF ALL WEEKS
 198: OF GREAT LENT
 199: AT THE Midnight Office
 200: On the first day of Great Lent we do not make prostrations at the Midnight Office, except three great ones at the prayer of St. Ephrem, and on other Lenten days we make 3 small prostrations: 1. At each of the three Trisagions. 2. At both "O come, let us worship". 3. At each Glory: "The Blameless"; also 16 usual ones at the prayer of St. Ephrem, that is 4 great and 12 small[^511].
 201: 
 202: AT MATINS
 203: Note: We begin prostrations from the Kathismata and make: 1. At "Alleluia" of each "Glory" of the Kathismata - 3 prostrations[^512]. 2. At "More honorable" of each of the 6 verses of the Song of the Theotokos - 1 prostration. 3. At "It is truly meet" - 1 prostration. 4. At "Glory to God in the highest" - 3 prostrations. 5. At the final Trisagion - 3 prostrations. 6. At the prayer of St. Ephrem - 16 prostrations, that is 12 small and 4 great.
 204: RUBRIC
 205: ##### 4.1.7.1 From the beginning to the end of the litany "In peace let us pray to the Lord", everything, just as on every day
 206: ##### 4.1.7.2 Instead of "God is the Lord" we sing Alleluia in the sequential tone of the Octoechos
 207: ##### 4.1.7.3 We sing three Trinity Hymns of the current tone, given in the Horologion, three for each tone. They are all sung three times with the refrain "Glory" to the second, and "Both now" - to the third. At each first one we make a commemoration of the weekday service, at the second - a commemoration of all saints, at the third - a commemoration of the Theotokos. However, since the weekday service of the week changes daily, and the troparia are sung the same each day of the week (except Saturdays and Sundays, on which, because they are not Lenten, the Trinity Hymns are not sung), at the end of each first Trinity Hymn a colon is given, which signifies that the troparion must be completed with the commemoration of the weekday service, the form of which is indicated at the end of the 3rd troparion of Tone 1
 208: Note
 209: These three commemorations we make also at the Exapostilaria following the canon. But the Lenten Exapostilarion has only one troparion in each tone, which is sung three times, therefore, when it is sung the first time, the commemoration of the weekday service is added to it, when - the second time, with the refrain "Glory", then - the commemoration of all saints, and when the third time, with the refrain "Both now", then - the commemoration of the Theotokos. These commemorations are added where the colon is given, that is before "And save me".
 210: ##### 4.1.7.4 Three Kathismata with their Sessional Hymns, the Sessional Hymns of which, sung after the 1st Kathisma, are of the Octoechos of the current tone, given also at the end of the Triodion. The Sessional Hymns sung after the 2nd and 3rd Kathismata are of the Triodion
 211: ##### 4.1.7.5 Psalm 50 and the first petition of the Great Litany "Save, O God", and after the exclamation "Through the mercy and compassion" immediately - the Canon
 212: ##### 4.1.7.6 Odes and Canons. The Biblical Odes, given at the end of the Psalter, are intertwined with the odes of the canon, as given: before the ode of the canon the corresponding ode of the Psalter is recited, leaving its last verses for refrains to the troparia of the canon, in such quantity as there will be troparia in the ode of the canon, including the heirmos, except two, for to the penultimate troparion we refrain "Glory", and to the last - "Both now". The 2nd Ode is recited in full before the ode of the canon, and to the troparia of its canon we refrain: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee". According to our ancient custom, the Odes of the Psalter are recited only in those odes in which the triodion occurs, and in the other odes we refrain the usual refrains to the troparia of the canon. The Greek Typikon prescribes singing the Odes of the Psalter in the tone of the Menaion canon, but now we do not even know what their melody was
 213: The Canons will be only of the Menaion and Triodion, for the Octoechos, according to the Greek rubric, during Great Lent is not sung, with the exception of Sundays. In some odes there will be 3 canons on 14, that is of the Saint of the Menaion with heirmos on 6 and both canons of the Triodion on 8: one on 4 and the second on 4. In some odes there will be only one canon of the saint on 4, and in the second ode there will be only two canons of the Triodion on 8, with heirmos on 9. This difference regarding the number of canons and their troparia in the odes arises because the Triodion canons do not occur daily in all odes, but in general only in three odes in the following sequence:
 214: On Monday: 1st, 8th and 9th.
 215: On Tuesday: 2nd, 8th and 9th.
 216: On Wednesday: 3rd, 8th and 9th.
 217: On Thursday: 4th, 8th and 9th.
 218: On Friday: 5th, 8th and 9th.
 219: On Saturday: 6th, 7th, 8th and 9th.
 220: Therefore, there will be:
 221: On Monday: at Odes 1, 8, and 9 - 3 canons on 14, that is of the Menaion with heirmos on 6 and both canons of the triodion on 8, and afterwards - one more separate troparion of the Triodion with the refrain "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee", and the Katavasia - Heirmos of the 2nd canon of the triodion. At other odes there will be only one canon of the saint on 4, with heirmos on 5; only at Odes 3 and 6 the canon of the saint is read without the heirmos, for it is taken afterwards, as Katavasia[^513].
 222: On Tuesday: at the 2nd Ode, since the saint does not have this ode, there will be only two canons of the triodion on 8, and afterwards - one more separate troparion and Katavasia - Heirmos of the 2nd canon of the triodion; at the 8th and 9th Odes - 3 canons on 14 exactly as on Monday. At other odes there will be only the canon of the Menaion on 4 exactly as on Monday.
 223: On Wednesday: at the 3rd, 8th, and 9th Odes there will be 3 canons on 14 exactly as at the 1st, 8th, and 9th Odes on Monday. And at other odes there will be only one canon of the saint on 4, as on Monday.
 224: On Thursday: at the 4th, 8th, and 9th Odes there will be 3 canons on 14, as on Monday. At other odes - only the canon of the saint on 4 and the rest, as on Monday.
 225: On Friday: at the 5th, 8th, and 9th Odes there will be 3 canons on 14, as on Monday; and at other odes - only one of the saint on 4.
 226: On Saturday: at the 6th, 7th, 8th, and 9th Odes there will be 3 canons: one of the saint and two of the Triodion, at other odes there will be two canons: of the temple and of the saint; however, for Saturday a separate rubric will be given, since Saturday is not a Lenten day.
 227: •	If two saints fall, then we read both their canons together on 6[^514], that is of the first saint with heirmos on 3 and of the second without heirmos on 3. So also to the saint on 6.
 228: The Katavasia will be always the heirmos of the last canon either of the triodion, or of the Menaion: of the triodion where there will be a triodion, and where there will be only the Menaion, then the Katavasia of the Menaion will be only after Odes 3 and 6, for at the 8th and 9th there will always be a triodion and therefore there will always be the Katavasia of the triodion.
 229: A more precise example of the combination of the Odes of the Psalter with the Odes of the Canon is given at the 1st Ode in the Moscow Typikon, and is presented as follows: "After this we begin: 'Let us sing to the Lord' in the tone of the canon of the Menaion of the saint of the day and the verses of the odes are recited hurriedly, each Choir - its verse, until they reach 'The waters became thick' and from this they begin verses on 14, and we sing the Menaion with heirmos on 6. And we sing thus: the first Choir reads the verse 'The waters became thick' and sings the heirmos. The second Choir reads the second verse 'The enemy said' and, after it, - the troparion of the canon, and in sequence verses by choirs up to 'Then hastened'. From the verse 'Then hastened' we begin the triodion of Kyr Joseph on 4. And at 'The Lord reigning' we sing the 2nd triodion of Kyr Theodore the Studite, and one choir sings the troparion, and the second choir - the 2nd verse and the troparion. After this both choirs, having united, sing: Glory: Trinity Hymn, in a higher voice, Both now: Theotokion. Then we sing in the highest voice: 'Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee', and we sing the other troparion of Theodore, because the ode has 5 troparia. At the end we sing the Katavasia - heirmos of the second canon"[^515].
 230: Regarding the refrains to the troparia of the canon, know that in order to find the number of refrains as quickly as possible, the last four, six, and eight verses of the Biblical Odes (except the 2nd, for it is read in full before the heirmos) from the bottom up are marked in the middle of the song, or on the side, with the inscription: "on 4, on 6, on 8". But on 14 they are not counted off, since 6 verses from 8 upwards are easily counted. However, the counting of 14 verses in current Psalters does not coincide exactly with the counting in previous Psalters, for where the rubrics place the 14th verse at "The waters became thick", current Psalters place the 14th verse at "The enemy said", and "The waters became thick" moves to the 15th verse. The 6th Ode has only 12 verses, so do not forget to divide these two verses of it on 4. The 9th Ode, one, of the Theotokos, is sung whole before the heirmos with "More honorable", and the other, of Zachariah, is sung whole in the refrains, and in those editions where there are only 13 verses, one verse must be divided into 2.
 231: The last edition of the Lviv Psalter does not give the counting of the last verses, except for the 9th Ode; and, in general, in recent editions they did not care about the counting of verses.
 232: After the 3rd Ode - Sessional Hymn of the Saint[^548], after the 6th - Kontakion and Ikos of the Saint; if the saint does not have this, then the Martyric Sessional Hymn of the Octoechos of the current tone, given also at the end of the Triodion. After the 9th Ode - "It is truly meet" and after the litany - Exapostilarion of the tone, which is in the Horologion, three times, with refrains and commemorations, as the Trinity Hymns, here on page 338, in the note.
 233: ##### 4.1.7.7 Before the Small Doxology the Priest exclaims: "To Thee belongs glory" and the rest, and at "Glory to God in the highest" we make three prostrations
 234: ##### 4.1.7.8 Aposticha of the Triodion, Glory: of the saint, if there be, Both now: Usual Theotokion in the tone of "Glory"

 237: #### 4.1.7.1 AT THE HOURS
 238: ##### 4.1.7.1.1 We make 3 small prostrations: at "O come, let us worship", at each Trisagion, at "Alleluia", which is after the three psalms, and at "Alleluia" after each antiphon; at each of the three singings of the troparion with two verses we bend the knees[^517] and, after the Theotokion, - 3 prostrations, and at the prayer of St. Ephrem - 16 usual ones

 247: ##### 4.1.7.1.8 In the archcathedral temple the Hours 3rd, 6th, 9th, Typika and Vespers are celebrated together, beginning at 11 o'clock in the morning, and in the afternoon, at the usual time of Vespers, - Great Compline[^518]
 248: ##### 4.1.7.1.9 The last prayer of the 9th Hour "O Master Lord Jesus Christ" is transferred to the Typika, to the place of the prayer "O All-holy Trinity", and the prayer "O All-holy Trinity" with the psalm following it is transferred, according to the rubric of our Pochaiv Triodion, to the end of Vespers[^519]. And on Wednesday and Friday, since Vespers will be with the Presanctified, "O All-holy Trinity" cannot be transferred to the end of Vespers, for it ends with the Liturgy and therefore remains in its place at the Typika, exactly so the prayer "O Master Lord Jesus Christ" remains in its place at the 9th Hour

 250: AT THE TYPIKA (Typika)
 251: Note: The first part of the Typika, from the beginning to the Beatitudes, falls out in Great Lent, and the last, from "O All-holy Trinity", is transferred to the end of Vespers. In the middle part the stichera on the Beatitudes and the Epistle and Gospel fall out.

 255: And a great prostration[^520].

 271: Note on Prostrations
 272: We make three small prostrations: at "O come, let us worship", at "Alleluia" after the pre-introductory psalm and after each of the three antiphons of the Kathisma (although now we read only the beginning of the Kathisma); after "Vouchsafe, O Lord", at the Trisagions; at the prayer of St. Ephrem - 16 usual ones and one prostration after "It is truly meet"[^522].

 276: 3.	18th Kathisma with 3 prostrations at Alleluia after each of its antiphons (today we read only the beginning of the Kathisma).
 277: ##### 4.1.7.1.16 On "Lord, I have cried" - 6 stichera: 3 of the Triodion and 3 of the Menaion, Glory, Both now: Theotokion of the Menaion. If there is a Doxastikon of the saint, then Theotokion - usual, in the tone of the Doxastikon
 278: - If two saints fall, we sing to one in the evening stichera on 3, and to the 2nd in the morning at the Praises - stichera on 4[^523].
 279: - If a saint on 6 falls, we sing to him stichera on 3, just as to a saint on 4; thus we sing also in the middle of a feast, e. g. December 20 and September 15.
 280: ##### 4.1.7.1.17 Prokeimenon of the Triodion and one reading of the Triodion, and afterwards also another Prokeimenon and second reading of the Triodion
 281: ##### 4.1.7.1.18 After the 2nd reading immediately - "Vouchsafe" and 3 prostrations
 282: ##### 4.1.7.1.19 Aposticha of the Triodion with the usual verses of the Horologion. If there is a Doxastikon of the saint, then we select the Theotokion in His tone, as on "Lord, I have cried"; if not, then Glory, Both now: Triodion
 283: ##### 4.1.7.1.20 After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart", at the Trisagion, - 3 prostrations; and after "Our Father" - troparia "Virgin Theotokos" and the two others with a prostration at the end of each, then "Beneath Thy tender mercy" without a prostration
 284: 9.	"Lord, have mercy" (40) and the rest, as in the Horologion, with the prayer of St. Ephrem and 16 usual prostrations.
 285: ##### 4.1.7.1.21 Trisagion with prostrations and, after "Our Father", - "Lord, have mercy" (12)
 286: 11.	"O All-holy Trinity" and "Blessed be the name of the Lord" (3) with prostrations.
 287: ##### 4.1.7.1.22 Glory, Both now: Psalm "I will bless the Lord"
 288: 13.	"It is truly meet" and a prostration; Glory, Both now: "Lord, have mercy" (2), "Lord, bless".
 289: ##### 4.1.7.1.23 Dismissal "O Christ our true God" with the commemoration of the service of the day and the saint
 290: 
 291: AT Great Compline
 292: ##### 4.1.7.1.24 At the usual time of Vespers we sing Great Compline with prostrations, as we mentioned for Tuesday and Thursday evening of Cheesefare week, here on page 327
 293: ##### 4.1.7.1.25 On Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday of the first week of Great Lent, after "O come, let us worship", we recite Psalm 69 "O God, come to my assistance", given in the order of Great Compline after the 3rd "O come, let us worship", after the prayer "O Master God the Father"; then one fourth part of each ode of the Great Canon (Matins on Thursday before the 5th Sunday of Lent)[^524]. Refrain to the troparia of the canon - "Have mercy on me, O God, have mercy on me"[^525], to the troparion of St. Mary of Egypt - "Venerable Mother Mary, pray to God for us", and to the troparion of St. Andrew - "Venerable Father Andrew, pray to God for us". According to the rubric, 3 small prostrations should be made at each troparion of the canon, however, among us this is not done, since there are no people in church at that time
 294: The rubric for Great Compline we have partly here on page 327, and partly - in the Horologion.
 295: 
 296: ### 4.1.8 Vespers on Wednesday and Friday with Presanctified
 297: Note on Prostrations
 298: On Wednesday we make 3 small prostrations: at the Trisagion at the beginning, at "O come, let us worship", at "Alleluia" after the pre-introductory psalm and after each antiphon of the Kathisma and at "Let my prayer be set forth". Great prostrations, according to local custom, we make at "Light of Christ", when the Priest blesses the people crosswise with the triple-candle; at the conclusion of the singing "Let my prayer be set forth" and after "Now the Powers of Heaven", when the consecrated Lamb is taken from the artophorion and placed on the diskos[^526]. And on Fridays at Vespers and at Compline we do not make prostrations, only the prescribed ones at the Presanctified, that is: after "Let my prayer be set forth" - 3 prostrations[^527], after the Entrance of the Holy Gifts - 3 prostrations and at "Let my prayer be set forth" - 3 prostrations, and among us also at "Light of Christ" - 3 prostrations.
 299: RUBRIC
 300: ##### 4.1.8.1 After "Blessed is the Kingdom" we recite "O Heavenly King", Trisagion (with prostrations) and, after "Our Father", - "Lord, have mercy" (12), Glory, Both now: "O come, let us worship" three times (with prostrations)
 301: ##### 4.1.8.2 Of the eight prayers recited at the prefatory psalm, the Priest recites here only the last 5, for the first three he has to read afterwards, one at each of the three antiphons of the Kathisma
 302: 3.	18th Kathisma, with a prayer at each of its three antiphons and with a Small Litany after each antiphon.
 303: ##### 4.1.8.3 On "Lord, I have cried" - 10 stichera: Triodion on 6 and Menaion on 4, Glory, Both now: Theotokion of the Menaion. If there is a Doxastikon of the saint, then we select the Theotokion in His tone. (On Friday evening stichera: Idiomelon of the Triodion twice, Martyria of the Octoechos of the current tone - 4[^528] and of the Saint - 4, Glory: of the saint, if there is one, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the departing tone; if not, then Glory, Both now: the same Theotokion)
 304: ##### 4.1.8.4 Entrance with the Censer (on the Finding of the Precious Head of the Forerunner, on the 40 Martyrs and on Great Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday[^566] entrance - with the Gospel)
 305: ##### 4.1.8.5 At "O Gladsome Light" - Prokeimenon of the Triodion, one reading of the Triodion and the second Prokeimenon of the Triodion[^529]; then the Priest, having taken the triple-candle with the censer and exclaiming "Wisdom, Aright", begins "The Light of Christ", blessing with the triple-candle crosswise to the east, then, blessing to the west, says: "Illumines all"[^530]; all make three prostrations to the ground, and the Reader sings: "The Reading from Proverbs" and, when the Priest or Deacon exclaims: "Let us attend", reads the second reading of the Triodion
 306: 7.	"Let my prayer be set forth". Has after it three verses and is sung six times, that is: twice - before the first verse, once - after each verse and again once at the end. And among us the first time "Let my prayer be set forth" is sung by the Priest, the second time - by the Choir, all three verses - by the Priest, after each the Choir - "Let my prayer be set forth", the last time in a higher voice up to the half - the Priest, and from the half - the Choir. Where there are two choirs, they sing "Let my prayer be set forth" alternately: the first begins after the Priest, and the second half is sung by both choirs together. When the Priest sings, he himself stands, and the Choir and people kneel; when the Choir sings, the Choir stands together with the people, and the Priest kneels. If there are two choirs, the one singing stands, and the other kneels; people who are on the side of the right choir kneel, stand and sing with the right choir, and those on the left - with the left[^531].
 307: The Priest sings "Let my prayer be set forth" first in front of the altar, then the 1st verse - on the south, the 2nd - on the west, the 3rd - on the north side, and at the end the first half - again in front of the holy table[^532]. He censes each side of the altar twice, that is before the beginning of his singing and at the end of the Choir's singing, that is at "The lifting up of my hands", for then, having censed, he moves to the next side of the altar, in order to cense there also, so that the Choir is ready to sing its verse[^533].
 308: ##### 4.1.8.6 Immediately after the end of the singing of "Let my prayer be set forth" is exclaimed "Let us all say" and according to the order - Liturgy of the Presanctified
 309: Notes
 310: ##### 4.1.8.7 If there is no Liturgy of the Presanctified, then we sing Vespers according to the rubric of Monday, Tuesday and Thursday evening, that is from the 10 stichera on "Lord, I have cried" we transfer the first 3 to the Aposticha, and the other 6 we sing on "Lord, I have cried"[^534]; and there will be on Wednesday stichera of the Triodion - 3 and of the Menaion - 3, and on Friday Martyria of the Octoechos - 3 and of the Menaion - 3. On Friday evening, after "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart", there will be no Lenten troparia with prostrations, but the Troparion of the Saint, Glory, Both now: Theotokion from the Sunday ones, in the tone of the Troparion of the Saint[^651] and, after the litany "Have mercy on us, O God", - 3 great prostrations[^535] and the Great Dismissal, as usual
 311: ##### 4.1.8.8 If on this day falls a saint with Polyeleos, namely the Finding of the Precious Head of the Forerunner and the 40 Martyrs, and also on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday of Passion Week[^536], then immediately after "Let my prayer be set forth" there will be censing and on the two previously named feasts their Epistle and Gospel are read, the Gospel - beginning from "Wisdom, Aright". On the three days of Passion Week only the Gospel is read, beginning from "And that we may be accounted worthy", since there is no Epistle
 312: ##### 4.1.8.9 By the decision of the Synod of Lviv, the pastor must celebrate the Liturgy of the Presanctified on every Wednesday and every Friday of Great Lent and on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday of Passion Week
 313: Note on the number of prostrations per day. The number of prostrations made in church reached once 300 per day, excluding the Midnight Office: "Three hundred during the day and night, without the Midnight Office". (Greek Triodion, our Manuscript Typikon and Tserkovne Oko on the 1st Monday of Lent).
 314: 
 315: ### 4.1.9 First Saturday of Great Lent
 316: Memory of the Holy Great Martyr Theodore the Tyro[^537]
 317: On Friday evening
 318: AT VESPERS WITH PRESANCTIFIED: Everything according to the general rubric, here on page 349.
 319: #### 4.1.9.1 AT COMPLINE
 320: Note
 321: Compline on all Fridays of Great Lent, according to the Greek rubric, is Small, and according to the Pochaiv Triodion, Tserkovne Oko and the Moscow Typikon - Great. However, in our times, when abbreviations prevail, we should adhere to the Greek rubric, the more so because even in our Horologia, in the order of Great Compline, troparia are given only for 4 days of the week, that is for Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday. We do not make prostrations, as was already said on page 349.
 322: RUBRIC
 323: ##### 4.1.9.1.1 If it be Small Compline, then after "It is truly meet" we recite the Kontakion of the Great Martyr; if Great, then after the 1st Trisagion - Troparion of the Great Martyr, Glory, Both now: Theotokion (Sunday, in the tone of the Troparion of the Saint)[^538]; after the 2nd Trisagion - usual troparia "Have mercy on us, O Lord"; after "It is truly meet" - Kontakion of the Great Martyr, and the Troparion "O Lord of Hosts" we do not recite[^539]
 324: ##### 4.1.9.1.2 At Compline we sing the Canon for the Dead, which is in the Octoechos for the current tone, and the Canons of the Menaion to the saints of the nearest Saturday and Sunday we sing, if the Ecclesiarch prefers, one - at Compline on Friday with the Canon for the Dead, and the other - on Sunday at Compline[^540]. The Greek Triodion adds: "we do so on all Friday evenings of holy and Great Lent". Before the Canon for the Dead we should sing also the usual Theotokion Canon of the Octoechos, for the rubric does not exclude it[^541]
 325: AT MATINS
 326: ##### 4.1.9.1.3 From the beginning to the canon everything - according to the general rubric for a saint without Polyeleos on Saturday, except the 2nd Sessional Hymn, which will not be of the Octoechos, but of the Triodion of St. Theodore
 327: ##### 4.1.9.1.4 Canons 3 [making] 14: Temple with heirmos on 6 and two of Theodore on 8. Katavasia after each ode - "I shall open"
 328: After the 3rd Ode - Sessional Hymn of the Saint, after the 6th - Kontakion and Ikos of the Saint, after the 9th - Exapostilarion of the Saint.
 329: ##### 4.1.9.1.5 Stichera of the Praises to the Saint on 4, Doxastikon - to him, and Theotokion - in the Triodion
 330: ##### 4.1.9.1.6 Small Doxology and, after "Let us complete", - Aposticha of the Saint with his two verses and the subsequent order of Matins according to the rubric for a saint without Polyeleos on Saturday
 331: AT THE HOURS: At all: Troparion and Kontakion to the Saint.
 332: AT THE LITURGY: Everything - to the Saint, and the Epistle and Gospel first - of the day, and then - of the Saint.
 333: 
 334: ### 4.1.10 First Sunday of Great Lent
 335: Of Orthodoxy
 336: [^542]Notes
 337: ##### 4.1.10.1 The Triodion service of this Sunday has neither an All-Night Vigil nor a Polyeleos[^543], but is combined with the Sunday service of the Octoechos
 338: ##### 4.1.10.2 The service of a saint without Polyeleos we sing at Compline or on another day
 339: #### 4.1.10.1 AT Great Vespers
 340: 1.	"Blessed is the man", as usual.
 341: ##### 4.1.10.1.1 On "Lord, I have cried" - 10 stichera: Sunday of the Octoechos - 6 and of the Triodion - 4, Glory: Triodion, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the tone (Dogmatikon)
 342: ##### 4.1.10.1.2 Sunday Aposticha, Glory: Triodion, Both now: Triodion
 343: ##### 4.1.10.1.3 At the end: Sunday Troparion, Glory: "We venerate Thy most pure image", Tone 2; Both now: Sunday Theotokion in the same Tone 2
 344: AT COMPLINE: After "It is truly meet" - Kontakion of the Triodion only.
 345: #### 4.1.10.2 AT Great Matins
 346: ##### 4.1.10.2.1 On "God is the Lord": Sunday Troparion twice, Glory: "We venerate Thy most pure image", Both now: Sunday Theotokion in the same Tone 2
 347: ##### 4.1.10.2.2 Everything else up to the canon - Sunday, as usual, only "Glory" will be "Open to me the doors", Both now: "Lead me on the paths of salvation" and at "Have mercy on me, O God": "Thinking upon the multitude"
 348: ##### 4.1.10.2.3 Canons 3 [making] 14: Octoechos Sunday on 4, Cross-Resurrection on 2, Theotokos on 2 and Triodion on 6[^544]. Katavasia of the Triodion
 349: After the 3rd Ode - Sessional Hymn of the Triodion; after the 6th - Kontakion and Ikos of the Triodion; after the 9th - Sunday Exapostilarion, Glory: Triodion, Both now: Triodion.
 350: Stichera of the Praises - 9: 5 of the Octoechos and 4 of the Triodion, the three last - of the Triodion, Both now: "Most blessed Art Thou".
 351: ##### 4.1.10.2.4 After the Doxology - Sunday Troparion, one of the two usual ones
 352: ##### 4.1.10.2.5 After the dismissal - Glory, Both now: Gospel Sticheron
 353: AT THE HOURS: At all - Sunday Troparion, Glory: "We venerate Thy most pure image", Kontakion of the Triodion.
 354: #### 4.1.10.3 AT THE LITURGY
 355: ##### 4.1.10.3.1 Troparion Sunday and "We venerate Thy most pure image", Glory, Both now: Kontakion of the Triodion
 356: ##### 4.1.10.3.2 Everything else - of Orthodoxy, only Communion Hymn - "Praise the Lord" and "Rejoice in the Lord"
 357: 
 358: MONDAY, TUESDAY, WEDNESDAY, THURSDAY AND FRIDAY
 359: ### 4.1.11 Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday of the Second Week of Great Lent
 360: Everything - according to the rubric for Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday of the 1st week of Great Lent, here on page 347 and following.
 361: Note
 362: Let it be known that from this Monday of the 2nd week of Lent the canons of the saints in the Menaion, which fall from the Saturday of Lazarus to the Sunday of Ap. Thomas, are sung at Compline with the Theotokion Canons. First the Canon of the Theotokos is sung, and after it - the Canon of the Menaion. After the 3rd Ode - Kontakion and Sessional Hymn of the Menaion, and after the 6th - Sessional Hymn of the Theotokos; after the canon - Stichera of the Menaion (Triodion of this day).
 363: 
 364: ### 4.1.12 Saturday of the Second Week of Great Lent
 365: Note
 366: The service of this Saturday, as also the services of the 3rd and 4th Saturdays of Great Lent, differ from the services of Meatfare Saturday and the Saturday before the Sunday of Pentecost in that it does not exclude fully either the service of the Menaion, or the service of the day of the Octoechos, that is to all saints and the dead. The services of Meatfare Saturday and the Saturday before the Sunday of Pentecost exclude generally the service of the Menaion, and from the service of the Octoechos little is taken, but have their own order in the Triodion exclusively for the dead. Therefore, we suppose that the two litanies for the dead: "In peace let us pray to the Lord" and "Have mercy on us, O God", which according to our later rubric are given at Vespers and at Matins, and the litany for the dead "Again and again", which is said between the odes of the canon, should be taken only on these two Saturdays which are exclusively for the dead, and on the other three - usual litanies.
 367: RUBRIC
 368: AT VESPERS WITH PRESANCTIFIED
 369: 1.	18th Kathisma.
 370: ##### 4.1.12.1 On "Lord, I have cried" - 10 stichera: Idiomelon of the Triodion of the day twice, 4 Martyria of the Octoechos and 4 of the Menaion of the saint, Glory: of the saint, if there be, but if not, then Glory: Sticheron for the Dead of the tone, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the departing tone
 371: ##### 4.1.12.2 Instead of the Prokeimenon of the day of the Horologion there will be Prokeimenon of the Triodion and reading, second Prokeimenon and second reading of the Triodion, then "Let my prayer be set forth" and the rest of the Presanctified
 372: Notes
 373: ##### 4.1.12.3 After the end of the Presanctified, in other services of this day (except the Panakhida for the dead) vestments of red color should rather be used, than black, for red ones are - predominantly for martyrs
 374: ##### 4.1.12.4 If there be no Presanctified, then we sing Vespers according to the rubric given here, on page 347
 375: AT COMPLINE: Compline, according to the Greek rubric, we sing Small. After "It is truly meet" - Kontakion of the Triodion "With the saints give rest"[^546].
 376: Midnight Office - Saturday.
 377: AT MATINS
 378: ##### 4.1.12.5 Instead of "God is the Lord" we sing Alleluia in Tone 2 with verses
 379: ##### 4.1.12.6 Troparion of the day "Apostles, prophets" twice; Glory: "Remember, O Lord", Both now: Theotokion "Holy Mother"
 380: ##### 4.1.12.7 After the 1st Kathisma - Small Litany and Sessional Hymn of the Octoechos of the current tone
 381: 4.	17th Kathisma ("The Blameless"), in two stations, with refrains and troparia "The Choir of the saints"; after each station - litany for the dead, then we sing the Sessional Hymn "Give rest" with its Theotokion and Psalm 50.
 382: ##### 4.1.12.8 Canons 3 [making] 14: of the Temple of the Lord or Theotokos with heirmos on 6, of the Saint of the Menaion on 4 and of the Octoechos of the current tone the second[^547] on 4. If the Temple is of a Saint, then - Canon of the Saint with heirmos on 6, Temple on 4 and Octoechos on 4. From the 6th Ode, leaving the Canons of the Temple and Octoechos, we sing the Canon of the Saint of the Menaion on 6 and both canons of the tetraodion on 8. Refrain to the troparia of the tetraodion - "Holy Martyrs, pray to God for us". At the end of the eight troparia of each ode of the tetraodion we add two more troparia: one Martyric with the Martyric refrain, and the second - for the dead with the refrain for the dead. From the two Martyric refrains "Wondrous is God" and "To the saints that are in His earth" and from the two refrains for the dead "Their souls" and "Blessed are they Whom Thou Hast chosen", the first we refrain to the Martyric and for the dead of the 6th and 8th Odes, and the second - to the Martyric and for the dead of the 7th and 9th Odes. Katavasia after Odes 3, 6, 7, 8, and 9 - Heirmos of the last canon: after the 3rd - of the Octoechos, after the others - of the Triodion
 383: After the 3rd Ode - Sessional Hymn of the Saint, after the 6th - Kontakion and Ikos for the Dead, after the 9th - Exapostilarion of the Octoechos (to all saints, Glory: to the dead).
 384: ##### 4.1.12.9 Stichera of the Praises, Martyria of the Octoechos - 4, Glory: for the Dead, Both now: Theotokion of the "Glory"
 385: ##### 4.1.12.10 After the Small Doxology at the Aposticha - Stichera for the Dead of the Octoechos with their verses for the dead
 386: ##### 4.1.12.11 At the end: Troparion to all saints ("Apostles, prophets"), Glory: for the dead "Remember, O Lord", Both now: "Holy Mother"
 387: AT THE HOURS: At all - Troparion of the day ("Apostles, prophets"), Glory: "Remember, O Lord", Kontakion "With the saints give rest".
 388: #### 4.1.12.1 AT THE LITURGY
 389: ##### 4.1.12.1.1 Troparia: "Apostles, prophets" and "Remember, O Lord"; Glory: Kontakion "With the saints give rest", Both now: "Thee as a wall and haven"
 390: ##### 4.1.12.1.2 Everything else - of the day and of the dead
 391: ### 4.1.13 Second Sunday of Great Lent
 392: Everything - according to the general rubric for a saint without Polyeleos on Sunday, here on pp. 47-54 [→REF:p47-54], only:
 393: AT Great Vespers: On "Lord, I have cried" there will be 6 Sunday stichera of the Octoechos and 4 to the saint of the Menaion.
 394: AT COMPLINE: After "It is truly meet" - Kontakion of the Triodion.
 395: #### 4.1.13.1 AT Great Matins
 396: ##### 4.1.13.1.1 Before the Canon we sing "Open to me the doors" and the rest, as on the first Sunday of Lent
 397: ##### 4.1.13.1.2 Canons: Sunday of the current tone with heirmos on 6, Triodion on 4 and Saint of the Menaion on 4
 398: After the 3rd Ode - Kontakion and Ikos of the Sunday and to the Saint, if he has one; Glory: his Sessional Hymn, Both now: his Theotokion; after the 6th - Kontakion and Ikos of the Triodion.
 399: ##### 4.1.13.1.3 Stichera of the Praises - 9: Sunday of the Octoechos on 8, with the usual verses of the Praises psalms, one of the Triodion with the verse "Arise, O Lord my God", then Glory: and again the same sticheron; Both now: "Most blessed Art Thou"
 400: ##### 4.1.13.1.4 At the end of Matins - Glory, Both now: Gospel Sticheron
 401: AT THE HOURS: Instead of the Sunday Kontakion we read the Kontakion of the Triodion, the rest - according to the general rubric.
 402: #### 4.1.13.2 AT THE LITURGY
 403: ##### 4.1.13.2.1 Instead of the Sunday Kontakion we sing the Kontakion of the Triodion
 404: ##### 4.1.13.2.2 Sunday Prokeimenon of the current tone and the rest - according to the general rubric
 405: 
 406: ### 4.1.14 Third Week of Great Lent
 407: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday
 408: Everything - according to the general Lenten rubric given for the first week of Great Lent, here from p. 347.
 409: Third Saturday of Great Lent
 410: Everything - according to the rubric of the second Saturday of Great Lent, here on page 357.
 411: THIRD SUNDAY OF GREAT LENT - VENERATION OF THE CROSS
 412: Notes
 413: ##### 4.1.14.1 The service of a saint without Polyeleos we sing at Compline
 414: ##### 4.1.14.2 The entire divine service, according to the Synod of Lviv, should be celebrated in violet vestments (according to the previous - in purple)
 415: #### 4.1.14.1 AT Great Vespers
 416: 1.	"Blessed is the man", as usual.
 417: ##### 4.1.14.1.1 On "Lord, I have cried" - 10 stichera: 6 Sunday of the Octoechos and 4 of the Triodion; Glory: Triodion, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the tone
 418: ##### 4.1.14.1.2 Sunday Aposticha; Glory, Both now: Triodion
 419: ##### 4.1.14.1.3 At the end: Sunday Troparion, Glory: of the Cross, Both now: Theotokion from the Sunday ones, in the tone of the Cross
 420: ##### 4.1.14.1.4 Dismissal: "Christ our true God, Who rose from the dead, through the prayers of His most pure Mother, by the power of the precious and life-giving Cross, which we venerate today, through the intercessions of the holy, glorious and all-laudable apostles, of our venerable and God-bearing fathers and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for He is good and loves mankind"
 421: BRINGING OUT OF THE PRECIOUS CROSS FROM
 422: THE SACRISTY TO THE ALTAR
 423: The bringing out of the Precious Cross from the sacristy to the altar takes place after the dismissal of Vespers, according to the rubric given for September 14, here on pp. 121-122 [→REF:p121-122].
 424: AT COMPLINE: After "It is truly meet" - Kontakion to the Cross "No longer does the flaming sword guard".
 425: #### 4.1.14.2 AT Great Matins
 426: ##### 4.1.14.2.1 On "God is the Lord": Sunday Troparion twice, Glory: to the Cross, Both now: Theotokion from the Sunday ones in the tone of the Cross
 427: ##### 4.1.14.2.2 Everything else up to the canon - Sunday, as usual, only after the 50th Psalm we sing "Open to me the doors" and the rest
 428: ##### 4.1.14.2.3 Canons 3 [making] 14: Octoechos Sunday with heirmos on 4, Theotokos on 2 and Triodion on 8. Katavasia of the Triodion
 429: After the 3rd Ode - Sessional Hymn of the Cross; after the 6th - Kontakion and Ikos of the Cross; after the 9th - Sunday Exapostilarion, Glory: of the Cross, Both now: Theotokion of the Cross.
 430: ##### 4.1.14.2.4 Stichera of the Praises - 9: 4 Sunday of the Octoechos and 5 of the Triodion, of which the three last - with the verses of the Cross; Glory: once more the last sticheron of the Triodion, Both now: "Most blessed Art Thou"
 431: ##### 4.1.14.2.5 During the Great Doxology the bringing out of the Precious Cross from the altar to the tetrapod takes place, according to the rubric given here on pp. 122-123 [→REF:p122-123]; then veneration, immediately after the singing of the troparion "Save, O Lord", for then the Priest begins to sing the troparion "Before Thy Cross" (3) and there will be veneration in such a way as given here on pp. 124-127 [→REF:p124-127]
 432: ##### 4.1.14.2.6 After the dismissal - Glory, Both now: Gospel Sticheron
 433: AT THE HOURS: At all - Sunday Troparion, Glory: of the Cross. Kontakion - only of the Cross.
 434: #### 4.1.14.3 AT THE LITURGY
 435: ##### 4.1.14.3.1 Troparion Sunday and of the Cross; Glory, Both now: Kontakion of the Cross
 436: ##### 4.1.14.3.2 Instead of the Trisagion we sing "Before Thy Cross"
 437: ##### 4.1.14.3.3 Everything else - only of the Cross
 438: Note on the Veneration of the Precious Cross
 439: After the dismissal of the Liturgy, and also after the end of every service celebrated in church, from this day until the end of the 6th Hour of the following Friday, veneration of the Precious Cross takes place: the Priest, having come before the tetrapod, sings together with the people "Before Thy Cross we bow down" (3). If there be a sufficient number of people, the Choir sings the stichera of veneration until all have venerated, according to the rubric given on page 127, in the note[^549].
 440: 
 441: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday
 442: of the fourth week of Great Lent
 443: Everything - according to the general Lenten rubric of the previous weeks, except the veneration of the Precious Cross, according to the previously stated. Only Wednesday and Friday differ from the other three days in that at Matins, instead of the Canon of the Menaion, they have the Cross Canon of the Triodion. Also at Vespers on Tuesday for Wednesday all 6 stichera on "Lord, I have cried" will be of the Cross; and the Canon of the Menaion on these two days we take at Compline.
 444: ### 4.1.15 Fourth Saturday of Great Lent
 445: Everything - according to the rubric of the second Saturday of Great Lent, here on page 357.
 446: ### 4.1.16 Fourth Sunday of Great Lent
 447: Everything - according to the rubric of the second Sunday of Great Lent, here on page 360.
 448: Note
 449: The service of St. John of the Ladder, which some later [typika] prescribed to sing on this Sunday, is usually not taken among us. And if someone, namely in monasteries, wishes to sing it, let him sing it instead of the service of the regular saint of the Menaion, according to the rubric for a saint without Polyeleos on 4, and let him take the service of the regular saint at Compline. According to this Typikon, the service of St. Mary of Egypt is sung on the fifth[^550] Sunday of Lent, but if someone wishes, he may sing it instead of the service of the regular saint.
 450: 
 451: ### 4.1.17 Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday of the Fifth Week of Great Lent
 452: Everything - according to the general Lenten rubric of past weeks.
 453: Thursday of the fifth week of Great Lent
 454: on which we sing the Great Canon
 455: The service of the regular saint is transferred to another day.
 456: ON WEDNESDAY EVENING
 457: AT VESPERS WITH PRESANCTIFIED
 458: Everything - according to the Lenten rubric, as usual, except the stichera on "Lord, I have cried", which are taken 28 on 29, for the first Idiomelon is repeated, also one more at "Glory" and one at "Both now".
 459: Refrains to the first 20 stichera we take from "Lord, I have cried", beginning from "Fall into their own nets"; to the 21st and 22nd stichera we refrain two usual verses from the Aposticha of Vespers; and to the other seven - "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee".
 460: Notes
 461: ##### 4.1.17.1 The stichera, not only the two first, but also all others, we sing in the tone of the Idiomela, for of the three types of Prosomoia given in the Triodion at the other stichera, two in our Heirmologia we do not find; and the one which is given at the stichera of St. Andrew of Crete, although it is given also in the Heirmologia, nevertheless, today we do not use. The stichera of St. Andrew of Crete, in the Greek text are given according to the order and in the sequence of the 24 letters of the Greek alphabet
 462: ##### 4.1.17.2 If there be no Presanctified, then the Idiomelon and Martyricon stichera on "Lord, I have cried" are not taken, but are transferred with their two refrains to the Aposticha
 463: ##### 4.1.17.3 It is not good to neglect prostrations at the stichera of St. Andrew
 464: ##### 4.1.17.4 At the entire divine service of this day we use sacred vestments of Lenten colors, as usual
 465: AT COMPLINE: We sing Small, without prostrations. After "It is truly meet" - Kontakion of the Great Canon.
 466: Midnight Office: Without prostrations. After the 1st Trisagion - usual troparia, after the 2nd - Kontakion of the Great Canon.
 467: AT MATINS
 468: ##### 4.1.17.5 From the beginning to the end of the Sessional Hymns of the Octoechos, given at the end of the Triodion, at the 1st Kathisma, we sing everything according to the general Lenten rubric, then Psalm 50 and immediately, having omitted the litany "Save, O God", the Great Canon[^551]. At the time of the singing of the canon the holy doors are opened and candles are lit on the holy table. Before the holy doors in cathedral churches a rug is spread, on which first the Bishop, if he be present, and then the other sacred ministers two by two, according to the rank of their dignity, at each ode make one great prostration, after the singing of each troparion of the ode of the canon. In our seminary, the seminarians make prostrations before the holy doors, and in the sanctuary, before the steps of the altar, all eight superiors make prostrations according to the rank of their dignity, one at one ode, by turn, and at the 9th Ode - all eight together, in epitrachelia
 469: ##### 4.1.17.6 Canons two: one - the Great [Canon] of St. Andrew, of nine odes, the second - triodion, contains the 4th, 8th and 9th Odes, which also in these odes takes the first place. The odes of the nine-ode canon do not have an equal number of troparia and each of them has at the end two troparia to St. Mary of Egypt and one to St. Andrew of Crete. The triodion we sing on 10 troparia with the first heirmos, for the 2nd heirmos is not sung. Refrains to the troparia of the Great Canon are these: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee", then "Venerable Father Andrew, pray to God for us", then "Venerable Mother Mary, pray to God for us". To the troparia of the triodion the refrain will be - "Holy Apostles, pray to God for us"[^552], because according to content they belong to the service of Thursday. At each troparion of the Canon of St. Andrew the rubrics prescribe three prostrations, but we make only one, however, great, and in cathedral temples the clergy makes prostrations only by turn and adapted to the nine odes of the canon. The choirs sing the canon in the middle of the church, each at a separate analogion, making at the troparia of the canon a small prostration. As Katavasia at all odes we take the heirmos of the last canon[^553]
 470: After the 3rd Ode - Sessional Hymn of the Triodion, after the 6th - Kontakion and Ikos of the Triodion with the Beatitudes; after the 9th - Trinity Sessional Hymn, all this - with the usual litanies. At the 9th Ode we sing "More honorable", as the Moscow and the new Constantinopolitan Typika also have. After the Canon - "It is truly meet"[^554].
 471: ##### 4.1.17.7 Everything else, from the Praises psalms to the end of Matins, is taken according to the general Lenten rubric, only, if we do not add the 1st Hour, then after the 16 final prostrations at the prayer of St. Ephrem we recite the Trisagion with "Our Father" and "Lord, have mercy" (12), and then the Priest: "Glory to Thee, O Christ God" and dismissal
 472: #### 4.1.17.1 AT THE HOURS
 473: Everything - according to the usual Lenten rubric, however, after the Trisagion we recite at all Hours only the one Kontakion of the Canon, and the 1st Hour - without Kathisma.
 474: AT THE TYPIKA AND AT VESPERS: Everything - according to the usual Lenten rubric.
 475: LITURGY
 476: According to the rubric there should be the Presanctified, however, now we do not sing it during Great Lent, with the exception of Wednesdays and Fridays. In the archcathedral church on this day only read liturgies are celebrated.
 477: 
 478: FIFTH SATURDAY OF GREAT LENT - OF THE AKATHIST[^555]
 479: Note
 480: The service of this feast is of the small type; it has only the Katavasia at Matins after each ode and the Great Doxology and is combined with the usual service of Lenten Saturday and with the Temple Canon at Matins. The peculiarity of this feast lies in that at its Matins the whole order of the Akathist to the Most Pure Virgin Mary is sung, the 12 ikos-Kontakia of which are divided into four quarters, the first of which is sung instead of the Sessional Hymn after the first Kathisma, the second - instead of the Sessional Hymn - after the second Kathisma, the third - after the 3rd, and the fourth - after the 6th Ode of the Canon; the initial Kontakion is sung at the beginning and at the end of each quarter, and before the last singing of it - once more the first Ikos[^556]. This Matins, according to the rubric, is sung at the 4th hour of the night, but we sing it at the usual time[^557]. The service of the regular saint, according to the rubric of the Greek Triodion, is sung at Compline.
 481: RUBRIC
 482: AT VESPERS WITH PRESANCTIFIED
 483: ##### 4.1.17.1.1 Kathisma usual
 484: ##### 4.1.17.1.2 On "Lord, I have cried" - stichera on 10: Idiomelon of the day twice, one Martyric and of the feast on 7, Glory, Both now: of the feast
 485: ##### 4.1.17.1.3 At "O Gladsome Light" - Prokeimenon of the Triodion and reading, second Prokeimenon of the Triodion and reading and the rest of the Presanctified
 486: Small Compline: After "It is truly meet" - Kontakion of the feast only[^560].
 487: Midnight Office - Saturday.
 488: AT MATINS
 489: ##### 4.1.17.1.4 On "God is the Lord": Troparion of the feast twice; Glory, Both now: once more
 490: ##### 4.1.17.1.5 After the 1st Kathisma - Small Litany and the initial Kontakion "To the Directress" is sung by the Choir. The Priest, dressed in all sacred vestments of light color, opens the holy doors and censes everything as usual; then, having come to the altar, sings the first quarter of the ikos-Kontakia and, after its conclusion, the same choir sings once more the initial Kontakion "To the Directress". All rubrics at this singing prescribe standing; (and therefore this is called Akathist, that is non-sitting). The Choir sings the Kontakion in the middle of the church majestically and solemnly
 491: ##### 4.1.17.1.6 After the 2nd Kathisma and after the 3rd and 6th Odes of the Canon, immediately after the Small Litany, the Priest sings the other three quarters of the ikos-Kontakia, and the Choir - the Kontakion "To the Directress" at the beginning and at the end of each quarter. At the beginning of each quarter the Priest censes everything just as at the beginning of the first quarter[^558]
 492: This Akathist order is celebrated usually at the altar. In the cathedral temple it is sung at the altar of the Mother of God, which is located in its right nave; and then the Priest censes the altar and everything else, as usual, and immediately, having left the holy doors open, goes out through them to the altar of the Most Holy Theotokos and sings there the Akathist order, censing from the altar at the beginning of each quarter the icon of the Mother of God, the sacred ministers, the choirs and the people. After singing the 4th quarter of the ikos-Kontakia the Priest returns to the sanctuary, closes the holy doors and goes to the sacristy, where he takes off the sacred vestments and, having put on the epitrachelion, continues the service of Matins.
 493: ##### 4.1.17.1.7 Canons 2 [making] 12: Temple of the Saint with heirmos on 6 and of the feast on 6. Katavasia "I shall open my mouth" up to the 6th Ode. From the 6th Ode we do not take the Canon of the Temple, but we sing 3 canons on 14, that is of the feast on 6 and both canons of the triodion on 8 with the addition of two troparia, that is one Martyric with the refrain "Wondrous is God", and the second - for the dead, with the refrain "Their souls", and the Katavasia of the Triodion. Refrain to the troparia of the Canon of the Theotokos - the general "Most Holy Theotokos, save us", however, among us they like to refrain the acrostic of the canon "Container of Joy, to Thee alone it is fitting to rejoice". In Greek: "Vessel of joy, to Thee alone it is fitting to rejoice". Both the troparia and this refrain we sing to the melody given in the new Heirmologion on the Akathist Saturday
 494: After the 3rd Ode, after the last singing of the Kontakion "To the Directress", we recite the SESSIONAL HYMN of the feast; after the 6th, immediately after the Small Litany, is sung the last quarter of the ikos-Kontakia with the Kontakion "To the Directress" before the beginning and after the conclusion, however, its last Kontakion "O All-praised Mother" is sung three times, after this - the 1st Ikos and then - "To the Directress". At the 9th Ode we sing "More honorable" and after the 9th - Exapostilarion of the feast.
 495: ##### 4.1.17.1.8 Stichera of the Praises - 4: all - of the feast, Glory, Both now: of the feast
 496: ##### 4.1.17.1.9 After the Great Doxology - Troparion of the feast
 497: AT THE HOURS AND AT THE LITURGY: Everything - only of the feast; only the Epistle and Gospel first - of the day, and then - of the feast.
 498: ### 4.1.18 Fifth Sunday of Great Lent
 499: Everything - according to the rubric of the 2nd Sunday, here on page 360.
 500: MONDAY, TUESDAY, WEDNESDAY, THURSDAY AND FRIDAY
 501: ### 4.1.19 Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday and Friday of the Sixth Week of Great Lent
 502: Everything - according to the general rubric of past weeks.
 503: 
 504: ## 4.2 Flower Triodion (Pentecostarion)
 505: PRESCRIPTIONS OF THE SYNOD OF LVIV TO PASTORS
 506: ON DIVINE WORSHIP
 507: FROM THE SATURDAY OF LAZARUS TO BRIGHT TUESDAY
 508: INCLUSIVE
 509: ##### 4.2.1 On the Saturday before Flowery Sunday, called Lazarus [Saturday], let the Liturgy be sung in church
 510: ##### 4.2.2 On Flowery Sunday let everything be celebrated as usual, according to the rubric of a feast of the Lord of the first rank with the addition of the blessing of branches at Matins
 511: ##### 4.2.3 On the three following days of Great Week it is fitting to sing the Liturgy of the Presanctified
 512: ##### 4.2.4 On Thursday of Passion Week it is fitting to sing the Liturgy together with Vespers
 513: ##### 4.2.5 On the same day, after sunset, it is fitting to sing the Office of the "Passions" with the 12 Gospels
 514: ##### 4.2.6 On Friday, which we mark as a solemn feast, let the Hours be celebrated in the morning in church, called Royal, and about noon - Vespers with the bringing out of the Shroud[^559], which, when it is brought out, is placed before the iconostasis in the so-called tomb, and there let it remain for constant veneration by the people until Resurrection Matins
 515: ##### 4.2.7 It would be very desirable that the pastors on the same day, after the placing of the Shroud, preach to the people at a convenient time a word on the passion and death of Christ
 516: ##### 4.2.8 It is also entrusted to the same pastors to celebrate on this Friday, after sunset, Tomb Matins in church, in view of the divine service of this day and in view of the solemn rites celebrated at its end
 517: ##### 4.2.9 On Great Saturday itself it is fitting to sing the Liturgy of St. Basil with Vespers
 518: ##### 4.2.10 On the Sunday of the Resurrection very early it is fitting to sing Matins with all the rites that precede and accompany it, according to the rubric approved by this Synod. In cathedral churches, similarly as in non-cathedral ones, this Matins is usually anticipated and celebrated on Saturday evening; the Synod considers that such a custom may be adhered to
 519: ##### 4.2.11 On the first three days of Bright Week it is fitting daily to sing Matins, Liturgy and Vespers in church
 520: ##### 4.2.12 The Synod forbids all priests read liturgies throughout the whole Passion Week, and on the first three days of this week prescribes only the Liturgy of the Presanctified; on Great Thursday and Saturday - only the sung Liturgy, that is of St. Basil the Great with Vespers (Title IV, Chapter I. 3. 5). On Great Friday, with the exception of the feast of the Annunciation, the Liturgy should not be celebrated
 521: Note
 522: From this Saturday to the Sunday of Ap. Thomas inclusive only the Triodion is sung, and the Menaion - only if the Annunciation falls, and from Bright Monday to the Sunday of Ap. Thomas inclusive, if a saint with Vigil or Polyeleos falls. The Canons of saints without Polyeleos of these 16 days are prescribed for Compline, beginning from Monday of the 2nd week of Great Lent, as was noted above, on page 357.
 523: 
 524: ### 4.2.1 Lazarus Saturday
 525: Note
 526: The service of this feast is of the small type and only at Matins, from the Canon onwards, - great. However, also before the Canon it has some parts of the Sunday service, namely after the 2nd Kathisma, that is "The Blameless", it has "The Choir of angels", after the 2nd Sessional Hymn it has "The Resurrection of Christ" and before the Exapostilarion - "Holy is the Lord our God" three times.
 527: RUBRIC
 528: On Friday evening
 529: AT VESPERS WITH PRESANCTIFIED
 530: ##### 4.2.1.1 Kathisma proper
 531: ##### 4.2.1.2 On "Lord, I have cried" - 10 stichera: Idiomelon of the day twice, Martyricon once, then 7 of the feast, Glory, Both now: of the feast
 532: ##### 4.2.1.3 At "O Gladsome Light" - Prokeimenon of the Triodion and one reading of the Triodion, then 2nd Prokeimenon, 2nd reading of the Triodion and everything else of the Presanctified
 533: AT Small Compline
 534: We sing the Canon of Lazarus in the Triodion, after the Canon, instead of "It is truly meet", - Heirmos of the 9th Ode of the Canon. After the Trisagion - Kontakion of the feast only.
 535: AT THE Midnight Office
 536: After the 1st Trisagion, instead of the troparia "Uncreated Nature", we read the Troparion of Lazarus; after the 2nd Trisagion, instead of the troparia "Remember, O Lord", - Kontakion of Lazarus, and the prayer "Remember" we do not say.
 537: AT MATINS
 538: ##### 4.2.1.4 On "God is the Lord": Troparion of the feast twice, Glory, Both now: the same
 539: ##### 4.2.1.5 After the 1st and 2nd Kathismata - Sessional Hymn of the feast, however, after the 2nd Kathisma, before the Sessional Hymn, we sing "The Choir of angels" exactly as on Sunday; and after the Sessional Hymn - "The Resurrection of Christ", Psalm 50 and immediately Canon
 540: ##### 4.2.1.6 Canons of the feast - two: 1st - with heirmos on 8 and 2nd - on 6. From the 6th Ode - tetraodion, heirmos - twice, troparia - on 6, then the other canon on 6. Katavasia after each ode - Heirmos of the 2nd Canon. Refrain to the troparia - "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee". After the 3rd Ode - Sessional Hymn, after the 6th - Kontakion and Ikos of the feast; at the 9th we do not sing "More honorable"; after the 9th we do not say "It is truly meet" until the Sunday of Ap. Thomas; after the 9th - Exapostilarion of the feast, however, before the Exapostilarion we sing "Holy is the Lord our God" three times
 541: ##### 4.2.1.7 Stichera of the Praises - 8: all - of the feast, with two Sunday verses, as every Sunday; Glory: of the feast, Both now: "Most blessed Art Thou"
 542: ##### 4.2.1.8 After the Great Doxology - Troparion of the feast only
 543: ##### 4.2.1.9 Dismissal specific
 544: AT THE HOURS AND AT THE LITURGY: Everything - only of the feast, and at the Liturgy, instead of the Trisagion, we sing "All Who have been baptized into Christ".
 545: ### 4.2.2 Flower Sunday (Palm Sunday)
 546: [^562]Everything - according to the general rubric of a feast of the Lord with All-Night Vigil without Litiya. It has everything proper to itself, and at the Liturgy - Antiphons and Entrance Hymn. However, before the Troparion of Flowery [Sunday] we sing yesterday's Troparion of Lazarus; only after the Great Doxology we sing the Troparion of Lazarus alone.
 547: AT Great Vespers: On "Lord, I have cried" - stichera on 10; and at the blessing of loaves - Troparion of Lazarus twice and of Flowery [Sunday] - once.
 548: #### 4.2.2.1 AT Great Matins
 549: ##### 4.2.2.1.1 On "God is the Lord": Troparion of Lazarus twice, Glory, Both now: of Flowery [Sunday]
 550: ##### 4.2.2.1.2 The blessing and distribution of branches takes place, according to the rubric, immediately after the 50th Psalm, during the kissing of the Gospel. According to our custom, the blessing takes place after the 50th Psalm, and the distribution - during the anointing with oil (myrovanie), that is during the canon. And it takes place thus: When the Priest has sung the Gospel, he places it on the analogion near the tetrapod, between two candles lit on candlesticks. On the tetrapod are placed branches and prepared censers and sprinklers. The Priest approaches the tetrapod and at the time when the Choir reads the 50th Psalm, having put incense in and blessed the censer, censes the branches from the four sides of the tetrapod and, after the conclusion of the 50th Psalm, when the Deacon exclaims (if there be none, then the Priest himself) "Let us pray to the Lord", reads aloud (from the Sluzhebnik (lit. "Service Book") or from the Triodion[^563] ) the first prayer "O Lord our God", and the Choir responds: "Amen". Priest: "Peace be to all"; deacon: "Bow your heads unto the Lord"; and, after "To Thee, O Lord", the Priest reads the second prayer "O Lord God Almighty... unto ages of ages"[^564]; choir: "Amen"; the Priest sprinkles the branches with holy water, saying: "These branches are blessed and sanctified" and the rest; and, after singing the litany "Save, O God", with His right hand anoints the people, and with His left hand distributes to all the branches, which the Deacon solemnly hands to him, and if there be no deacon, then one of the church servers[^565]
 551: After the 9th Ode we do not read the Exapostilarion, but immediately: "Holy is the Lord our God" (3) in Tone 4.
 552: AT THE LITURGY: After the Entrance - Troparion of Lazarus, Glory: of FLOWERY [SUNDAY], Both now: Kontakion of FLOWERY [SUNDAY]. We sing the Trisagion.
 553: FAST FOR THE WHOLE PASSION WEEK
 554: On Monday, Wednesday and Friday the Synod of Lviv prescribes a strict fast. On Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday it permits also dairy products (Title XI, part 4).
 555: ### 4.2.3 Great Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday
 556: Notes
 557: ##### 4.2.3.1 The sacred vestments of these days and of the whole Passion Week, beginning from Flowery Sunday evening, should be of violet color
 558: ##### 4.2.3.2 All these three days have one form of divine service, that is Lenten, as in the Forty Days [Lent], only with certain exceptions, as given below:
 559: AT VESPERS
 560: a) On Flowery Sunday evening
 561: ##### 4.2.3.3 On "Lord, I have cried" - stichera of the Triodion on 6, Glory: Triodion, Both now: Triodion
 562: ##### 4.2.3.4 Entrance, Prokeimenon of the day ("Bless the Lord now") and immediately "Vouchsafe, O Lord"
 563: ##### 4.2.3.5 Aposticha of the Triodion with specific verses
 564: ##### 4.2.3.6 After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart" with the Trisagion - Troparion "Virgin Theotokos" and everything else with prostrations, as on the previous Sundays of Great Lent
 565: ##### 4.2.3.7 Dismissal specific, so also on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday at the end of the Hours: "Christ the Lord, Who goes"[^567]
 566: b) On Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday evening
 567: AT VESPERS WITH PRESANCTIFIED
 568: ##### 4.2.3.8 On "Lord, I have cried" - 10 stichera: all - of the Triodion, Glory, Both now: Triodion
 569: ##### 4.2.3.9 Entrance with the Gospel and, after "O Gladsome Light", - two Prokeimena of the Triodion, each - with its reading
 570: ##### 4.2.3.10 After "Let my prayer be set forth" the Priest: "And that we may be accounted worthy" and the rest and reads the Gospel of Matthew, Section 98 and the rest of the Presanctified with the dismissal "Christ the Lord, Who goes"
 571: Note: If there be no Presanctified, then on "Lord, I have cried" we sing stichera on 6, and the three last we transfer to the Aposticha with the usual verses, singing the first twice. We make the Entrance with the Gospel and, after the second reading of the Triodion, we sing the Gospel, as above, and everything else with prostrations, according to the Lenten custom.
 572: #### 4.2.3.1 AT COMPLINE
 573: On Sunday evening we sing Small Compline, according to the rubric of other Sundays of Great Lent, and at it - the triodion of the Triodion, and after the Trisagion - Kontakion of the Triodion only.
 574: On Monday and Tuesday evening - Great Compline with prostrations according to the Lenten rubric, and at it also - the triodion of the Triodion and after the Trisagion - Kontakion of the Triodion, then "O Lord of Hosts, be with us"[^568].
 575: On Wednesday evening we sing Small Compline[^569], also at it - the triodion of the Triodion and, after the Trisagion, - Kontakion of the Triodion only.
 576: AT THE Midnight Office: Nothing special.
 577: AT MATINS
 578: ##### 4.2.3.1.1 At Alleluia, instead of the Trinity Hymns, we sing the Troparion "Behold the Bridegroom" twice, Glory, Both now: the same
 579: ##### 4.2.3.1.2 Three regular Kathismata with their Sessional Hymns, then "And that we may be accounted worthy", Gospel of Matins[^570], according to the sequence of Gospels, Psalm 50 and "Save, O God"[^571]
 580: ##### 4.2.3.1.3 Canon only one: triodion on Monday and Wednesday, or diodion [two-ode canon] on Tuesday. Troparia - on 12, heirmoi - twice. We do not recite the [Biblical] Odes, but only the refrain to the troparia of the canon "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee", then the Katavasia, heirmos of the canon once both choirs together. Before the Kontakion-Ikos the Priest sings the Small Litany; at the 9th Ode we do not sing "More honorable", nor "It is truly meet" after the canon, but immediately after the Katavasia - Small Litany and Exapostilarion "Thy bridal chamber" twice, Glory, Both now: three times the same
 581: ##### 4.2.3.1.4 Stichera of the Praises - 4: of the Triodion, Glory, Both now: Triodion, Small Doxology and, after "Let us complete", - Aposticha of the Triodion and everything else with prostrations, as on the Lenten days of Great Lent
 582: #### 4.2.3.2 AT THE HOURS
 583: Everything - according to the general Lenten rubric of Great Lent, only:
 584: ##### 4.2.3.2.1 At the 1st and 9th Hours there will be no Kathisma, but it will be only at the 3rd and 6th
 585: ##### 4.2.3.2.2 Immediately after the Theotokion "O Theotokos, Thou Art the vine" at the 3rd Hour and, after the corresponding Theotokia, at the other two Hours, the rubrics prescribe the reading of the Four Gospels, which today among us is read only in cathedral, or conciliar, churches[^573]. At the 6th Hour we read the Gospel not immediately after the Theotokion, but after the conclusion of the Troparion of the Prophecy and the Paremia with its Prokeimena. The reading of the Four Gospels covers all the Evangelists, that is Matthew, Mark and Luke in full, and John - only up to the "Passion of Christ", that is up to "Now is the Son of man glorified", Section 46, verse 13.32. All the Evangelists, taken together, are divided into 9 readings, according to the number of the three Hours (3, 6, 9) and three days (Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday). Matthew is divided into 2 readings, Mark - into 2, John - into 2, and Luke - into 3. The first reading covers the first half of Matthew, the second - the second half of Matthew, the third - the first half of Mark, the fourth - the second half of Mark, the fifth - the first part of Luke, the sixth - the second part of Luke, the seventh - the third part of Luke, the eighth - the first half of John, the ninth - the second half of John. The rubric does not indicate where the first half of the three Evangelists and the first and second parts of Luke end. But since Matthew has 28 chapters, its half ends with the 14th chapter, Mark - 16 chapters, so its half ends with the 8th chapter, Luke - 24 chapters, so its first part ends with the 8th chapter, and the second - with the 16th. John, up to "Now is [the Son of man] glorified", has 12 chapters and part of the 13th chapter, therefore its half ends with the 6th chapter and part of the 7th
 586: The Priest, at the beginning of each reading, dressed in a phelonion of Lenten color, opens the holy doors and censes everything as usual, then, having come out through the holy doors to the analogion placed before the holy doors facing the people, on which stand two candlesticks with lit candles, reads from there the Gospel, beginning from "And that we may be accounted worthy". After the conclusion of each reading, having kissed the beginning of the reading and leaving the Gospel on the analogion until the end of the 3rd reading, he returns to the sanctuary and, having closed the holy doors, takes off the phelonion[^574].
 587: ##### 4.2.3.2.3 After the Trisagion - Kontakion of the Triodion
 588: AT THE TYPIKA
 589: ##### 4.2.3.2.4 Only one Kontakion of the Triodion
 590: ##### 4.2.3.2.5 In Slavonic rubrics and the Greek Typikon of Sabbas, on Great Wednesday, instead of the dismissal the prayer "O Master most merciful" is given, which is at Vespers with All-Night Vigil, and in Slavonic ones - also the prayer of forgiveness for sins committed in Great Lent, and commemorations. However, these superfluous additions of the Greco-Slavs are unknown to the Greeks. The prayer "O Master most merciful" and the forgiveness may be retained perhaps only in monasteries. The commemorations, which are superfluous here, will be taken later, at the end of Compline and the Midnight Office, which have nothing in common with forgiveness for the sins of the Forty Days
 591: On Wednesday
 592: AT VESPERS WITH PRESANCTIFIED,
 593: AT COMPLINE AND AT THE Midnight Office
 594: Everything - according to the rubric of Monday and Tuesday, here on pp. 379-380 [→REF:p379-380], only on Wednesday, after the dismissal of the Liturgy of the Presanctified, the prostrations in church cease, and in the cells are made until the ringing for Matins of the bright Resurrection of Christ[^575]. We, however, until the Resurrection of Christ make three great prostrations in church, at the end of the Divine Service, singing the verse "Though Thou didst suffer", and during the veneration of the Shroud, singing "The noble Joseph".
 595: 
 596: ### 4.2.4 Great Thursday
 597: AT MATINS
 598: 1.	"Blessed is our God", "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee", "O Heavenly King" and everything else, as usual, with the Two Psalms and with the Six Psalms up to the end of the litany "In peace let us pray to the Lord".
 599: ##### 4.2.4.1 Instead of "God is the Lord" we sing Alleluia in Tone 8, that is in the tone of the following troparion; but since this troparion has a specific melody in the Heirmologion, we sing Alleluia according to the pattern of its melody
 600: ##### 4.2.4.2 Troparion "When the glorious disciples" twice, Glory, Both now: once more the same
 601: ##### 4.2.4.3 There will be no Kathismata and Sessional Hymns, but immediately the Gospel from Luke, Section 108 and 1st verse of Section 109, that is the 39th verse of the 22nd chapter[^577]; then Psalm 50 and, leaving out "Save, O God", we sing immediately the Canon
 602: ##### 4.2.4.4 Canon only one: heirmoi - twice, troparia - on 6[^578] with the refrain "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee". Katavasia after each ode - heirmos of the same canon once, both choirs together. After the 3rd Ode we recite the Sessional Hymn, after the 6th - Kontakion and Ikos, at the 9th we do not sing "More honorable", nor after the 9th - "It is truly meet", but instead of this, - the heirmos of the canon[^580] and immediately the Exapostilarion twice, Glory, Both now: the same
 603: ##### 4.2.4.5 Stichera of the Praises - 4 and, after the Small Doxology, - "Let us complete" and Aposticha with specific verses
 604: 7.	"It is a good thing" once, Trisagion with "Our Father" and Troparion "When the glorious disciples", without Theotokion.
 605: ##### 4.2.4.6 Priest: "Wisdom"; Choir: "Bless"
 606: Priest: "Blessed be He... ages"; Choir: "Amen"; and 1st Hour.
 607: #### 4.2.4.1 AT THE HOURS
 608: ##### 4.2.4.1.1 At all: Troparion and Kontakion of Great Thursday, however, at the 1st Hour, after the Theotokion "What shall we call Thee", we read the Troparion of the Prophecy, Prokeimenon, Paremia and 2nd Prokeimenon
