 609: ##### 4.2.4.1.2 The Dismissal "Christ the Lord, Who goes"[^581] we recite at the 1st Hour, and at the others, since they are sung together with the Typika, we recite this dismissal at the end of the Typika. All this we recite in our cells
 610: AT THE TYPIKA
 611: ##### 4.2.4.1.3 Begins from the Beatitudes, without stichera. The Creed may be omitted, since it will be at the Liturgy
 612: ##### 4.2.4.1.4 Instead of the usual Kontakia we recite the Kontakion of Great Thursday
 613: ##### 4.2.4.1.5 After the Kontakion - "Lord, have mercy" (40), "O All-holy Trinity"[^582] and dismissal
 614: Great Thursday evening
 615: AT VESPERS WITH THE LITURGY OF ST. BASIL[^583]
 616: Note
 617: "It is fitting for the Priest on Great Thursday at the Liturgy to consecrate two Lambs, in order to consume one at Communion, and to place the other in the artophorion and keep in the tabernacle in the usual place until today (Friday)". Thus in our Sluzhebnik[^584]. Regarding the Lamb itself, which is to be kept in the tabernacle until the day of exposition, the Synod of Lviv orders that "it before consecration be fitted to its vessel, the so-called Melchizedek, into which it is well inserted and carefully wiped, so that afterwards crumbs do not fall from it; so that placed in such a way in the Melchizedek, it be consecrated at the Liturgy of one of the preceding days and kept in the tabernacle until the exposition itself". When the Priest prepares the Lamb at the Proskomedia, wishing to use it for exposition, he does not say over it the words "In remembrance of the Lord" etc., nor does He perform over it the sacred actions which are usually performed over the Lamb that is to be consumed at the same Divine Service, for it is considered only communicative; it is enough only to cut it, so that it would be convenient to break and consume it on another day.
 618: RUBRIC
 619: ##### 4.2.4.1.6 From the beginning to "Lord, I have cried" everything - according to the rubric of the Eve of the Nativity of Christ, here on pp. 169-170 [→REF:p169-170]
 620: ##### 4.2.4.1.7 On "Lord, I have cried" - stichera on 10
 621: ##### 4.2.4.1.8 Entrance with the Gospel and 3 readings of the Triodion, the two first - with their Prokeimena, and the third - without Prokeimenon. The Prokeimenon of the day from the Horologion is not taken
 622: ##### 4.2.4.1.9 Immediately after the 3rd reading - Small Litany with the exclamation of the Trisagion, Trisagion, Prokeimenon of the Triodion, Epistle and Gospel and, according to the order, Liturgy of Basil the Great
 623: ##### 4.2.4.1.10 Instead of the Cherubic Hymn, also after the transfer of the Holy Gifts, instead of the Communion Hymn and "Let our mouths be filled", we sing the Troparion "Of Thy Mystical Supper". So in general editions. In our Manuscript Typikon, our Sluzhebnyky (lit. "Service Books") and the Moscow Typikon, instead of "In Thee rejoiceth", is prescribed the Heirmos of the 9th Ode of the Canon ("Come, let us the faithful"). The Euchologion of Benedict gives "Of Thy Mystical Supper" only instead of "In Thee rejoiceth". (In the order of the Liturgy of Basil)
 624: AT Small Compline: Triodion of the Triodion and, after the Trisagion, - Kontakion of Great Friday only.
 625: AT THE DAILY Midnight Office: Everything - as usual, in the cells.
 626: 
 627: ### 4.2.5 Great Friday
 628: AT MATINS
 629: THE SERVICE OF THE HOLY AND SAVING PASSION
 630: OF OUR LORD JESUS CHRIST
 631: Notes
 632: ##### 4.2.5.1 We sing this Matins after sunset; according to the rubric - at the 2nd hour of the night
 633: ##### 4.2.5.2 Before the holy doors is placed an analogion with two candlesticks, facing the people, and on it - the Gospel
 634: GENERAL OVERVIEW
 635: From the usual beginning to the end of the troparion after "Alleluia" and from the Canon to the end of Matins everything - according to the rubric of Matins of Great Thursday, here on pp. 383-384 [→REF:p383-384]. Between the troparion and the canon there will be five Sessional Hymns, each of which has before it three antiphons of the Passion troparia, without Kathismata and small litanies, then the Beatitudes, Prokeimenon and Psalm 50. Besides this we read 12 Passion Gospels: the first - after the troparion, the five following - after each of the five Sessional Hymns, the seventh - after the Beatitudes, the eighth - after the 50th Psalm, the ninth - after the Exapostilarion, the tenth - after the Praises, the eleventh - after "Let us complete", the twelfth - after the Aposticha. After the singing of each Gospel we ring all the church bells and, after the twelfth Gospel, we do not ring until the Resurrection itself, but instead of bells we use wooden clappers. But it is better already at Passion Matins not to ring, but to strike clappers or boards, for Passion Matins is a time of sorrow, to which the joyful sounds of bells do not correspond. Also in Rome already at Passion Matins clappers are used.
 636: DETAILED RUBRIC
 637: ##### 4.2.5.3 From the usual beginning to the end of the litany "In peace let us pray to the Lord" everything - as at Matins daily[^585]
 638: ##### 4.2.5.4 Instead of "God is the Lord" we sing Alleluia in the tone of the following troparion
 639: ##### 4.2.5.5 Troparion "When the glorious disciples" twice, Glory, Both now: once more the same
 640: ##### 4.2.5.6 When the troparion is sung the third time, the Priest vests in a violet phelonion, goes before the steps of the altar, bows to the Holy Mysteries and, having opened the holy doors, recites the prayer of the censer, after which, having blessed the censer: "Blessed is our God", censes around the holy table, then, having stood before the steps of the altar and bowed low, goes out through the holy doors before the iconostasis and censes the local icons, the choirs and the people and, having returned through the holy doors to the sanctuary, gives up the censer and, having again bowed low, sings the Small Litany without exclamation, then goes out through the holy doors to the analogion and exclaims: "And that we may be accounted worthy", "Peace be to all", "Wisdom, Aright" and the rest. The Choir, instead of "Glory to Thee, O Lord", sings "Glory to Thy Passion, O Lord"[^586]. Priest: "Let us attend" and reads the first Gospel. After the conclusion of the reading the Choir, instead of "Glory to Thee, O Lord", sings: "Glory to Thy long-suffering, O Lord"[^587]. The Priest, having kissed the beginning of the reading, returns to the sanctuary and, having closed the holy doors and bowed low to the Holy Mysteries, goes to the sacristy, takes off the phelonion and goes to his place
 641: All this - exactly so at the readings of the other Gospels, with the exception of the litany and censing, which according to the rubric of our Triodia and the Typikon of the Lviv University, will be only at the 1st Gospel and at the five Sessional Hymns, and the censing - only of the holy table. They give thus: "We do not sit at these Sessional Hymns, since the Priest censes the holy table, but we sing them standing"[^588]. Finally we consider that it is fitting to cense not only at the Sessional Hymns, but also at all other Gospels, for the censing takes place not for the sake of the Sessional Hymns, but for the sake of the Gospels, however, only the holy table (around), as our Triodia have, which mention the censing only of the holy table. Everything should be censed only twice, that is at the 1st Gospel and at the Canon, at the heirmos of the 9th Ode.
 642: According to Slavonic rubrics the Abbot or Superior should sing the first Gospel, and according to others also the twelfth. In the cathedral temple the Bishop reads them, others - the sacred ministers, according to the rank of their dignity[^589].
 643: If there be deacons, they remain from the beginning of Matins, dressed in dalmatic with orarion of violet color, in the sanctuary, at their places, until they begin to sing the third time the troparion "When the glorious disciples"; then they come out together with the Priest who will sing the Gospel, dressed in a violet phelonion, before the steps of the altar and, having bowed together with him to the Holy Mysteries, open the holy doors, cense everything as usual, as at the beginning of the Liturgy, return before the steps of the altar and, having given up the censers and bowed both together to the Holy Mysteries, go out, each through his door, before the holy doors and, again having bowed to the Holy Mysteries, stand there until the second deacon after the singing of the troparion sings the Small Litany; then, having bowed to the Holy Mysteries and having exchanged their places, they proceed to the analogion so that, when the Priest approaches the analogion, the first Deacon is on the right, and the second - on the left of him. When the Priest, having bowed to the Holy Mysteries, comes out through the holy doors to the analogion, the first Deacon exclaims: "And that we may be accounted worthy". Priest: "Peace be to all". Second deacon: "Wisdom, Aright. Let us listen". Priest: "The Reading from (Name)". First deacon: "Let us attend". Priest - reading. After the conclusion of the reading, the Priest kisses the beginning of the reading first himself, afterwards the Deacon who is on the right kisses [it], and after him the one who is on the left. All three return to the sanctuary: the Priest - through the central, and the deacons - through the side doors, stand together with the Priest before the steps of the altar and, having closed the holy doors and bowed all together to the Holy Mysteries, go to their places. At the other Gospels, since there will be no Small Litany, the deacons, having come out before the holy doors, bow and, having exchanged places, proceed to the analogion and, when the Priest stands between them, exclaim: "And that we may be accounted worthy" and the rest, as above.
 644: If the Bishop or other sacred ministers be present, the deacons should cense them before the choirs and neither the Priest nor the deacons kiss the Gospel before the Bishop and sacred ministers. And therefore both deacons together carry the open Gospel to the Bishop and sacred ministers to kiss, then to the Priest standing in the holy doors, and when he kisses it, then they also kiss [it] and place [it] on the analogion; then, having bowed low to the Holy Mysteries, return, each through his door, to the sanctuary.
 645: ##### 4.2.5.7 After the singing of the first Gospel follow five Sessional Hymns, each of which has before it three antiphons of the Passion troparia, and after itself - one Passion Gospel. The number of troparia in all antiphons is not the same and therefore, according to the rubric, each must be repeated[^590], except the Theotokion, with which each antiphon concludes, with the refrain "Glory, Both now"[^591]
 646: ##### 4.2.5.8 The Beatitudes, with the Prokeimenon and the 6th Gospel at the end. The number of stichera on the Beatitudes - 7, and with "Glory, Both now" - 9[^592]
 647: ##### 4.2.5.9 Psalm 50 and the eighth Gospel
 648: ##### 4.2.5.10 Canon - triodion, heirmoi - twice, troparia - on 12, Katavasia after each ode - its heirmos, both choirs together. After the 5th Ode - Small Litany and Kontakion-Ikos; at the 9th Ode we do not sing "More honorable", but only the heirmos "More honorable"[^593]; after the 9th we do not sing "It is truly meet", but we sing the Katavasia[^594]; then - Small Litany and three times the Exapostilarion with the refrain "Glory, Both now", as usual, then - the ninth Gospel
 649: ##### 4.2.5.11 Stichera of the Praises on 4, Glory: one sticheron, Both now: another, then - the tenth Gospel
 650: 10.	"To Thee belongs glory"[^595], "Glory to Thee Who Hast shown us the light" and the Small Doxology.
 651: ##### 4.2.5.12 Litany "Let us complete" and, after the exclamation "For Thou Art a merciful [God]"[^596], immediately - the eleventh Gospel
 652: ##### 4.2.5.13 Aposticha and the twelfth Gospel
 653: 13.	"It is a good thing", Trisagion, "Our Father", Troparion of Friday "Thou Hast redeemed".
 654: ##### 4.2.5.14 Litany "Have mercy on us, O God" and the specific dismissal of Great Friday, intermediate, that is Priest: "Wisdom", Choir: "More honorable"; Priest: "Glory to Thee, O Christ" and the rest, as usual[^597]. We do not combine with the 1st Hour
 655: ERECTION OF THE TOMB OF GOD
 656: On Friday morning, before the beginning of the Royal Hours, the Shroud and the most beautiful Book of the Holy Gospels is placed on the holy table. Before the holy doors is placed the Tomb of God, at which, according to the custom of the northern and western Latin churches[^598], the Holy Mysteries are exposed until the Resurrection of Christ itself. Our Sluzhebnyky prescribe placing on this Tomb the Artophorion with the Holy Mysteries. According to the custom of our archcathedral temple, the Holy Mysteries are exposed in a monstrance on the main altar. And the Tomb of God should be erected so that above it rises a cross without the Crucified One, with a cloth hung on its crossbar and with the instruments of Christ's passion, it should be decorated with costly carpets, surrounded by many candlesticks and lamps and vessels with small trees and flowers. The front board of the sarcophagus is covered with red damask, to which a cloth is attached, and to it afterwards the Shroud will be attached. The board itself should not lie horizontally, but slanted so that the Shroud attached to it would be visible and accessible for veneration.
 657: ROYAL HOURS
 658: In the archcathedral church they are sung at 10 o'clock in the morning, together with the Typika and with Vespers[^599]. We sing everything according to the rubric of the Royal Hours of the Eve of the Nativity of Christ. However, since the Tomb of God is placed before the holy doors, the analogion of the Gospel is placed a little further from it, the analogia of other readings - further from it. And everything that on the Eve of the Nativity of Christ the sacred ministers recite before the holy doors, they now recite before the Tomb, but they do not cense the Tomb, since there is nothing in it yet.
 659: TYPIKA (Typika)
 660: We join it to the 9th Hour, but we do not celebrate from the beginning, as on the Eve of the Nativity, but from the Beatitudes, without stichera, in this way:
 661: 1.	"The Beatitudes", "Glory, Both now"; "Remember us, O Lord" (3).
 662: 2.	"The Choir of heavenly hosts" with verses, Both now: "I believe".
 663: 3.	"Remit, pardon", "Our Father", Kontakion of Great Friday.
 664: 4.	"Lord, have mercy" (12); priest: "O All-holy Trinity".
 665: 5.	"Blessed be the name of the Lord" (3), "I will bless the Lord".
 666: 6.	"It is truly meet" with "More honorable than the Cherubim".
 667: ##### 4.2.5.15 Priest: "Glory to Thee, O Christ God" and dismissal of Great Friday, to the people
 668: Today there is no Liturgy, unless the Annunciation falls, and immediately after the Typika we begin Vespers.
 669: On Great Friday
 670: AT VESPERS
 671: Notes
 672: ##### 4.2.5.16 At this Vespers there will be an Entrance with the Gospel and, at its end, at the last sticheron of the Aposticha, - the procession with the Shroud and the placing of it in the Tomb[^600]
 673: ##### 4.2.5.17 All actions that the sacred ministers at usual Vespers perform before the iconostasis, at this Vespers they perform before the Tomb of God
 674: RUBRIC
 675: ##### 4.2.5.18 From the usual beginning to "Lord, I have cried" everything - as at Daily Vespers, without Kathisma
 676: ##### 4.2.5.19 On "Lord, I have cried" - stichera on 6, Glory: one sticheron, Both now: another. Entrance with the Gospel
 677: ##### 4.2.5.20 Instead of the Prokeimenon of the day there will be Prokeimenon of the Triodion, Paremia and third Paremia; then - third Prokeimenon of the Apostle, Apostle, "Alleluia" and Gospel. At "Alleluia" there will be censing. "Let us attend. Peace be to all. Wisdom, let us attend" we exclaim only at the 1st and 3rd Prokeimena. We begin the Gospel from "Wisdom, Aright". Instead of "Glory to Thee, O Lord" before the Gospel will be "Glory to Thy Passion, O Lord", and after the Gospel - "Glory to Thy long-suffering, O Lord", exactly so as at Matins
 678: 4.	"Let us all say", "Vouchsafe", "Let us complete" and Aposticha.
 679: ##### 4.2.5.21 At the last sticheron of the Aposticha, that is at "Thee, Who Art clothed with light", takes place the procession with the Shroud and the placing of it in the Tomb. According to the custom of our cathedral churches this takes place in the following way: During the singing of the Aposticha the procession is formed in the church. On the altar, on the left side, stands the monstrance, candles are lit on the altar and at the Tomb
 680: The sacred ministers, the Bishop and the four most worthy canons, who will carry the Shroud, vest in all sacred vestments of their rank, and the other canons and priests - only in epitrachelia and phelonia, some - only in epitrachelia, and two deacons - in all diaconal [vestments]. Lit candles are distributed to the canons and other priests in the sanctuary, and to the brotherhood - in the church. The sacred ministers approach the steps of the altar and bow low. The Bishop ascends to the altar, takes the Shroud, spread on the altar, and gives it to the four canons so that each holds it by one corner. Then the Deacon who is on the right ascends to the altar and, having bowed low, unlocks the artophorion, takes from there the pyx with the Holy Mysteries, places [it] on the (folded) antimension, takes from there the Lamb with the stand into which it is inserted, not touching it with his fingers, but holding by the stand, places [it] into the monstrance and locks it well. Having locked the pyx, he places [it] into the artophorion and, having bowed, locks it also; and places the monstrance on the antimension so that it faces the people, steps aside until the Bishop, kneeling, censes the Holy Mysteries three times, each time - with a prostration at the end, and, having taken upon himself the omophorion (aer), approaches the altar. Then the Deacon, having bowed to the Holy Mysteries, takes with both hands the monstrance and hands it to the Bishop, who before that makes a prostration. The Bishop turns to the right to the people, and when the singers begin to sing "Thee, Who Art clothed with light", goes out behind the clergy through the holy doors on the northern side of the Tomb into the church and, having entered under the canopy, surrounded by candle-bearers and preceded by two deacons who cense unceasingly, proceeds behind all to the church doors. In front goes the cross-bearer, then the banner-bearers, four girls icon-bearers, after them - the church brotherhood, the seminarians, the seminary choir, then, from the holy doors, - priests, canons, four sacred dignitaries who carry the Shroud, turned with feet to the people, and at the end - the Bishop with deacons who cense, and candle-bearers. The procession goes out of the church and turns to the right, that is to its northern side and, having gone around the church three times (or, as now they do there, - once), returns to the church. Those who carry the Shroud, and the other priests stand before the Tomb, and the Bishop with the deacons returns by the southern side of the Tomb, through the holy doors, to the sanctuary. The right deacon receives from his hands the Holy Mysteries and places [them] on the altar. The Bishop kneels and, having put aside the omophorion (Velum), censes the Holy Mysteries three times, each time bowing his head; the Deacon, having bowed, exposes the Holy Mysteries at the top of the tabernacle. Having bowed before the steps of the altar, all three depart: the Bishop through the central, the deacons - through the side doors before the Tomb. The Bishop receives the Shroud from the canons who hold it, and places [it] on the Tomb, and they fasten it to the Tomb. When the singers have finished singing "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart", the Trisagion and the rest with "Our Father", the Bishop exclaims: "For Thine is the Kingdom" and begins to sing with the servers the troparion "The noble Joseph"; at the end he makes with the servers a low bow, and all the people - a great prostration to the ground. Then the second time the same troparion - the second choir, and all - a prostration, as before. And where there will be only one choir, the first time the troparion is sung by the sacred ministers, the second time - by the Choir, the third time the half - by the sacred ministers, and from "wrapped [it]" and further - by the Choir[^601]. After the singing of the troparion and after the prostrations all kiss the Shroud, according to the order, having made before the kissing one prostration: first the Bishop, and after him - all other sacred ministers, according to the rank of their dignity. After this there will be the Great Dismissal, specific to this Saturday, after which the sacred ministers return to the sanctuary, leaving the holy doors open until the end of Bright Week, take off the sacred vestments and go out, and the people kiss the Shroud[^602].
 681: 
 682: The icon of the Shroud is transferred on Holy and Great Friday from the sanctuary at the end of Vespers, while the Dismissal Troparia "The noble Joseph", etc. are sung, and is placed on a prepared table in the middle of the presbytery, where there are already and remain lit candles with vessels of flowers throughout the whole day until the hour of Matins of Great Saturday (which is celebrated on the evening of Great Friday).
 683: 
 684: Notes
 685: ##### 4.2.5.22 Where there will be only one priest, let him choose for himself four most honorable laymen to carry the Shroud
 686: ##### 4.2.5.23 If the pastor has several churches, then in the mother [church] He sings Vespers with the bringing out of the Shroud, and in the filial ones - only brings out the Shroud thus: after "Blessed is our God" and "O come, let us worship" (3) immediately - procession with "Thee, Who Art clothed with light" and, after the procession, - "Glory to Thee, O Christ God", dismissal and "The noble Joseph" (3) with prostrations
 687: Small Compline
 688: This Compline, as also the Midnight Office, we read in private. At Compline - the Canon on the Crucifixion of the Lord and on the Lamentation of the Most Holy Theotokos.
 689: After "It is truly meet" - Kontakion of Great Saturday.
 690: SATURDAY Midnight Office: Everything - as usual.
 691: ### 4.2.6 Matins of Great Saturday
 692: Notes
 693: ##### 4.2.6.1 This Matins we sing usually on Friday evening, after sunset, although the rubrics prescribe it at the 7th hour of the night
 694: ##### 4.2.6.2 The sacred ministers remain during Matins before the Tomb of God, where seats and a table with candlesticks and books are prepared for them. Sitting, they sing Matins from there: the priests - in epitrachelia and phelonia, and the deacons - in dalmatics of violet color
 695: RUBRIC
 696: ##### 4.2.6.3 From "Blessed is our God" to "O come, let us worship" exclusively everything - as usual at Matins; then after "Lord, have mercy" (12), without "O come, let us worship" the Priest immediately: "Glory to the Holy" and the Six Psalms up to "God is the Lord", as usual[^603]
 697: ##### 4.2.6.4 On "God is the Lord" - Troparion "The noble Joseph" (2), Glory: "When Thou didst descend", Both now: "The angel stood by the tomb"[^604]
 698: 3.	17th Kathisma ("The Blameless") in three stations with the Encomia (Praises), with censing at the beginning of each station and a Small Litany after each station.
 699: Regarding the censing, we suppose that it is sufficient to cense only the Shroud (together with the Holy Mysteries, if they be exposed on the tomb), the choirs and the people[^605].
 700: About the Encomia (Praises), in Greek Triodia called Engkomia (praise), let it be known that before each of them one verse of the Kathisma is sung, until all are finished; only the first troparion of each station (in the editions of Pochaiv Triodia also the second troparion of the second station) is sung without a verse both at the beginning and at the end of each station, with the exception of the third, after which the first troparion is not sung and the Small Litany is not recited, but immediately - "The Choir of angels" and, after the singing of it, - Small Litany.
 701: ##### 4.2.6.5 After "The Choir of angels" with the Small Litany - Sessional Hymn, 50th Psalm and Canon
 702: ##### 4.2.6.6 Canon: heirmoi - twice, troparia - on 12. Refrain - "Glory to Thee, O Lord, for Thy holy burial". Katavasia, heirmos of the canon, - both choirs together
 703: After the 3rd Ode - Sessional Hymn, after the 6th - Kontakion-Ikos, at the 9th we do not sing "More honorable"[^606] and after the 9th we do not recite "It is truly meet", but the heirmos; and afterwards, instead of the Exapostilarion, we sing "Holy is the Lord our God" (3).
 704: 6.	4 Stichera of the Praises, then one at "Glory" and one at "Both now".
 705: ##### 4.2.6.7 At the Great Doxology we make the Entrance with the Gospel and, instead of the one troparion after the Doxology, there will be one Sticheron of the Praises (Shroud [Epitaphios]), two troparia and three readings, that is one - of the Prophecy, one - of the Apostle and one - of the Gospel
 706: The Entrance takes place thus: During the singing of the Stichera of the Praises the Priest and deacons, if there be any, having bowed low before the Shroud, and simultaneously also before the Holy Mysteries, go to the sacristy and vest in all sacred vestments of their rank. During the singing of the Doxastikon also the other sacred ministers, who are before the Tomb of God, dressed in phelonia, having bowed low, depart to the sanctuary and, when the Priest with the deacons comes before the steps of the altar, stand together with him on both sides and bow all together to the Holy Mysteries. After singing the Praises [Stichera] the Priest exclaims: "Glory to Thee Who Hast shown us the light", then puts incense in for the left deacon and, when the Doxology ends, approaches the altar, takes from it the Gospel, gives it to the right deacon and, preceded by candle-bearers and the Deacon with the censer, they make the Entrance just as at the Liturgy. Having stood before the Tomb of God: the right deacon - on the right, and the left - on the left of the Priest, closer to the Tomb, the other sacred ministers - on two wings, a little at a distance, await the conclusion of the Trisagion and the sticheron "Come, let us bless". After the conclusion of the singing of the sticheron the first deacon, raising the orarion in the direction of the people, exclaims: "Let us attend", the Priest, blessing the people: "Peace be to all", the second deacon, raising the orarion: "Wisdom, let us attend" and we sing the Troparion "The noble Joseph" once. The first deacon places the Gospel on the analogion facing the people, the second gives up the censer and the Troparion of the Prophecy once[^607].
 707: Then again: "Let us attend. Peace be to all. Wisdom, let us attend", Prokeimenon, Reading of the Prophecy, Second Prokeimenon, Reading of the Apostle and "Alleluia", during which the deacons cense the Tomb of God, the present sacred ministers and the people. After this the first deacon: "Wisdom, Aright! Let us listen"; Priest: "The Reading from the Holy Gospel according to Matthew". Choir: "Glory to Thy Passion, O Lord". Second deacon: "Let us attend"; the Priest sings the Gospel, facing the people. After its conclusion the Choir: "Glory to Thy long-suffering, O Lord". Then the Priest, having kissed and closed the Gospel, leaves it on the analogion, and the first deacon sings the litany "Let us all say", and the second - "Let us complete our prayer" in full, as usual.
 708: ##### 4.2.6.8 After the dismissal we sing the Troparion "The noble Joseph" (3) with prostrations exactly as at Vespers. The Deacon takes the Gospel from the analogion, the sacred ministers depart to the sanctuary and take off the sacred vestments, the Deacon places the Gospel on the altar and, having bowed, departs and unvests
 709: #### 4.2.6.1 AT THE HOURS
 710: ##### 4.2.6.1.1 At all: Troparion and Kontakion of Great Saturday
 711: ##### 4.2.6.1.2 Dismissal of Matins of Great Saturday
 712: AT THE TYPIKA: Exactly as on Great Thursday, here on page 385; however, the Greek Triodion does not give the Typika.
 713: On Great Saturday evening
 714: AT VESPERS WITH THE LITURGY OF ST. BASIL
 715: ##### 4.2.6.1.3 According to the custom of the archcathedral church, this Vespers begins at 9 o'clock in the day[^608]
 716: ##### 4.2.6.1.4 On this day there will be only one Vespers, that is Great with the Liturgy of St. Basil and without All-Night Vigil, and after the Prayer behind the Ambo, or (as the rubrics prescribe) after the dismissal of the Liturgy, there will be the Blessing of Loaves, as usual at the All-Night Vigil
 717: ##### 4.2.6.1.5 The form and rubric of this Vespers is the same as the Vespers on the Eve of the Nativity, here on pp. 169-171 [→REF:p169-171], without "Blessed is the man"; only here, after "O Gladsome Light", there will be no Prokeimenon, but immediately 15 readings, between which there will be no troparia, and at the 6th reading all verses of the Song of Moses are read with the refrain "For gloriously has He been glorified", and at the 15th reading the verses of the Song of the Three Youths are read with the refrain "Praise the Lord and exalt Him above all for ever". Instead of "Alleluia" we sing the last verse of the 81st Psalm with its other verses, in the form of a Prokeimenon[^609]. Dismissal of Matins of Saturday
 718: ##### 4.2.6.1.6 Although the service of the feast usually begins at Vespers of the preceding day and therefore the whole Resurrection service should be celebrated in bright vestments, nevertheless, since the Liturgy, with which Vespers is sung, is still of the Saturday day, in the part of the verses on "Lord, I have cried" we sing about the descent of the Savior's soul into hell and therefore from the beginning of Vespers we use violet vestments, and afterwards change them after the conclusion of the Apostle, at the verses instead of "Alleluia", in order to read the Gospel already in bright vestments[^610]
 719: ##### 4.2.6.1.7 Throughout the whole Bright Week, beginning from the Vespers of this day, the Resurrection service is sung and, besides the stichera of the Triodion, are sung also the Resurrection stichera of the Octoechos, each day - in a different tone, that is on Sunday - in Tone 1, on Monday - in Tone 2, on Tuesday - in Tone 3, on Wednesday - in Tone 4, on Thursday - in Tone 5, on Friday - in Tone 6, on Saturday - in Tone 8, omitting Tone 7
 720: #### 4.2.6.2 AT COMPLINE
 721: In Greek and Slavonic Triodia, except ours, Compline is not given, but from the Blessing of Loaves to the Tomb Order, which is sung immediately before Resurrection Matins, the reading of the whole book of the "Acts of the Apostles" is prescribed, although among us today these "Acts" are sung perhaps only in cathedral and seminary temples; and they are sung by verses by clerics two by two, alternately.
 722: This Compline should be Small. Finally, even our Triodion leaves the choice to read it or not, for it is written about it: "if there be". In any case, in our Triodion is given the Canon on the Burial of Christ and on the Lamentation of the Most Holy Theotokos. After the 9th Ode, instead of "It is truly meet", will be the heirmos of this ode and, after the Trisagion, - Kontakion of Great Saturday.
 723: INSTEAD OF THE Midnight Office[^611]
 724: Note: We sing it before the Shroud, immediately before Resurrection Matins either only in epitrachelion and phelonion, as usual in the provinces, or in all sacred vestments of violet color, as in cathedral churches.
 725: RUBRIC
 726: ##### 4.2.6.2.1 From the usual beginning to "O come, let us worship" we celebrate everything, as usual at the Midnight Office; and immediately Psalm 50 and Canon
 727: ##### 4.2.6.2.2 The Tomb Canon of Matins of Great Saturday "He Who in ancient times hid the pursuing tyrant beneath the waves of the sea"; according to the rubric, heirmoi - twice, and troparia - on 12 (today - with heirmos on 4), with the refrain "Glory to Thee, O Lord, for Thy holy burial", after which Katavasia and heirmos - both choirs together
 728: After the 3rd Ode - Sessional Hymn, and after the 6th - Kontakion-Ikos of Great Saturday; after the 9th "It is truly meet" will not be, but only the heirmos of this ode.
 729: ##### 4.2.6.2.3 Trisagion and the rest with "Our Father" and Troparion "When Thou didst descend"
 730: ##### 4.2.6.2.4 Litany "Have mercy on us, O God", which is at the Midnight Office, and dismissal of Matins of Great Saturday[^612], beginning from "Glory to Thee, O Christ God"
 731: ##### 4.2.6.2.5 At the end: "The noble Joseph" (3) with prostrations, as at Matins of Great Saturday, but the Shroud is kissed only by the sacred ministers, according to rank, and the Bishop, taking the Shroud from the Tomb, hands it to four canons and thus all the sacred ministers return to the sanctuary and four canons hang the Shroud behind the holy table over the High Place[^613]. Then they depart to the sacristy, take off the violet vestments and vest in all bright sacred vestments of their rank, and at this time in the church all candles are lit
 732: Note on the Shroud
 733: Regarding the time and place of the placing of the Shroud we do not find an ancient rubric, for this rite is later and different in different regions. According to the custom of our archcathedral church the Shroud remains hung behind the holy table, over the High Place, from Resurrection Matins to the Apodosis of the Resurrection inclusive, that is until Wednesday before the Ascension. According to the custom of our other churches, the Shroud, taken from the Tomb before Resurrection Matins, is placed on the holy table, where it remains during the whole Bright Week, and from the Sunday of Ap. Thomas to the Apodosis of the Resurrection - behind the holy table. According to others - it remains on the altar, the antimension with the Gospel is placed on it and the Liturgy is celebrated on it. However, it is better to place the Shroud behind the holy table, for lying on the altar, it is often significantly damaged by candles, from which wax drips on it.
 734: ### 4.2.7 Beginning of Holy Pentecost
 735: PROCESSION WITH THE HOLY MYSTERIES AROUND THE CHURCH[^614]
 736: After the Shroud is taken from the Tomb of God and transferred to the sanctuary, the sacred ministers, having dressed in all the brightest sacred vestments of their rank, go out before the steps of the altar and, having bowed all together low to the Holy Mysteries, bend their knees and receive lit candles; so also the brotherhood in the church. The Deacon, who is on the right (or the Priest himself, if there be no deacons) approaches the middle of the altar and, having bowed low, places the Gospel on its right side, then, having taken the Holy Mysteries from the tabernacle and placed them on the antimension, steps aside a little, and the Bishop (or main priest), having censed the Holy Mysteries three times, as usual, and having taken upon himself the omophorion, rises, ascends the steps and, having bowed, receives the Holy Mysteries, after which turns to the people and begins to sing the sticheron "Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior". Under the joyful sound of all bells the procession around the church takes place, with everything, as was given on Great Friday at Vespers, here on page 394, except the Shroud, which now, by the decision of bl. m. Cardinal Sembratovych, should not be carried, for this does not correspond to the joy of the Resurrection; rather it is fitting to carry the icon of the Resurrection, as it is in the Triodion, at the beginning of Resurrection Matins, during the procession to the church doors. Therefore, when the main sacred minister begins to sing the sticheron "Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior", the choirs and people take up the singing and sing it, repeating, all the time, until the procession ends, namely the circuit of the church either three times, or at least once. When the circuit ends, all enter the church; in order, however, to avoid confusion during the second procession, those carrying banners and icons remain before the church doors, and in the church prepare for the procession the cross-bearer with two candle-bearers, the brotherhood, choirs and clergy. When the sacred ministers enter the sanctuary, the main priest ascends to the altar and, having turned to the people, blesses them with the Holy Mysteries, quietly saying: "Save, O God, Thy people and bless Thine inheritance", places the Holy Mysteries on the altar, descends before the steps, bends the knees and, having taken off the omophorion, censes the Holy Mysteries three times, as usual; the Deacon, having approached the Holy Mysteries, bows low, takes them with the stand from the monstrance and places into the artophorion, and places the artophorion into the tabernacle and, having bowed, locks it. And where there will be no monstrance, the Holy Mysteries are placed in the artophorion and with it are locked in the tabernacle.
 737: Note: This procession with the Holy Mysteries before Resurrection Matins - is a later addition of our churches, borrowed not from the Greeks and not from the Romans, but only from the Latin churches of these parts, superfluous to the majesty of our Resurrection Matins and is not given in our rubrics.
 738: 
 739: ### 4.2.8 Resurrection Matins
 740: ##### 4.2.8.1 PROCESSION BEFORE THE CHURCH DOORS. All people go out of the church, and after them go out also the sacred ministers. And the procession takes place thus: All sacred ministers, in all their sacred bright vestments, stand before the steps of the altar. The main sacred minister takes the cross, the Deacon - the censer, all together bow low to the Holy Mysteries and turn to the west. The main one begins to sing the sticheron "Thy Resurrection, O Christ Savior", all take up the singing of the sticheron and go out from the sanctuary to the church: the Priest - through the holy [doors], and all other sacred ministers - through the Deacon's doors; at this time all bells ring, and all go to the great church doors and, having gone out of the church, stand according to rank before the church doors, which are immediately closed[^615]. In the middle of the church is placed on the holy table first of all the icon of the Resurrection of Christ, usually on the Artos, also other holy icons, reliquaries and the book of the Holy Gospels in the most precious binding or something else of the sacred things, all this - according to the number of priests who will give them to be kissed by the people at the end of Matins. Outside, before the church doors, Matins begins in the following way[^616]
 741: ##### 4.2.8.2 BEGINNING OF MATINS. Immediately after the church doors are closed, the main priest, holding with his left hand the cross, and with his right - the censer and censing the church doors[^617], exclaims loudly: "Glory to the Holy" and the rest. The Choir responds: "Amen"; the Priest gives up the censer and sings loudly the troparion "Christ is risen", also all - the same, then the Priest the second time - the same and all - the same, and the third time the Priest - the same and all - the same, then the Priest in a high voice exclaims the verses, and all after each verse sing this troparion once[^618]. At the end the Priest, having sung in a higher voice the same troparion only up to "trampling down death by death" inclusive, opens the doors, and all finish: "and upon those in the tombs bestowing life" and again all bells ring, all enter the church[^619]. The Matins prayers at Resurrection Matins throughout the whole Bright Week are not recited, for they are connected with the Six Psalms, and since there will be no Six Psalms here, there will be no prayers. If it were necessary to recite the prayers, it should be indicated in the rubric where they should be recited, for during the verses "Let God arise", which take the place of the Six Psalms, it is not possible to recite them, for at this time the rubric orders the Priest to sing verses, and not to add prayers as well
 742: ##### 4.2.8.3 ENTRANCE INTO THE CHURCH. The entrance of the procession into the church takes place in the reverse order to the exit from the church, that is first enters the main priest, after him - other priests and sacred ministers, all the clergy, then singers, brotherhood, banner- and icon-bearers, the cross-bearer and all people. The priests enter the sanctuary and approach the holy table. The Bishop, if there be one, departs to his throne. The Deacon stands in his place before the holy doors and sings from there the litany
 743: ##### 4.2.8.4 After the entrance into the church the first deacon sings the Great Litany "In peace let us pray to the Lord", standing in the usual place, and immediately we sing the Canon
 744: ##### 4.2.8.5 Canon of the Resurrection: heirmoi - 4 times (in Greek ones - twice), troparia - on 12. (Today heirmoi - once, troparia with heirmos - on 4). Katavasia after each ode - heirmos of the canon, both choirs together - once. The Priest sings the heirmoi, and the choirs - the troparia and Katavasia. Refrain to the troparia of the canon - "Christ is risen from the dead", at the penultimate - "Glory", and at the last - "Both now", as usual
 745: At the beginning of the canon, after the singing of the heirmos, the Priest censes everything, as usual[^620].
 746: After each ode the deacons, from their usual places before the holy doors, sing the Small Litany with separate exclamations, which the priests sing alternately in the sanctuary[^621].
 747: After the 3rd Ode - Hypakoe; after the 6th - Kontakion-Ikos and "The Resurrection of Christ" (3), "Jesus having risen from the grave" once (according to others - three times); at the 9th, after "O Theotokos and Mother of Light", the usual censing takes place and, instead of "More honorable" we sing "The angel cried" and "Shine, shine"; after the 9th - Exapostilarion of the Resurrection three times.
 748: ##### 4.2.8.6 Stichera of the Praises - 8: 4 Sunday of the Octoechos of Tone 1, with the usual verses from "Praise Him", and 4 of the Resurrection with specific verses, then Glory, Both now: to the Resurrection, "Christ is risen" (3), can be more, until the kissing is finished
 749: ##### 4.2.8.7 KISSING ONE ANOTHER. Is prescribed in the rubrics at "Christ is risen", after the conclusion of the last sticheron of the Resurrection. However, today we do not kiss one another as in the sticheron: "and let us embrace one another", but we kiss only the precious cross, the Gospel and holy icons, which the priests hold, greeting everyone who approaches with the words: "Christ is risen", and they answer: "Truly He is risen". If there be many people, then we begin the kissing not after the stichera of the Resurrection, but from their beginning, that is from the verse "Let God arise". If there be very many people, then the kissing will be also during the canon. And this kissing takes place thus:
 750: If there be only one priest, he stands in the holy doors and from there gives the cross to be kissed by the people, greeting everyone: "Christ is risen", and the one Who kisses answers: "Truly He is risen". If there be several priests, then first the main one goes out from the holy doors and stands before the iconostasis, on the right side, that is opposite the icon of the Savior, looking to the north. After Him the second priest comes out from the holy doors with the Gospel, approaches the main one, and he gives him the cross to kiss, saying: "Christ is risen", having kissed, in His turn, gives Him the Gospel to kiss, answering: "Truly He is risen" and stands on His left. Then comes out the third priest with the icon of the Resurrection of Christ, approaches the first and He gives Him the cross to kiss, saying: "Christ is risen", and having kissed gives Him the icon of the Resurrection to kiss, answering: "Truly He is risen", and approaches the second priest, who gives him the Gospel to kiss, saying: "Christ is risen", and He, having kissed the Gospel, gives the second to kiss the icon of the Resurrection, answering: "Truly He is risen", and stands on the left of the second. The fourth priest comes out with the icon of the Theotokos, approaches the first, also the second and the third, of whom each gives him his object to kiss, saying: "Christ is risen", and having kissed gives each of them the icon of the Theotokos to kiss, answering: "Truly He is risen". So do also all other priests, as many as there be. In cathedral churches the Bishop, sitting on his throne opposite the icon of the Savior, gives the cross to be kissed, also each of the canons gives His insignia to be kissed, sitting on the seat. And when the kissing between the priests ends, then other sacred ministers and all the people approach one by one each Priest in turn, starting from the first, and kiss his insignia, answering: "Truly He is risen"[^622]. After the kissing once was read the "Homily" of Chrysostom, which is in the Flower Triodion.
 751: ##### 4.2.8.8 Litanies "Have mercy on us, O God" and "Let us complete" are sung by deacons, standing in their usual places
 752: ##### 4.2.8.9 Great Dismissal, specific, at which, instead of "More honorable", we sing "Shine, shine"[^638] and, instead of "Glory, Both now", we sing "Christ is risen" once. The Priest stands with the cross in the holy doors, and the Deacon (if there be none, then the Priest himself) exclaims: "Wisdom". Choir (or second deacon, if there be one)[^623]: "Bless"
 753: Priest: "Blessed be Christ our God... ages".
 754: Choir: "Amen". "Confirm, O God, the catholic faith unto ages of ages".
 755: Priest: "Most Holy Theotokos, save us".
 756: Choir: "Shine, shine...".
 757: Priest: "Glory to Thee, O Christ God, our hope, glory to Thee".
 758: Choir: "Christ is risen from the dead... bestowing". "Lord, have mercy" (3), "Lord, bless".
 759: Priest: Dismissal with the cross: "Christ, Who rose from the dead, trampling down death by death and upon those in the tombs bestowing life, our true God, through the prayers of His most pure Mother, of the holy, glorious and all-laudable apostles, of our venerable and God-bearing fathers and of all the saints, have mercy on us and save us, for He is good and loves mankind".
 760: Then, raising the cross up, exclaims: "Christ is risen" (3), and we each time answer: "Truly He is risen". We sing the final "Christ is risen" (3), the whole troparion, and after this we finish with the singing "and to us He has granted life eternal, let us worship His Resurrection on the third day"[^624].
 761: Note on the doors of the iconostasis
 762: "Let it be known also that throughout the whole Bright Week the great holy doors of the iconostasis and the small side ones in all churches remain open also during communion" (Rubric of our Pochaiv Triodion and Russian Typika).
 763: RESURRECTION HOURS
 764: Instead of each of the four Hours, also instead of Compline and the Midnight Office, throughout the whole Bright Week we celebrate a short order, given in the Triodion, in our Horologia and Molitvoslovs at Resurrection Matins.
 765: Note: If the Hours are read together, then "Blessed is our God" we say only at the 1st Hour, and the others we begin from "Christ is risen" (3).
 766: #### 4.2.8.1 AT THE LITURGY
 767: Everything - according to the general rubric of a feast of the Lord, only:
 768: ##### 4.2.8.1.1 Instead of "O Heavenly King", at the Proskomedia, at the Liturgy and wherever else, we recite "Christ is risen" (3) until the Ascension; and from the Ascension to the Descent [of the Holy Spirit], instead of "O Heavenly King", we read nothing[^625]
 769: ##### 4.2.8.1.2 Regarding "Christ is risen", one should know that at "Glory to Thee, O Christ God" before the dismissal of the Proskomedia and at the Liturgy we recite "Christ is risen" once, "Lord, have mercy" (3) and "Lord, bless"
 770: At "Blessed is the Kingdom" we sing "Christ is risen" three times, that is once - the Priest and both choirs - once each (although in our Triodion is given: "priest - three times and choirs the same - three times"), and where there is only one choir, then the Priest - once and the Choir - once, then half - the Priest and half (from "and upon those in the tombs") - the Choir.
 771: Also at "With the fear of God", instead of "Blessed is He that cometh" and instead of "We have seen the true light", we sing "Christ is risen" once. Instead of "Let our mouths be filled" and "Blessed be the name of the Lord" - "Christ is risen" (3)[^626]. Among us usually "Christ is risen" is recited also instead of "Be exalted, O God, above the heavens", however, this violates the memory of the mystery of Christ's Ascension, which is mentioned in this place of the Liturgy from the beginning. Our priests say "Christ is risen" (only these two words) also after "With the fear of God", after "Save, O God" and after "Always, now and ever", however, in no rubric do we find this.
 772: ##### 4.2.8.1.3 Instead of the Trisagion we sing "All Who have been baptized into Christ"
 773: ##### 4.2.8.1.4 During the reading of the Gospel, at each verse, all bells are rung[^627]
 774: Our Sluzhebnyky: "If served conciliarly, then this Gospel is read by all priests and deacons by verses as the Superior decides". About this you have a detailed rubric in our and Russian Triodia. However, the custom that one and the same Gospel be read by all priests and deacons - is a superfluous invention of the Greco-Slavs, which today takes place among us only when the Gospel is read in different languages, as happens in our cathedral temples, in which the Bishop reads it in Greek from the holy doors, then the Deacon - in Slavonic from the ambo, and at the end canons and priests, placed throughout the whole church, in different liturgical languages. In Russia the Bishop reads the Gospel in Slavonic, and other priests - in Hebrew, in Greek and in Latin, in those languages in which the inscription on the Cross was written, then in other new languages (Muralt. 14. Brief. S. 142). The Greeks also read the Gospel, according to the new custom, in different languages, however, not at the Liturgy, but at Vespers (the Gospel read at Vespers of this day), as happens in the Patriarchate of Constantinople[^628].
 775: ##### 4.2.8.1.5 Instead of "It is truly meet", according to the new rubric, we sing the heirmos "Shine, shine" with the refrain "The angel cried" as in the Triodion and in the Constantinopolitan Typikon, but without the troparia of the 9th Ode of the Canon, as in our Sluzhebnyky, for these troparia are not about the Most Holy Theotokos, but about Christ's Resurrection
 776: ##### 4.2.8.1.6 Before the dismissal, instead of "More honorable", we sing "Shine, shine" and instead of "Glory, Both now" - "Christ is risen" once. Dismissal with the cross and the rest, which is after the dismissal with the raising of the cross exactly as was indicated for Resurrection Matins
 777: ##### 4.2.8.1.7 BLESSING OF THE ARTOS. After the Prayer behind the Ambo[^629] takes place the blessing of the Artos, for which you have the prayer in the Sluzhebnik after the Liturgy of the Resurrection; after the prayer the Artos is sprinkled with holy water. And this Artos with the feast, that is the icon of the Resurrection, after the dismissal of the Liturgy, is carried from the altar, on which it was blessed, to the tetrapod, where it remains until Bright Saturday and the faithful entering the church kiss it. On Bright Saturday at the Liturgy, after the Prayer behind the Ambo, the Priest, having come out through the holy doors, reads over it the prayer for breaking, given only in our Sluzhebnik on Bright Saturday, and after this, it is taken from the tetrapod, broken in the sacristy and on the next day, that is on the Sunday of Ap. Thomas, after the Prayer behind the Ambo, is distributed to the faithful by the Priest standing in the holy doors[^630]
 778: Note: Throughout the whole Bright Week it is permitted to eat meat dishes.
 779: BLESSING OF PASCHAL FOODS
 780: It takes place, according to our custom and according to the rubric of the Triodion, outside the church or after the Liturgy (and then, going out of the church, we sing the Stichera of the Resurrection at will), or after Matins, or in homes on Saturday evening. The order of this blessing with sprinkling with holy water at the end you have both in the Sluzhebnik, and in the Trebnik, and in the Triodion, and in the Molitvoslov, after the Resurrection Hours.
 781: ### 4.2.9 On the Day of Resurrection in the Evening
 782: AT VESPERS
 783: Notes
 784: ##### 4.2.9.1 The sacred ministers, dressed in all sacred vestments of their rank during the whole Vespers stand in the sanctuary at the altar, coming out only for the Entrance (and deacons - also for the litanies) before the holy doors and for the final kissing of the sacred insignia, if there be several priests - as was given for Matins[^631]
 785: ##### 4.2.9.2 Censing is done three times, that is at the usual beginning, only before the holy table, then at "Lord, I have cried" and at "O Gladsome Light", as usual
 786: ##### 4.2.9.3 Entrance takes place with the Gospel, for it is to be read
 787: RUBRIC
 788: ##### 4.2.9.4 The Priest and deacons, if there be any, dressed in all sacred vestments of their rank, come before the steps of the altar and bow low, as usual. The Priest receives the censer with the usual prayer of blessing the censer, censes before the holy table, exclaiming: "Blessed is our God"[^632]; then, having given up the censer, ascends with the deacons the steps and sings "Christ is risen" once and both choirs - once each. After this the Priest recites clearly "Let God arise" and other verses with "Glory, Both now". The choirs, at each verse, sing "Christ is risen" once or three times exactly as was indicated for the beginning of Matins. Afterwards the Priest: "Christ is risen" up to "trampling down death by death", and the choirs: "and upon those in the tombs" and the rest
 789: 2.	"In peace let us pray to the Lord" the Priest sings at the altar, and if a Deacon - then before the iconostasis.
 790: 3.	"Lord, I have cried" - in Tone 2, with the usual censing. Stichera - Resurrection of the Octoechos of Tone 2, given in the Triodion; Glory: Triodion, Both now: 1st Theotokion (Dogmatikon) of Tone 2.
 791: ##### 4.2.9.5 Entrance with the Gospel and usual censing at "O Gladsome Light"; and, after the Great Prokeimenon, the Deacon, and if there be none, then the Priest himself: "And that we may be accounted worthy", priest: "The Reading from John...". Deacon: "Let us attend", and the Priest himself reads the Gospel from the holy doors (From John Sect. 65, up to "not believe")
 792: 5.	"Let us all say", "Vouchsafe" and "Let us complete".
 793: ##### 4.2.9.6 At the Aposticha: one Resurrection Sticheron of the Octoechos, given in the Triodion, then Resurrection Stichera with their verses and the kissing of the cross, or also of other sacred insignia exactly as was given for Matins. After the final "Christ is risen" immediately dismissal with the cross and the rest exactly as was given for Matins
 794: COMPLINE AND Midnight Office: Everything - according to the pattern of the Resurrection Hours, here on page 416.
 795: ### 4.2.10 General Rubric for All Days of Bright Week
 796: AT VESPERS
 797: Everything - as on the day of Resurrection in the evening, here on p. 421 [→REF:p421], except the Entrance, which takes place with the censer, and not with the Gospel, and there will be no Gospel.
 798: Note
 799: According to the previous rubric the Priest, at Vespers of Bright Week, from Monday onwards, should not use all sacred vestments, but from the beginning - only the epitrachelion, from the Entrance to the end - also the phelonion[^633]. Among us the custom is observed to use all sacred vestments on the first three days of Bright Week, that is on Sunday, Monday and Tuesday evening, since our people mark all these three days by abstention from work and presence at divine service. On other days of this week it is sufficient to use only the epitrachelion and phelonion.
 800: COMPLINE AND Midnight Office: According to the pattern of the Resurrection Hours, here on page 416.
 801: AT MATINS
 802: Everything - according to the rubric of the Resurrection, here on page 408, only:
 803: ##### 4.2.10.1 At the beginning of Matins we do not go out before the church doors, but begin it in the sanctuary, before the altar[^634]
 804: ##### 4.2.10.2 We sing the Small Litany only after the 3rd, 6th and 9th Odes
 805: #### 4.2.10.1 AT THE HOURS
 806: Exactly as on the day of Resurrection, only on Bright Saturday the 9th Hour is read already with three psalms, as usual, and at it - Resurrection Troparion of Tone 8 "From the height", and Kontakion - to the Resurrection "Though Thou didst descend into the grave".
 807: #### 4.2.10.2 AT THE LITURGY
 808: ##### 4.2.10.2.1 Everything - as on the day of Resurrection, changing daily the Prokeimenon, Apostle, Alleluia and Gospel
 809: ##### 4.2.10.2.2 On Saturday, after the Prayer behind the Ambo, we read the prayer for the breaking of the Artos, given in our Liturgikon, in the order of Bright Saturday[^635]
 810: GENERAL RUBRICS from the Sunday of Ap. Thomas to the Ascension
 811: To the divine service from the Sunday of Ap. Thomas to the Ascension one could apply the general rule in the middle of a feast of the Lord. However, since each Sunday, beginning from the Sunday of Ap. Thomas, has a separate name and a separate service, which extends to the other weekdays of the given week and is as if a separate feast in the Easter time, the place of the Resurrection service is taken by the service of the Sunday, also on weekdays, together with some parts of the Sunday service of the Octoechos, except the eight-day feast of Mid-Pentecost, to which the Sunday service yields on weekdays. General rules of this time are as follows:
 812: ##### 4.2.10.2.3 At the beginning of every service, instead of "O Heavenly King", we sing "Christ is risen" (3)[^636], and at the end of every divine service, according to our custom, we also sing "Christ is risen" (3), also at the end we add: "and to us He has granted life eternal, let us worship His Resurrection on the third day"[^637]; and before the dismissal, instead of "More honorable", we sing "Shine, shine"[^638]
 813: ##### 4.2.10.2.4 At Vespers: On Sunday evening for Monday there will be no Entrance, as happens on the Sundays of Lent (for here there is no Great Prokeimenon, and the Triodia give the litany "Have mercy on us, O God" at the end of Vespers), except the Sunday of Ap. Thomas, which, as a feast of the Lord, has also a Great Prokeimenon. Finally, in the provinces the Great Entrance is made every Sunday evening, regardless of whether there is a feast or not
 814: ##### 4.2.10.2.5 At Compline: From today we begin to sing the Canons of the Theotokos. After "It is truly meet" throughout the whole week, we recite the Kontakion of the Sunday; only during the eight days of the feast of Mid-Pentecost we read the Kontakion of Mid-Pentecost
 815: ##### 4.2.10.2.6 We sing the Midnight Office as usual, only after the 1st Trisagion on the feast of Mid-Pentecost[^642] we take the Troparion of Mid-Pentecost, and on the Apodosis of the Resurrection[^643] - the Resurrection Troparion of the Sunday with its Theotokion; and after the 2nd Trisagion in the middle of Mid-Pentecost we take the Kontakion of Mid-Pentecost, and outside Mid-Pentecost - Kontakion of the Resurrection. The prayer "Remember, O Lord" will not be
 816: ##### 4.2.10.2.7 We begin Matins from "Glory to the Holy" and immediately "Christ is risen" (3), then "Glory to God in the highest" and the rest; before the 50th Psalm we recite "The Resurrection of Christ": on Sundays - three times, and on weekdays - once[^639]
 817: ##### 4.2.10.2.8 At the Hours: after "Blessed is our God" we recite "Christ is risen" (3), and after the dismissal - "Christ is risen" (3) and add: "and to us He has granted life eternal" and further
 818: Note: Since we do not exclaim "Blessed is our God" when the Hour is combined with Matins or with the preceding one, also since we do not impart the dismissal when the Hour is combined with the following one, then we do not read "Christ is risen" then.
 819: ##### 4.2.10.2.9 At the Liturgy: "Christ is risen" we sing where also on the Resurrection of Christ; here, on pp. 416-418 [→REF:p416-418]
 820: Antiphons: the two first - Resurrection, and the third - daily with the Resurrection refrain, also at "O come, let us worship" both on Sundays and on weekdays.
 821: We conclude the troparia with the Kontakion of the Resurrection, except the Week of Thomas and Mid-Pentecost, for then we conclude with their Kontakion just as in the Triodion; although the troparia of the Week of Thomas can be concluded also with the Kontakion of the Resurrection, as it is in our Sluzhebnyky, in our Manuscript Typikon and Tserkovne Oko.
 822: Instead of "It is truly meet" we sing "The angel cried" and "Shine, shine", except the eight days of Mid-Pentecost, which has its heirmos.
 823: We sing the Resurrection dismissal, except the Week of Thomas, which has a specific dismissal. The dismissal with the cross we sing only on Sundays[^641], on the feast of Mid-Pentecost and on the Apodosis of the Resurrection.
 824: We suppose that also on some other days, when there be a sufficient number of people, it would be good to sing the dismissal with the cross, however, not every day, as some do, having for this neither rubric nor general custom.
 825: ##### 4.2.10.2.10 The services of saints without Polyeleos, which fall on these Sundays, as also on others until Pentecost, on the feast of Mid-Pentecost and on the Apodosis of the Resurrection, we take at Compline
 826: SPECIFIC RUBRICS
 827: from the Sunday of Ap. Thomas to the Ascension
 828: ### 4.2.11 Sunday of the Apostle Thomas
 829: Second Sunday from the Resurrection. Tone 1.
 830: We serve All-Night Vigil.
 831: We sing everything according to the general rubric of a feast of the Lord of the first rank, however, at Great Vespers there will be no readings, at Matins we sing "The Resurrection of Christ" (3) (according to others - once), and at the Liturgy there will be no specific antiphons; the feast is leavetaken on the following Saturday.
 832: WEEKDAYS OF THE WEEK OF AP. THOMAS
 833: On the weekdays until the Sunday of the Myrrh-bearers we sing everything according to the general rubric in the middle of a feast; only at the Aposticha of Vespers and at the Sessional Hymns of Matins, which are after the 1st Stichology, and at the Praises (for there will be stichera also at the Praises and afterwards, at the Aposticha) there will be some stichera taken from the weekday service of the Octoechos, according to the tone and day of the week, except Saturday, which has the full service of the feast. Also at Matins, before the 50th Psalm - "The Resurrection of Christ" once. On Saturday we sing 3 canons: of the feast with heirmoi on 6, of the saint whose temple it is on 4 and of the Menaion on 4.
 834: 
 835: ### 4.2.12 Sunday of the Myrrh-Bearing Women
 836: Third from the Resurrection. Tone 2.
 837: #### 4.2.12.1 AT Great Vespers
 838: 1.	"Blessed is our God", "Christ is risen" (3), Trisagion and the rest with "Our Father", "Lord, have mercy" (12), "O come, let us worship" (3).
 839: ##### 4.2.12.1.1 On "Lord, I have cried" - 10 stichera: 4 Sunday and 6 of the Myrrh-bearers (3 which are at "Lord, I have cried", and 3 which are at the Litiya); Glory: of the Myrrh-bearers, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the tone (Dogmatikon)
 840: ##### 4.2.12.1.2 At the Aposticha - Stichera of the Resurrection with their verses; Glory: "Thee, Who Art clothed with light", Both now: "The Day of Resurrection"[^644]
 841: ##### 4.2.12.1.3 After the final Trisagion: Sunday Troparion of Tone 2; Glory: "The noble Joseph", Both now: "The angel stood by the tomb"
 842: ##### 4.2.12.1.4 Dismissal of the Resurrection, without the cross
 843: AT COMPLINE: After "It is truly meet" - Kontakion of the Myrrh-bearers.
 844: #### 4.2.12.2 AT Great Matins
 845: ##### 4.2.12.2.1 On "God is the Lord": Sunday Troparion twice, Glory: "The noble Joseph", Both now: "The angel stood by the tomb"
 846: ##### 4.2.12.2.2 After the 1st and 2nd Stichology - Sessional Hymns of the Myrrh-bearers; after "The Blameless" - "The Choir of angels"; Hypakoe of the tone and everything else up to the canon - Sunday, as usual. Gospel will be the 2nd Sunday and "The Resurrection of Christ" three times (according to others - once)
 847: ##### 4.2.12.2.3 Canons 3 [making] 14: Resurrection with heirmos on 4, Theotokos of the Triodion on 2 and of the Myrrh-bearers on 8. Katavasia of the Resurrection
 848: After the 3rd Ode - Sessional Hymn of the Triodion[^645]; after the 6th - Kontakion-Ikos of the Triodion; at the 9th we do not sing "More honorable"[^646], but we sing "The angel cried" and "Shine, shine"; after the 9th - "Holy is the Lord our God" (3) and Exapostilarion of the Resurrection, Glory: of the Myrrh-bearers, Both now: the same.
 849: ##### 4.2.12.2.4 From the Praises to the end everything - according to the general rubric of the Sunday
 850: AT THE HOURS: At all - Sunday Troparion, Glory: "The noble Joseph"; Kontakion - of the Myrrh-bearers.
 851: AT THE LITURGY: After the Entrance - Troparion Sunday and "The noble Joseph"; Glory: Kontakion of the Triodion, Both now: of the Resurrection ("Though Thou didst descend into the grave").
 852: WEEKDAYS OF THE WEEK OF THE MYRRH-BEARERS
 853: Everything - according to the general rubric of a saint in the middle of a feast; only at the Aposticha of Vespers and at the Sessional Hymns, which are after the 1st Stichology of Matins and at the Praises (for there will be stichera also at the Praises and afterwards, at the Aposticha) there will be some stichera or troparia, taken from the weekday service of the Octoechos of the current tone, different on different weekdays, except Saturday, which has everything of the feast. And in particular, at the end of Vespers: Troparion "The noble Joseph", Glory: of the saint, Both now: to the Myrrh-bearers, the Troparia "The noble Joseph" and "When Thou didst descend" in the evening we take alternately, every other day[^647].
 854: AT COMPLINE: After the Trisagion - Kontakion of the Sunday. "Thus we take until the Sunday of All Saints" (Triodion).
 855: AT MATINS
 856: On "God is the Lord": Troparion "The noble Joseph" once and "When Thou didst descend" once, Glory: of the saint, Both now: to the Myrrh-bearers. If there be two saints with their troparia, then, we suppose, the Sunday one need not be taken.
 857: At the Sessional Hymns and at the Praises there will be two troparia or two weekday stichera of the Octoechos of the current tone, with the usual refrains; before the 50th Psalm - "The Resurrection of Christ" once, at the end of Matins the troparia just as on "God is the Lord".
 858: #### 4.2.12.3 AT THE HOURS
 859: Since no rubric gives anything about this, we consider that it should be thus: At the 1st - Troparion "The noble Joseph", at the 3rd - Sunday and Glory: of the saint, at the 6th - to the Myrrh-bearers, at the 9th - again "The noble Joseph" and Glory: of the saint. Kontakia: at the 1st and 6th - of the Myrrh-bearers, at the 3rd and 9th - of the saint. If there be two saints, then at the 3rd, after "Glory", will be the Troparion to the first, and at the 9th - to the second saint[^648].
 860: #### 4.2.12.4 AT THE LITURGY
 861: Troparia: "The noble Joseph", Sunday and to the Myrrh-bearers; Glory: Kontakion of the Myrrh-bearers, Both now: Kontakion of the Resurrection[^649]; or Glory, Both now: Kontakion of the Myrrh-bearers, without the Kontakion of the Resurrection[^650].
 862: If the service to a saint or for some need is also taken, then after the three troparia of the Sunday we take also the troparion to the saint or for the need; also the Kontakion to the Myrrh-bearers, Glory: Kontakion to the saint or for the need, and Both now: Kontakion to the Myrrh-bearers. Epistle and Gospel of the day. Everything else - of the Sunday of the Myrrh-bearers or also to the saint or for the need, if there be any.
 863: ### 4.2.13 Sunday of the Paralytic
 864: Fourth from the Resurrection. Tone 3.
 865: #### 4.2.13.1 AT Great Vespers
 866: ##### 4.2.13.1.1 On "Lord, I have cried" - 10 stichera: 7 of the Octoechos (given also in the Triodion) and of the Triodion on 3. Glory: Triodion, Both now: Dogmatikon of the tone
 867: ##### 4.2.13.1.2 At the Aposticha one Sunday sticheron, then Stichera of the Resurrection, Glory: of the Paralytic, Both now: "The Day of Resurrection"
 868: ##### 4.2.13.1.3 After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart" - Sunday Troparion of Tone 3, Glory, Both now: Sunday Theotokion in the tone of the Troparion
 869: ##### 4.2.13.1.4 Dismissal of the Resurrection, without the cross
 870: AT COMPLINE: After "It is truly meet" - Kontakion of the Paralytic only.
 871: #### 4.2.13.2 AT Great Matins
 872: ##### 4.2.13.2.1 On "God is the Lord": Sunday Troparion twice, Glory, Both now: Sunday Theotokion in the tone of the Troparion
 873: ##### 4.2.13.2.2 Two usual Kathismata, Sunday Sessional Hymns, "The Blameless", everything else up to the canon - Sunday, as usual, only Gospel - 4th Sunday and "The Resurrection of Christ" (3)
 874: ##### 4.2.13.2.3 Canons 3 [making] 14: Resurrection with heirmos on 6, Theotokos of the Triodion on 2 and of the Paralytic on 6. Katavasia of the Resurrection
 875: After the 3rd Ode - Sessional Hymn of the Paralytic, after the 6th - Kontakion-Ikos of the Paralytic; at the 9th we do not sing "More honorable", but we sing "The angel cried" and "Shine, shine"; after the 9th - "Holy is the Lord our God" (3) and Exapostilarion of the Resurrection once, Glory: of the Paralytic, Both now: the same.
 876: ##### 4.2.13.2.4 Stichera of the Praises - 8 Sunday, as usual; Glory: of the Paralytic, Both now: "Most blessed Art Thou"
 877: ##### 4.2.13.2.5 After the Great Doxology - Sunday Troparion, one of the two
 878: ##### 4.2.13.2.6 Dismissal of the Resurrection; after the dismissal - 3rd Gospel Sticheron
 879: AT THE HOURS: At all - Sunday Troparion and Kontakion of the Paralytic.
 880: #### 4.2.13.3 AT THE LITURGY
 881: After the Entrance: Sunday Troparion, Glory: Kontakion of the Paralytic, Both now: Kontakion of the Resurrection. Everything else - of the Paralytic. Communion Hymn - "Receive the Body of Christ" and "Praise the Lord".
 882: WEEKDAYS OF THE WEEK OF THE PARALYTIC
 883: The service of the Paralytic covers only two weekdays - Monday and Tuesday, for on Wednesday the feast of Mid-Pentecost already begins.
 884: On these two weekdays we sing everything according to the rubric of the weekdays of the Week of the Myrrh-bearers here, on page 429, only the troparia we take thus: at the end of Vespers and Matins - Sunday Troparion, Glory: of the saint, Both now: Sunday Theotokion in the tone of the Troparion of the Saint[^651]. On "God is the Lord": Sunday Troparion twice, Glory: of the saint, Both now: Sunday Theotokion in the tone of the Troparion of the Saint.
 885: At all Hours: Sunday Troparion, and at the 3rd and 9th - also Glory: of the saint. Kontakia: at the 1st and 6th - of the Paralytic, at the 3rd and 9th - of the saint.
 886: At the Liturgy: Sunday Troparion, Glory: Kontakion of the Paralytic, Both now: Kontakion of the Resurrection. Epistle and Gospel of the day, everything else - of the Sunday. When the service to a saint or for a need is also taken, then: Sunday Troparion and of the saint or for the need; then - Kontakion of the Paralytic, Glory: of the saint or for the need, Both now: Kontakion of the Resurrection. Everything else - as above, and also to the saint or for the need; only Communion Hymn - "Receive the Body of Christ" and to the saint or for the need.
 887: Note: If two saints fall, then at Vespers or at Matins we select the Theotokion to the troparia according to the tone of the second, and on "God is the Lord" we sing all troparia once.
 888: On Wednesday of the fourth week from the Resurrection
 889: ### 4.2.14 Mid-Pentecost
 890: Note
 891: This feast is of the Lord, of eight days, which is commemorated on the Wednesday of the Paralytic and ends on the Wednesday of the Samaritan Woman, on which it is leavetaken. On the feast itself and on the Apodosis only the service of the feast is sung, and the service of the regular saint of the Menaion is sung at Compline; on other days - it is combined with the Menaion, except the Sunday of the Samaritan Woman, for then it is combined with the service of the Sunday. This feast has no All-Night Vigil, nor Polyeleos at Matins, only the Great Doxology, and at Vespers - both Entrance and readings. We begin its service on Tuesday evening, for the liturgical day begins in the evening of the preceding day.
 892: RUBRIC
 893: AT VESPERS
 894: ##### 4.2.14.1 Kathisma proper
 895: ##### 4.2.14.2 On "Lord, I have cried" - stichera of the feast on 6
 896: ##### 4.2.14.3 After the Entrance - Prokeimenon of the day and 3 readings of the feast
 897: ##### 4.2.14.4 Aposticha of the feast, Troparion of the feast and Great Dismissal, of Pascha
 898: AT COMPLINE: We take the stichera and canon of the regular saint; after the Trisagion - Kontakion of the feast.
 899: AT THE Midnight Office
 900: After the 1st Trisagion - Troparion of the feast, and after the 2nd - Kontakion of the feast; then "Lord, have mercy" (12) and dismissal. The prayer for the dead "Remember, O Lord" we do not take.
 901: AT MATINS
 902: ##### 4.2.14.5 On "God is the Lord": Troparion of the feast twice, Glory, Both now: the same
 903: ##### 4.2.14.6 Two regular Kathismata with the Sessional Hymn of the feast; then "The Resurrection of Christ" once, Psalm 50 and immediately - Canon
 904: ##### 4.2.14.7 Canons of the feast - 2 [making] 14: 1st - with heirmos on 8, and 2nd - on 6. Katavasia - Heirmos of the 2nd Canon
 905: After the 3rd Ode - Sessional Hymn, after the 6th - Kontakion-Ikos, after the 9th - Exapostilarion of the feast; at the 9th, instead of "More honorable", we sing the heirmos of the feast.
 906: ##### 4.2.14.8 Stichera of the Praises of the feast on 4; after the Great Doxology - Troparion of the feast, Great Dismissal, of Pascha
 907: AT THE HOURS: At all - Troparion and Kontakion of the feast.
 908: #### 4.2.14.1 AT THE LITURGY
 909: Everything - to the feast, only the two first Antiphons - Resurrection, and the third - usual with the Resurrection refrain; also at "O come, let us worship". Instead of "The angel cried" and "Shine, shine" we sing the heirmos of the feast.
 910: IN THE MIDDLE OF THE FEAST OF ### 4.2.14 Mid-Pentecost
 911: except the Sunday of the Samaritan Woman and the Apodosis
 912: We sing everything according to the rubric of the feast of the Sunday of Thomas here, on page 424; regarding troparia, we take them thus:
 913: ##### 4.2.14.1.1 At the end of Vespers and Matins: Troparion of the saint, Glory, Both now: Mid-Pentecost
 914: ##### 4.2.14.1.2 At Compline: Kontakion of Mid-Pentecost only
 915: ##### 4.2.14.1.3 On "God is the Lord": Troparion of Mid-Pentecost twice, Glory: of the saint, Both now: Mid-Pentecost
 916: ##### 4.2.14.1.4 At all Hours: Troparion of Mid-Pentecost, and at the 3rd and 9th - Glory: of the saint; Kontakia: at the 1st and at the 6th - to Mid-Pentecost, and at the 3rd and 9th - to the saint
 917: ##### 4.2.14.1.5 At the Liturgy: Troparion, Glory, Both now: Kontakion of Mid-Pentecost
 918: ### 4.2.15 Sunday of the Samaritan Woman
 919: Fifth from the Resurrection. Tone 4.
 920: Note
 921: The Feast of Mid-Pentecost blocks the service of the Samaritan Woman on Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday of this week, and on the other three days of it, that is after the Apodosis of the feast, the service of the Samaritan Woman is taken again; on this Sunday we sing the service of the Samaritan Woman with the service of Mid-Pentecost.
 922: RUBRIC
 923: #### 4.2.15.1 AT Great Vespers
 924: ##### 4.2.15.1.1 On "Lord, I have cried" - 10 stichera: 4 Sunday, 3 of Mid-Pentecost and 3 of the Samaritan Woman, Glory: of the Samaritan Woman, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the tone (Dogmatikon)
 925: ##### 4.2.15.1.2 At the Aposticha: one Sunday sticheron, then Stichera of Pascha with their verses, only Doxastikon - of the Samaritan Woman
 926: ##### 4.2.15.1.3 After "Now lettest Thou Thy servant depart" - Sunday Troparion, Glory, Both now: Mid-Pentecost
 927: ##### 4.2.15.1.4 Dismissal of Pascha, without the cross
 928: AT COMPLINE: After "It is truly meet" - Kontakion of the Samaritan Woman, Glory, Both now: Kontakion of Mid-Pentecost.
 929: #### 4.2.15.2 AT Great Matins
 930: ##### 4.2.15.2.1 On "God is the Lord": Sunday Troparion twice, Glory, Both now: Mid-Pentecost
 931: ##### 4.2.15.2.2 Kathismata proper and everything else up to the canon - Sunday, as usual, only Gospel - 7th Sunday and "The Resurrection of Christ" (3)
 932: ##### 4.2.15.2.3 Canons 4 [making] 14: Sunday with heirmos on 4, Theotokos of the Triodion on 2, Mid-Pentecost on 4 and of the Samaritan Woman on 4. Katavasia of the Resurrection
 933: After the 3rd Ode - Kontakion-Ikos of Mid-Pentecost and Sessional Hymn of the Samaritan Woman, Glory, Both now: Mid-Pentecost. After the 6th - Kontakion-Ikos of the Samaritan Woman. At the 9th, instead of "More honorable", - "The angel cried" and "Shine, shine"; after the 9th - "Holy is the Lord our God" (3) and Exapostilarion of the Resurrection once, Glory: of the Samaritan Woman, Both now: Mid-Pentecost.
 934: ##### 4.2.15.2.4 Stichera of the Praises - 8: 5 Sunday and 3 of the Samaritan Woman with their two verses; Glory: of the Samaritan Woman, Both now: "Most blessed Art Thou"
 935: ##### 4.2.15.2.5 After the Great Doxology - Sunday Troparion, one of the two
 936: ##### 4.2.15.2.6 Dismissal of Pascha, Glory, Both now: 7th Gospel Sticheron
 937: #### 4.2.15.3 AT THE HOURS
 938: At all: Sunday Troparion, Glory: Mid-Pentecost; Kontakia: at the 1st and 6th - of Mid-Pentecost, and at the 3rd and 9th - of the Samaritan Woman.
 939: #### 4.2.15.4 AT THE LITURGY
 940: ##### 4.2.15.4.1 Antiphons, as every Sunday
 941: ##### 4.2.15.4.2 After the Entrance: Sunday Troparion and of Mid-Pentecost, Glory: Kontakion of the Samaritan Woman, Both now: of Mid-Pentecost. Everything else - only of the Sunday. Communion Hymn - "Receive the Body of Christ" and "Praise the Lord"
 942: MONDAY AND TUESDAY IN THE MIDDLE OF
 943: ### 4.2.14 Mid-Pentecost
 944: We sing the service of Mid-Pentecost and of the Menaion of the saint according to the general rubric of the weekdays of the Week of Thomas here, on page 424; specifically we take the troparia according to the general rubric in the middle of the feast just as we gave before, on page 434.
 945: WEDNESDAY OF THE APODOSIS OF ### 4.2.14 Mid-Pentecost
 946: We sing the whole service only of the feast, as on the day of the feast itself here, on page 434, except the Entrance and readings at Vespers and Epistle and Gospel at the Liturgy, which will be - of the day. The service of the saint of the Menaion we take at Compline.
 947: THURSDAY, FRIDAY AND SATURDAY OF THE SAMARITAN WOMAN
 948: We sing everything according to the rubric of the weekdays of the Paralytic here, on pp. 432-433 [→REF:p432-433].
 949: ### 4.2.16 Sunday of the Man Born Blind
 950: Sixth from the Resurrection. Tone 5.
