 3561: ### 3.9.6 May: Constantine and Helen
 3562: and
 3563: ### 3.9.25 MAY
 3564: Third Finding of the Head of the Forerunner
 3565: The Service of the Holy Kings falls from the Friday after the Sunday of the Paralytic (4th after Pascha) to the Thursday after the Sunday of All Saints. The Service of the Finding falls from the Tuesday after the Sunday of the Samaritan Woman (5th after Pascha) to the Monday after the second Sunday after the Sunday of All Saints. Can fall:
 3566: 
 3567: ##### 3.9.25.1 On one of the weekdays of Pentecost
 3568: - According to the rule of St. George on p. 287-289.
 3569: 
 3570: ##### 3.9.25.2 On the Sunday of the Samaritan Woman and of the Blind Man
 3571: - According to the rule of St. George on p. 284-285.
 3572: 
 3573: ##### 3.9.25.3 On Mid-Pentecost Wednesday
 3574: - According to the rule of St. George on p. 286-287.
 3575: 
 3576: ##### 3.9.25.4 On Wednesday before the Ascension with the Apodosis of the Resurrection
 3577: - According to the rule of the Theologian on p. 293-295.
 3578: 
 3579: ##### 3.9.25.5 On Ascension Thursday
 3580: - According to the rule of the Theologian on p. 295-296.
 3581: 
 3582: ##### 3.9.25.6 On the Sunday of the Holy Fathers
 3583: - According to the rule of the Theologian on p. 296-298.
 3584: 
 3585: ##### 3.9.25.7 On Friday before the Sunday of the Descent with the Apodosis of the Ascension
 3586: - See the rule below, after all 14 cases.
 3587: 
 3588: ##### 3.9.25.8 On the Saturday of Souls before the Sunday of the Descent
 3589: - Transferred to the previous Thursday.
 3590: 
 3591: ##### 3.9.25.9 On the Sunday of the Descent
 3592: - Transferred to the previous Thursday.
 3593: 
 3594: ##### 3.9.25.10 On Monday of Pentecost
 3595: - Transferred to the following Tuesday.
 3596: 
 3597: ##### 3.9.25.11 On the Saturday of All Saints with the Apodosis of the Descent
 3598: - See the rule below, after all 14 cases.
 3599: 
 3600: ##### 3.9.25.12 On the Sunday of All Saints
 3601: - Transferred to the previous Friday.
 3602: 
 3603: ##### 3.9.25.13 On Thursday of the Eucharist
 3604: - According to the general rule of a Saint with Polyeleos in the middle of a feast.
 3605: 
 3606: ##### 3.9.25.14 On the Sunday of the Eucharist (only Finding)
 3607: - Transferred either back, to Sat., or forward, to Mon.
 3608:  
 3609: #### 3.9.25.1 RULE FOR THE 7th and 11th CASES
 3610: 
 3611: CONSTANTINE AND HELEN
 3612: AND
 3613: 
 3614: FINDING OF THE HEAD OF THE FORERUNNER
 3615: 
 3616: IN THE APODOSIS OF THE ASCENSION AND THE DESCENT
 3617: #### 3.9.25.2 AT Great Vespers
 3618: 1.	"Blessed is the man".
 3619: 
 3620: ##### 3.9.25.2.1 At "Lord, I have cried" - 10 stichera: 6 of the Feast and 4 of the Saint, Glory: of the Saint, Both now: of the Feast
 3621: 
 3622: ##### 3.9.25.2.2 Prokeimenon of the day and 3 readings to the Saint
 3623: 
 3624: ##### 3.9.25.2.3 Aposticha of the Feast, only Doxastikon - to the Saint
 3625: 
 3626: ##### 3.9.25.2.4 Troparion of the Saint, Glory, and now: of the Feast
 3627: #### 3.9.25.3 AT Great Matins
 3628: 
 3629: ##### 3.9.25.3.1 At "God is the Lord": Troparion of the Feast twice, Glory: to the Saint, Both now: of the Feast
 3630: 
 3631: ##### 3.9.25.3.2 First two sessional hymns of the Feast, after the Polyeleos with "Great Doxology" - two sessional hymns of the Saint, then Glory: his Post-Polyeleos Sessional hymn, Both now: of the Feast. Everything else up to the canon - to the Saint
 3632: 
 3633: ##### 3.9.25.3.3 Canons 3 making 14: first of the Feast with heirmos on 6, of the Saint on 4 and second of the Feast on 4. Sequential Katavasia. After the 3rd ode - Kontakion-Ikos and Sessional hymn of the Saint, Glory, and now: of the Feast; after the 6th - Kontakion-Ikos of the Feast; at the 9th "More honorable" we do not sing, but we sing the refrain of the Feast; to the troparia of the Saint we sing his usual refrain; after the 9th - Exapostilarion of the Feast, Glory: to the Saint, Both now: of the Feast
 3634: 
 3635: ##### 3.9.25.3.4 Stichera of the Praises - 6: 3 of the Feast and 3 of the Saint, with two of his refrains; Glory: of the Saint, Both now: of the Feast
 3636: 
 3637: ##### 3.9.25.3.5 After the Great Doxology - Troparion of the Saint, Glory, and now: of the Feast
 3638: AT THE HOURS: On all: Troparion of the Feast, Glory: to the Saint. Kontakion: on the 1st and 6th - of the Feast; on the 3rd and 9th - of the Saint.
 3639: 
 3640: #### 3.9.25.4 AT THE LITURGY
 3641: 
 3642: ##### 3.9.25.4.1 Troparion of the Feast and of the Saint, Glory: Kontakion of the Saint, Both now: of the Feast
 3643: 
 3644: ##### 3.9.25.4.2 Prokeimenon, Alleluia and Communion Hymn of the Feast and of the Saint. Apostle-Gospel of the day and of the Saint
 3645:  
 3646: ## 3.10 June
 3647: ### 3.10.1 June: Holy Apostles Bartholomew and Barnabas
 3648: Have 11 following cases:
 3649: 
 3650: ##### 3.10.1.1 On one of the weekdays of Pentecost
 3651: - According to the rule of St. George, here on p. 287-289.
 3652: 
 3653: ##### 3.10.1.2 On Friday of the Apodosis of the Ascension
 3654: - According to the rule of Constantine and Helen, here on p. 300-301.
 3655: 
 3656: ##### 3.10.1.3 On Saturday of Pentecost (of Souls)
 3657: - Transferred to the previous Thursday.
 3658: 
 3659: ##### 3.10.1.4 On the Sunday of Pentecost
 3660: - Transferred to the previous Thursday.
 3661: 
 3662: ##### 3.10.1.5 On Monday of Pentecost
 3663: - Transferred to the following Tuesday.
 3664: 
 3665: ##### 3.10.1.6 On Saturday of the Apodosis of Pentecost
 3666: - According to the rule of Constantine and Helen, here on p. 300-301.
 3667: 
 3668: ##### 3.10.1.7 On the Sunday of All Saints
 3669: - Transferred back, to Friday.
 3670: 
 3671: ##### 3.10.1.8 On Thursday of the Eucharist
 3672: - According to the general rule of a Saint with Polyeleos in the middle of a feast.
 3673: 
 3674: ##### 3.10.1.9 On the Sunday of the Eucharist
 3675: - Transferred back, to Saturday, or forward, to Monday.
 3676: 
 3677: ##### 3.10.1.10 On the Apodosis of the Feast of the Eucharist
 3678: - According to the rule of Constantine and the Finding, when they fall on the Apodosis of the Ascension and Pentecost, here on p. 300-301.
 3679: 
 3680: ##### 3.10.1.11 On the Co-suffering of the Most Holy Theotokos
 3681: - According to the rule of the Theologian, when it falls on the Ascension, here on p. 295-296[^439], however, without All-Night Vigil.
 3682: ### 3.10.2 June: Nativity of Saint John the Baptist
 3683: and
 3684: ### 3.10.3 June: The Holy Pre-eminent Apostles Peter and Paul
 3685: These two feasts, and also the Beheading of the Precious Head of the Forerunner, have the general rule of a Saint with All-Night Vigil, however, they exceed the Saint with All-Night Vigil in the following points:
 3686: 
 3687: ##### 3.10.3.1 At Matins, before their canon, the Canon to the Theotokos is not taken, but only their two canons on 14, heirmos of the first canon - twice, then troparia of both canons on 12, that is of one on 6 and of the other on 6
 3688: 
 3689: ##### 3.10.3.2 At the Liturgy the Apostle-Gospel is read only of the Saint, and of the day is read on the previous day just as on Feasts of the Lord and of the Theotokos
 3690: 
 3691: ##### 3.10.3.3 Their service is not celebrated in one day, but in two; however, on the second day their service - is of the daily type and combined with the service of the Octoechos and of the sequential saint so, that the Octoechos takes the first place, the Forerunner or the Chiefs [of the Apostles] - the second, according to the rule of a Saint on 4, and the sequential saint - the third. It is also proper to take their Troparion and Kontakion of the day at the Hours and at the Liturgy
 3692: #### 3.10.3.1 RULE FOR 24 AND 29 JUNE
 3693: if they fall with the Feast of the Eucharist
 3694: and with the Co-suffering of the Most Holy Theotokos[^440] 
 3695: In relation to the Feast of the Eucharist these saints have three cases:
 3696: 
 3697: ##### 3.10.3.1.1 In the middle of the Feast of the Eucharist
 3698: 
 3699: ##### 3.10.3.1.2 On Sunday, to which the Feast of the Eucharist is transferred
 3700: 
 3701: ##### 3.10.3.1.3 On the Apodosis of the Feast of the Eucharist
 3702: In the first case, that is in the middle of the feast, they are subject to the general rule of a Saint with All-Night Vigil in the middle of a feast, likewise also on Thursday of the Feast, for the Service of the Feast with All-Night Vigil is transferred to Sunday.
 3703: In the second case, that is on the Sunday of the Eucharist, by the decision of the Lviv Synod, the Sunday service is not taken and in our opinion (since there is no rule) one should sing the service of the Feast with the service of the Forerunner or of the Chiefs, according to the rule of the Theologian on 8 May, if it falls on the Ascension, here on p. 295-296.
 3704: In the third case, that is on the Apodosis of the Eucharist, subject to the rule of the Finding of the Head of the Forerunner on 25 May, when it falls on the Apodosis of the Ascension, here on p. 300-301. However, since in this case there will be All-Night Vigil, which the Finding does not have, here, at Small Vespers, after the stichera at "Lord, I have cried" and at the Aposticha is sung Both now: stichera of the Feast, and after the Troparion of the Saints - Glory, and now: Troparion of the Feast; likewise also at the Litya - stichera of the saints with Both now: of the Feast; at the blessing of loaves: Troparion of the Saints twice and "Rejoice, O Virgin Theotokos" once[^441].
 3705: In relation to the Feast of the Co-suffering, with which these saints can coincide (for the rule has nothing), they are subject to the rule of the Theologian on 8 May, when he falls on the Feast of the Ascension, here on p. 295-296. However, since the Co-suffering does not have All-Night Vigil, at Small Vespers everything is sung only to the Saint, and at Great Matins all sessional hymns will be to the Saint, Glory, and now: of the Feast. Everything else up to the canon - only to the Saints. Canon of the Feast with heirmos on 6 and to the Saints on 8. If 25 and 30 June, that is the second day of the Feast of these Saints, falls with the Co-suffering of the Most Holy Theotokos, then their service is taken at Compline. 
 3706: 
 3707: ## 3.11 July
 3708: ### 3.11.1 July: Deposition of the Precious Robe of the Most Holy Theotokos
 3709: Polyeleos - at choice[^442].
 3710: 
 3711: ##### 3.11.1.1 On weekdays
 3712: If this service is not sung with Polyeleos, then it has the appearance of a daily [service] with stichera at "The Praises" and with the Great Doxology, however, on weekdays it displaces the service of the Octoechos. If it be with Polyeleos, then Vespers and Matins - of Great type.
 3713: 
 3714: ##### 3.11.1.2 On Sunday
 3715: For the case of Sunday church books do not give a rule. We think that at Vespers, if there be no Polyeleos, at "Lord, I have cried" there should be 6 Resurrectional stichera and 4 of the Theotokos[^443]. If there be Polyeleos, then 4 Resurrectional and 6 of the Theotokos, Glory: of the Theotokos, Both now: Dogmatikon of the tone. At the Aposticha - Glory, and now: of the Robe. Troparia at the end of Vespers and at "God is the Lord" we end with the Troparion of the Robe, and at the Liturgy - with the Kontakion of the Robe.
 3716: At Compline, after "It is truly meet" - Kontakion of the Robe.
 3717: At Great Matins, if there be Polyeleos, from the Gradual to the canon everything only Resurrectional is sung, as usual. Everything else at Matins, at the Hours and at the Liturgy is sung according to the general rule of a feast of the Theotokos on Sunday. If there be no Polyeleos, then Sessional hymns of the Robe, of the Polyeleos and "Great Doxology" we do not sing. Everything else we sing according to the general rule of a feast of the Theotokos.
 3718: 
 3719: #### 3.11.1.1 RULE OF THE DEPOSITION OF THE PRECIOUS ROBE
 3720: 
 3721: ON THE CO-SUFFERING OF THE MOST HOLY THEOTOKOS 
 3722: In church books there is no rule for this case. However, we think that then the Service of the Deposition should be transferred to the following Saturday, and the Service of the sequential saint of Saturday sung at Compline.
 3723: ### 3.11.2 July: Holy Fathers of the first six ecumenical councils
 3724: Everything according to the rule of the Holy Fathers of the Seventh Ecumenical Council 11 October, here on p. 130-131.
 3725: ### 3.11.3 July: Holy Prophet Elias
 3726: The Service of the Prophet, by the decree of the Lviv Synod, must be celebrated with All-Night Vigil and from a weekday be transferred to Sunday.
 3727: Everything - according to the general rule of a Saint with All-Night Vigil on Sunday[^445].
 3728: Note: If the Sunday, to which the Service of the Prophet is transferred falls on 25 July, when there will be Polyeleos, it should be transferred to the previous Sunday.
 3729: ### 3.11.4 July: Dormition of St. Anne, mother of the Most Holy Theotokos
 3730: and memory of the holy women Olympias and Eupraxia
 3731: Note
 3732: Although even in ancient typikons the Service of St. Anne is given of small type with the service of the Octoechos and of the holy women[^446], however, with time it was honored with us with Polyeleos, and by the decision and decree of the Synod of Zamość, even with All-Night Vigil[^447]  (although with us there is none, but only Polyeleos); and with the Greeks - Great Vespers with stichera at the Litya, and also Great Matins, from the canon and further[^448].
 3733: "The canon of the holy women we take at Compline, when the Superior decides"[^449].
 3734: 
 3735: #### 3.11.4.1 RULE
 3736: Everything - according to the general rule of a Saint with Polyeleos, whether on Sunday, or on weekdays. However, stichera and troparia we do not end with Theotokia of the Octoechos, but of the Saint, as if Theotokia, only on Sunday at "Lord, I have cried" we end with the Dogmatikon of the tone, and the Praises - with the Theotokion "Most blessed Art Thou".
 3737: 
 3738:  
 3739: ### 3.11.5 July: Forefeast of the Procession of the Precious Cross
 3740: and of the holy and righteous Eudocimus
 3741: Notes
 3742: 
 3743: ##### 3.11.5.1 The Feast of the Procession of the Precious Wood on 1 August has a Forefeast, which is - today, that is 31 July, but it has no Afterfeast
 3744: 
 3745: ##### 3.11.5.2 Although it has a Forefeast, however, of small type, that is without Polyeleos, and the service of the Cross does not exclude the service of the sequential saint, nor of the Octoechos, neither in the Forefeast, nor on the Feast, nor on Sunday, nor on a weekday
 3746: 
 3747: ##### 3.11.5.3 In the Forefeast and on the Feast the first place is occupied by the service of the Octoechos, the second - of the Cross, the third - of the Saint
 3748: 
 3749: ##### 3.11.5.4 The service of the Forefeast has the composition of a service of a Saint on 4 and the service of St. Eudocimus also has the appearance of a Saint on 4, since these two services are combined with the service of the Octoechos both on weekdays, and on Sunday, then the order on weekdays will be according to the general rule of two saints, falling with the Octoechos on weekdays, only the stichera at "Lord, I have cried" and at the Aposticha we end with the stichera of the Forefeast, except Friday evening, when the stichera at "Lord, I have cried" we end with the 1st Theotokion of the tone. On Sunday the order will be according to the general rule of a Forefeast with one Saint without Polyeleos with Octoechos on Sunday. Likewise also troparia we do not end with the usual Theotokion, but with the Troparion of the Forefeast, according to the general rule of a Forefeast. Therefore, there will be:
 3750: 
 3751: #### 3.11.5.1 RULE OF THE FOREFEAST
 3752: 
 3753: OF THE PROCESSION OF THE PRECIOUS CROSS
 3754: 
 3755: ##### 3.11.5.1.1 On weekdays
 3756:

 3758:

 3760: 
 3761: ##### 3.11.5.1.3 At the Aposticha: stichera of the Octoechos, Glory, and now: of the Cross

After the 3rd ode - Sessional hymn of the Saint, Glory, and now: of the Cross[^452]; after the 6th - Kontakion-Ikos of the Saint, after the 9th - Exapostilarion of the Octoechos, Glory: of the Saint, Both now: of the Cross

 3777: AT THE HOURS AND AT THE LITURGY: Everything - according to the general rule of the Forefeast with a Saint without Polyeleos.
 3778: 
 3779: #### 3.11.5.2 AT THE LITURGY
 3780: 
 3781: ##### 3.11.5.2.1 Troparia: of the Cross, of the Martyrs and Glory, and now: of the Cross
 3782: 
 3783: ##### 3.11.5.2.2 Prokeimenon of the Cross and of the Martyrs
 3784: 
 3785: ##### 3.11.5.2.3 Apostle and Gospel of the Cross and of the Martyrs
 3786: 
 3787: ##### 3.11.5.2.4 Communion Hymn "The light of Thy countenance" ("Znamenovasya") and of the Martyrs "Rejoice in the Lord" ("Raduitesya")
 3788: After the Dismissal of the Liturgy, where the custom exists, the joint blessing of water and herbs takes place, during which we sing the troparia of the Cross, of the Martyrs and of the Theotokos, then the canon of the Cross, of the Martyrs and the canon for the blessing of water[^453].
 3789: 
 3790: ##### 3.11.5.2.5 On Sunday
 3791: Everything - according to the general rule of the Forefeast with a Saint without Polyeleos on Sunday, here on p. 81-83; only at the Praises all stichera - of the Octoechos, without the Forefeast. The Bringing Out of the Cross, its veneration and the blessing of water, according to the above-given rule for weekdays, as on Sunday[^451].
 3792:  
 3793: ## 3.12 August
 3794: 
 3795: ### 3.12.1 August: Procession of the Wood of the Precious Cross
 3796: and memory of the Holy Martyrs Maccabees
 3797: Note
 3798: The Procession of the Precious Cross, which took place once in Constantinople from the imperial palace to the most beautiful church of Sophia, we depict now by the bringing out of the Precious Cross in the evening first from the sacristy to the Holy Table, and then, on the day of 1 August, from the Holy Table to the tetrapod, at Matins during the Doxology, when the Veneration also takes place, according to the rule of 14 September, on p. 120, except the Exaltation, which happens only on 14 September on the Exaltation of the Precious Cross, and here there will be none. Besides this, in Slavic books on this day also the Lesser Blessing of Water is prescribed either at Matins immediately before the Veneration, or later, at another time of the day. In some places also the blessing of herbs takes place, as on the Dormition of the Most Holy Theotokos[^454].
 3799: 
 3800: #### 3.12.1.1 RULE
 3801: 
 3802: ##### 3.12.1.1.1 On weekdays
 3803: Everything, as in the Forefeast 31. VII, here on p. 308-309, however:
 3804: 
 3805: ##### 3.12.1.1.2 After the Dismissal of Vespers the Bringing Out of the Precious Cross from the sacristy to the Holy Table takes place, according to the rule of 14 September, here on p. 121-122
 3806: 
 3807: ##### 3.12.1.1.3 At Matins: Canon of the Octoechos on 4, of the Cross on 6 and of the Saints on 4. Katavasia after each ode - sequential "The Cross having been traced" (14 September). After the 3rd ode - Kontakion-Ikos and Sessional hymn of the Saints, only Both now: of the Cross; after the 6th - Kontakion-Ikos of the Cross; after the 9th - Exapostilarion of the Octoechos, Glory: of the Saints, Both now: of the Cross
 3808: 
 3809: ##### 3.12.1.1.4 Stichera of the Praises - 6: 3 of the Cross and 3 of the Saints, Glory: of the Saints, Both now: of the Cross
 3810: 
 3811: ##### 3.12.1.1.5 During the singing of the Praises the Priest, having vested in all sacred vestments (of violet color)[^455]  and having exclaimed before the steps of the Holy Table: "Glory to Thee, Who Hast shown us the light", and having censed the precious Cross, carries it out around the Holy Table through the northern doors before the Holy Doors, and after the end of the Great Doxology with the Trisagion, exclaims: "Wisdom, attend", goes before the tetrapod and, having placed the precious Cross on it, when the Choir sings the Troparion "Save, O Lord", censes it from four sides and venerates the precious Cross, everything exactly as on 14 September, here on p. 122-127
 3812: 
 3813: ##### 3.12.1.1.6 The Blessing of Water, if it be outside Matins, is celebrated whole just as you have in the Trebnik. If it be at Matins, then after the singing of the Doxology and the Troparion "Save, O Lord", that is immediately before the Veneration, in the rite of the Blessing of Water the beginning and the end is not taken, but immediately after the Troparion "Save, O Lord" begins "That rejoice" ("Yezhe raduisya") and ends with the stichera "O Most Holy Lady, receive", not taking the litany "Have mercy on us, O God" and the rest
 3814: 
 3815: ##### 3.12.1.1.7 The Blessing of Herbs, if there be any, usually takes place at the Liturgy after the Prayer behind the Ambo just as on the Dormition of the Most Holy Theotokos
 3816: 
 3817: ##### 3.12.1.1.8 On Sunday
 3818: Everything - according to the general rule of the Afterfeast with a Saint without Polyeleos on Sunday, here on p. 93-96, only:
 3819: 
 3820: ##### 3.12.1.1.9 On Saturday evening, after the Dismissal of Vespers the Bringing Out of the Precious Cross from the sacristy to the Holy Table takes place, and at Matins, during the Great Doxology, from the Holy Table to the tetrapod, according to the rule of 14 September. However, after the exclamation "Wisdom, attend", instead of the Troparion "Save, O Lord", we sing the Resurrectional Troparion, one of the two usual ones, at which the Priest should cense the Precious Cross from four sides and immediately after this perform the veneration of the Precious Cross, singing the Troparion "Before Thy Cross we bow down", or before the veneration perform also the rite of the Blessing of Water, according to the rule given here for weekdays, no. 5
 3821: 
 3822: ##### 3.12.1.1.10 At the Liturgy: the entire service is taken first of the Sunday, and then - of the Cross. The Service of the Saints, since it is without Polyeleos, is not taken. If someone would prefer to take it too, then Prokeimena, Alleluia and Communion Hymns will be only two: to the Cross and to the Saints, and Apostle-Gospels - three: sequential, of the Cross and of the Saints[^456]
 3823: ### 3.12.2 August: Transfiguration of the Lord
 3824: Everything - according to the general rule of a Feast of the Lord, only after the Prayer behind the Ambo[^457], as Slavic typikons give, or after the Dismissal of the Liturgy, as the Peremyshl Trebnik gives, the Priest blesses on the tetrapod the first grapes (and since we have no grapes, then the first fruits) with one prayer, given in the Menaion, or with three, given in our Trebnik[^458], with censing and sprinkling them with holy water at the end.
 3825: Note: If this blessing takes place after the Prayer behind the Ambo, then we think that it is not necessary to sing before that the Usual Beginning and everything else with "Our Father", Psalm 60, Troparion and Kontakion of the Feast[^459], but immediately "Let us pray to the Lord" and the prayer, for the Menaion prescribes only the prayer.
 3826: ### 3.12.3 August: Dormition of the Most Holy Theotokos
 3827: Everything - according to the general rule of feasts of the Theotokos, only where the custom exists, then after the Prayer behind the Ambo, or after the Dismissal of the Liturgy, the Blessing of Herbs takes place, according to the above-given rule for the blessing of fruits on 6 August, here before.
 3828: ### 3.12.4 August: Image Not-Made-By-Hands
 3829: and of the Holy Martyr Diomedes
 3830: Notes
 3831: 
 3832: ##### 3.12.4.1 The Service of the Holy Martyr is sung at Compline, and two services remain, that is of the Dormition and of the Image
 3833: 
 3834: ##### 3.12.4.2 Although the service of the Image, as of the Lord, is greater than of the Theotokos, however, here the Theotokos one takes the first place
 3835: 
 3836: ##### 3.12.4.3 The Service of the Image, according to the rule of our and Russian menaia, is on 6 and is celebrated according to the general rule of a Saint without Polyeleos on 6, with Praises and Great Doxology. It has also in the canon after each ode the sequential katavasia and, in Slavic books[^460], a separate Great Dismissal[^461]
 3837: 
 3838: ##### 3.12.4.4 Although the Service of the Image - is without Polyeleos, nevertheless, at the Liturgy we do not omit it, as other services of Saints without Polyeleos of feasts of the Lord and of the Theotokos

Katavasia after each ode - Kontakion-Ikos of the Dormition and Sessional hymn of the Image, Glory, and now: of the Dormition; after the 6th - Kontakion-Ikos of the Image, after the 9th - Exapostilarion of the Image, Glory, and now: of the Dormition

 3906:

 3908:

 3912:  
 3913: ### 3.12.5 August: Beheading of the Precious Head of St. John the Baptist
 3914: Everything - according to the rule of 24 June, however, by the decision of the Lviv Synod, must be transferred from a weekday to Sunday with All-Night Vigil. It is usually transferred to the following Sunday, only if the following Sunday falls on 1 September, then the service is transferred to the previous Sunday, so as not to coincide with three other services, that is Resurrectional, of the Indiction and of St. Simeon[^464]. The fast of the Beheading we do not transfer to Sunday, but keep on the very day of the feast[^465].
 3915: ### 3.12.6 August: Deposition of the Sash of the Most Holy Theotokos
 3916: Everything - according to the rule of the Deposition of the Robe 2. VII, here on p. 305-306.

 764: HOURS
 765: 
 766: OF THE EVE OF THE NATIVITY OF CHRIST AND THEOPHANY
 767: Notes
 768: 
 769: ##### 3.4.7.1 The Lviv Synod orders pastors to celebrate these Hours together with the Typika in church, in violet vestments, in view of the fast[^308], in bright vestments it is celebrated before Theophany only when the Hours from Saturday or Sunday are transferred back, to Friday, for then there is no fast, but it will be a general dispensation
 770: 
 771: ##### 3.4.7.2 Now we sing all the Hours adding "The Typika" (Typika); and therefore we begin the Hours 3rd, 6th and 9th from "O come, let us worship", and we make the dismissal only at the end of "The Typika"
 772: 
 773: ##### 3.4.7.3 These Hours are celebrated in the morning, earlier or later, at the decision of the Superior; according to the custom of the arch-cathedral church - at 9 o'clock before noon[^309], so that there would be a certain distance between the Hours and the Liturgy, which according to the custom of the same church begins at 11 o'clock. If the Hours begin earlier, then the Liturgy can also begin earlier, but since it is celebrated with Vespers, it should begin around 10 o'clock, as the Lviv Synod decreed about Vespers with the Presanctified[^310]
 774: 
 775: ##### 3.4.7.4 The composition and form of the Great Hours is the same as of the usual Hours, with the exception of three troparia and three readings, given after the Theotokion "What shall we call Thee" at the 1st Hour and after the corresponding ones at the other Hours. Regarding the essence, the Royal Hours differ from the usual ones also by the tripalm, which at the Royal Hours is special, appropriate to the given feast[^311]
 776: 
 777: ##### 3.4.7.5 In the temple, before the Holy Doors, opposite the people, two analogia are placed, on the first of which the Gospel is placed; the second, slightly lower, - opposite the Holy Doors, from which the Paremia and Apostle are to be read. Where there is no analogion for the Gospel, it lies on the Holy Table and is brought out by the Priest through the Holy Doors only for reading, and is supported by servers[^312]
 778: 
 779: ##### 3.4.7.6 The Royal Hours are celebrated with the Holy Doors closed, which are opened only for the reading of the Gospel
 780: 
 781: ##### 3.4.7.7 Candles on the altar are lit only for the reading of the Gospel
 782: 
 783: #### 3.4.7.1 RULE
 784: At the appointed time the Priest enters the temple and, having approached the Holy Table and having bowed low, kisses the Gospel, marks four Gospel readings and, having bowed again, goes out to the sacristy; puts on an epitrachelion, goes out before the closed Holy Doors, makes a low bow to the Holy Mysteries and begins the usual: "Blessed is our God". Choir: "Amen", also "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee", "O Heavenly King" and everything else, as usual, up to "O come, let us worship" inclusive[^320][^313]. At the second "O come, let us worship" the Priest, having bowed low, enters the sanctuary and, while the choirs sing the tripalm, reads it sitting in his place.
 785: When, after the Troparion of the Forefeast "Once Mary was registered", the Theotokion is also read, the choirs sing three stichera idiomesa[^314]  on 6, that is twice each. The first stichera both the first and the second time is sung without a refrain; the second - the first time with a separate refrain, and the second - with another separate refrain; the third - the first time with the refrain "Glory", and the second - with the refrain "Both now". All four above-mentioned refrains at all Hours - are the same. At the 9th Hour the third stichera is taken three times, that is the first time it is read loudly and piously by the canonarch in the middle of the church, without a refrain, then the second time - by one choir with the refrain "Glory", and the third - by the other with the refrain "Both now"[^315].
 786: After the singing of the three stichera there will be three readings: the first - of the Prophecy with a Prokeimenon, the second - of the Apostle without a Prokeimenon and without Alleluia, the third - of the Gospel, beginning it from "Wisdom, attend!", "Let us hear". All this is accompanied by the following actions: when the stichera end, the Priest puts on a phelonion and, having gone out before the steps of the altar and having bowed, opens the Holy Doors and exclaims: "Let us attend! Peace be unto all!" (blessing the people), "Wisdom! Let us attend!". The choirs sing the Prokeimenon. After its conclusion the Priest, having exclaimed before the title of the Prophecy "Wisdom!" and before the reading "Let us attend!", waits before the steps of the altar for the end of the reading of the Prophecy and, after its conclusion, having exclaimed "Wisdom!" and "Let us attend!" before the reading of the Apostle, as usual, puts incense into the censer with the short prayer "Incense we offer to Thee" and, having blessed the incense with the words "Blessed is our God", censes everything as usual, that is the Holy Table from four sides, the iconostasis, the choirs and the people[^316]. At the end of the Apostle, and together with it the censing, the candle-bearers go out before the analogion, and the Priest approaches the Holy Table and, having bowed, takes the Holy Gospel and, having placed it on the analogion, begins to sing the Gospel from "Wisdom, attend". After the singing of the Gospel the Priest, having kissed the beginning of the reading, leaves it there, closes the Holy Doors and, having bowed low to the Holy Mysteries, goes out to the sacristy, takes off the phelonion, goes out through the side doors before the Holy Doors for "Thou Who at all times" and remains there until the end of the Hour.
 787: Note: Since we sing all the Hours together, the prayer of blessing the incense should be said only at the 1st Hour, at the others - only "Blessed is our God" just as at Great Vespers with All-Night Vigil.
 788: If there be deacons, they put on dalmatics with an orarion before the beginning of the 1st Hour and remain vested until the end of the Typika. At the Prokeimenon, together with the Priest, they go before the steps of the altar and, having bowed low all together to the Holy Mysteries, open the Holy Doors. The right Deacon exclaims: "Let us attend!", and the left, after the giving of peace by the Priest: "Wisdom! Let us attend!". Also before the first and second reading - the right: "Wisdom!", and the left: "Let us attend!" and they cense everything as usual, as at the beginning of the Liturgy. At the end of the Apostle, and together with it the censing, both deacons stand with the Priest before the steps of the altar and, having bowed all three together to the Holy Mysteries, go out from the sanctuary: the Priest with the Gospel through the middle [doors], and the deacons, having swapped their sides, through the side doors to the analogion. The right Deacon exclaims: "Wisdom, attend!", "Let us hear", the Priest: "The reading from the Holy Gospel according to (Name)", and the left deacon: "Let us attend!". The Priest sings the Gospel. Having finished, the Priest kisses the beginning of the reading, also the right deacon, and after him the left. Having bowed low, the deacons return through their doors to the sanctuary and, together with the Priest, close the Holy Doors. Having bowed low all three together to the Holy Mysteries, they withdraw: the deacons to their places, and the Priest before the iconostasis for "Thou Who at all times".
 789: If the hierarch or other sacred dignitaries be present in the church, the deacons should cense them before the choirs, and neither the Priest nor the deacons should kiss the Gospel before the hierarch and sacred dignitaries, and therefore both deacons together carry the open Gospel to them for kissing, also to the Priest standing in the Holy Doors and, when he kisses it, the deacons themselves kiss [it], after which they place it on the analogion and, having bowed low to the Holy Mysteries, return, each through his doors, to the sanctuary.
 790: Question: When the Royal Hours are transferred from Sunday or Saturday back, to Friday, should one take on them the Troparion of the Eve or of the Forefeast, 22 or 23 December?
 791: Answer: The Typikon mentions the Troparion and Kontakion of the Eve, therefore we think that one should take [those] of the Eve. If someone thinks that this will not be good and takes one Troparion for two days, that is on the Eve and before the Eve, let him consider that the Troparion of the Forefeast is also taken the same on two different days of the Forefeast.
 792: THE TYPIKA (Typika)
 793: After the concluding prayer of the 9th Hour we immediately read the Typika just as in the Horologion, however, without the introductory verse that is before the first psalm, without the stichera on the "Beatitudes", without the Apostle-Gospel; also, if there be Liturgy, then also without the "Creed" and without "Blessed be the name of the Lord", and without the following 33rd Psalm, for all this will be taken at the Liturgy. When the Royal Hours are transferred back, to Friday, then since then there will be no Liturgy, here both the "Creed" and "Blessed be the name of the Lord" with the 33rd Psalm is read. Instead of the kontakia of the temple, of the day and others, one Kontakion of the Eve is taken. Here is the detailed rule for you.
 794: 
 795: DETAILED RULE
 796: 
 797: ##### 3.4.7.1.1 After the concluding prayer of the 9th Hour the Priest, having bowed before the Holy Doors, enters the sanctuary and sits in his place
 798: 
 799: ##### 3.4.7.1.2 The choirs read: Psalm 102 "Bless the Lord, O my soul" and Psalm 145 "Praise the Lord, O my soul", "Glory, Both now", "Only-begotten Son"
 800: 
 801: ##### 3.4.7.1.3 The Beatitudes: "In Thy kingdom... great in heaven", "Glory, Both now"
 802: 4.	"Remember us, O Lord" (3).
 803: 5.	"The heavenly choir", verse "Come unto Him", "The heavenly choir", Glory: "The Choir of holy angels", Both now: "Remit, pardon" (when there is no Liturgy, then Both now: "The Creed", also "Remit, forgive").
 804: 6.	"Our Father", Kontakion of the Eve once and "Lord, have mercy" (12).
 805: 
 806: ##### 3.4.7.1.4 The Priest goes out before the Holy Doors in an epitrachelion, reads the prayer "O All-Holy Trinity" (if there be Liturgy, then the Choir immediately: "It is truly meet" and the rest; if not, then before "It is truly meet" the Choir sings: "Blessed be the name of the Lord" (3) and Psalm "I will bless the Lord"[^418], and the Priest then waits before the Holy Doors until the end)
 807: 
 808: ##### 3.4.7.1.5 Choir: "It is truly meet" with "More honorable than the Cherubim"
 809: Priest: "Glory to Thee, O Christ God".
 810: Choir: "Glory, Both now", "Lord, have mercy" (3), "Master, bless".
 811: Priest to the people - dismissal of the day[^317].
 812: Note: If the Eve of the Nativity of Christ falls on a Saturday or on a Sunday, then the Liturgy of Chrysostom in the arch-cathedral church begins at 08.00 hours, and on the ### 3.5.3 Eve of Theophany - at 08.30 hours.
 813: Saturday before the Nativity of Christ
 814: If it falls on the Eve, see the rule for the Liturgy here on p. 154.
 815: Sunday before the Nativity of Christ
 816: If it falls on the Eve, see the rule here on p. 158-159.
 817:  
 818: ### 3.4.8 December: Nativity of our Lord Jesus Christ
 819: Note
 820: The service of the very day of the feast of the Nativity of Christ (as also of Theophany) departs from the general rules of a Feast of the Lord in the following points:
 821: 
 822: ##### 3.4.8.1 Its Vespers on the Eve is combined with the Service of Basil, if the Eve falls on one of the first five weekdays, starting from Monday
 823: 
 824: ##### 3.4.8.2 On this feast two Vespers are not celebrated: one Small at its proper time, and the second Great at the All-Night Vigil with Matins, as on other feasts, but one, Great, either with the Service of Basil, if the Eve falls on one of the five fast days of the week, or separately at its proper time, if it falls on Saturday or Sunday. All-Night Vigil is served with Great Compline
 825: 
 826: ##### 3.4.8.3 Vespers of this feast will be either with the Service of Basil, or separately, as on Saturday or on Sunday. It is never served completely, but, if it be with the Service, only until the end of the readings, after which the Small Litany is exclaimed and the exclamation of the Trisagion; and from here, according to the order, the Service of Basil. If it be separately, then only until the end of the litany "Let us complete", that is until the end of its second exclamation ("For Thine is the kingdom"), because the Aposticha and everything else is taken at the All-Night Vigil after the Litya
 827: 
 828: ##### 3.4.8.4 Vespers has not only 3 readings, as on other feasts, but 8 (on Theophany - 11); therefore, after the first three and after the second three readings, it has a separate troparion with its verses
 829: 
 830: ##### 3.4.8.5 Compline is served only until the end of "Glory to God in the highest" and immediately the Litya begins with the blessing of loaves and everything else, as at the All-Night Vigil with Vespers
 831: 
 832: ##### 3.4.8.6 Theophany has the Great Blessing of Water directly after Vespers; also, according to our custom, more solemnly - on the very day of the feast, after the Prayer behind the Ambo
 833: 
 834: ##### 3.4.8.7 On the Eve of the Nativity of Christ and Theophany, when there is to be the Service of Basil with Vespers, the Lviv Synod forbids read services. If several priests wish to serve, it orders them to sing only one service in the cathedral (Title IV, chap. I, part 5)
 835: 
 836: ##### 3.4.8.8 In the arch-cathedral church Vespers with the Service of Basil begins at 10.30. If the Eve falls on Saturday or on Sunday, then the Service of Chrysostom without Vespers will be at 08.30, and Vespers separately begins at 11.00, in order to hasten the Holy Supper, which according to the typikon should begin later, that is at 3 o'clock in the afternoon (current 1 o'clock after noon) on the Eve of the Nativity, and on the ### 3.5.3 Eve of Theophany - in the evening hours, that is at the usual time. All-Night Vigil with Compline - at the usual time[^318]. Now we will give three detailed rules: one - for the case of Vespers with the Service of Basil, one - for the case of Vespers which is celebrated separately, without the Service, and one - for the All-Night Vigil with Great Compline
 837: 
 838: #### 3.4.8.1 RULE
 839: 
 840: ##### 3.4.8.1.1 VESPERS WITH THE SERVICE OF BASIL
 841: with the Eve on Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday
 842: 
 843: ##### 3.4.8.1.2 From the beginning to "Blessed is the Kingdom" everything is exactly as usual at the Service without Vespers[^319]
 844: 
 845: ##### 3.4.8.1.3 After "Blessed is the Kingdom", immediately after "Amen" - "O Heavenly King" and the rest with the Trisagion, as usual, up to "O come, let us worship" inclusive
 846: 
 847: ##### 3.4.8.1.4 At the introductory Psalm the Priest, standing near the Holy Table, reads with uncovered head the usual evening prayers and afterwards from there exclaims the litany "In peace let us pray to the Lord". If there be also a Deacon, then he goes out at this litany before the Holy Doors
 848: 
 849: ##### 3.4.8.1.5 The Kathisma "Blessed is the man" will not be (for it is taken only on Saturday evening for Sunday or on Sunday evening for Monday), nor will there be a Small Litany, but immediately - "Lord, I have cried" with censing, as usual
 850: 
 851: ##### 3.4.8.1.6 At "Lord, I have cried" - 8 stichera, Glory, Both now: Stichera from the Heirmologion, if there be none, then according to the tone of the idiomesa
 852: 
 853: ##### 3.4.8.1.7 Entrance with the Gospel, with the usual prayer of the Entrance. If there be deacons, then the first of them, who is to the right of the Priest, carries the Gospel, and the second goes before him with the censer; and they do in this everything as at the Entrance with the Gospel at the Liturgy
 854: 
 855: ##### 3.4.8.1.8 Prokeimenon of the day from the Horologion, only on Friday evening for Saturday there will be the Great Prokeimenon of the Feast, given for the very day of the Feast at Vespers on 26 December. After the singing before the steps of the altar "Let us attend! Peace be unto all!", "Wisdom, let us attend!" the Priest withdraws behind the Holy Table and sits there during the readings in his place. The deacons, if there be [any], remain at the Holy Doors and from here exclaim according to the order "Wisdom" and "Let us attend" with the lifting of the orarion towards the people, as the order of All-Night Vigil prescribes
 856: 
 857: ##### 3.4.8.1.9 There will be 8 readings, and on Theophany - 11. After the first three and the second three readings of both feasts there will be a separate troparion with its verses; there will be three of them[^321], besides "Glory, Both now", for the whole troparion is sung only twice, namely: once before the first verse and once before the last verse, that is before "Both now", and after the other verses - only up to the half[^322]
 858: 
 859: ##### 3.4.8.1.10 At the end of the readings - Small Litany (which the Deacon, if there be one, sings before the Holy Doors) with the exclamation of the Trisagion and immediately the Trisagion; and further according to the order of the Liturgy of Basil
 860: 
 861: ##### 3.4.8.1.11 Apostle on the Nativity of Christ: to the Hebrews, zaspiv 303 "God, who at sundry times", Gospel according to Luke, zaspiv 100 "And it came to pass in those days". On Theophany: to the Corinthians, zaspiv 343 "Am I not an apostle? am I not free?", Gospel according to Luke, zaspiv 9 "Now in the fifteenth year"
 862: 
 863: ##### 3.4.8.1.12 Instead of "It is truly meet" we sing "In Thee rejoiceth" or, according to the later rule of our service books, the heirmos of the 9th ode of the canon given for Compline of the Eve
 864: 
 865: ##### 3.4.8.1.13 Communion Hymn "Praise the Lord"
 866: 
 867: ##### 3.4.8.1.14 After the Prayer behind the Ambo - "Blessed be the name of the Lord" with Psalm "I will bless the Lord"
 868: 
 869: ##### 3.4.8.1.15 After the Dismissal both choirs gather in the middle of the church and sing together the Troparion, Glory, Both now: Kontakion of the Feast
 870: 
 871: ##### 3.4.8.1.16 VESPERS WITHOUT THE SERVICE
 872: with the Eve on Saturday or on Sunday
 873: Note: In this case there will be the Service of Chrysostom at its proper time, without Vespers, according to the rule given before on p. 154, if Saturday, and on p. 159, if Sunday; Vespers at its proper time thus:
 874: 
 875: ##### 3.4.8.1.17 The Priest, having put on an epitrachelion and having gone out before the Holy Doors, bows low and begins the usual: "Blessed is our God". Choirs: "Amen", also "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee", "O Heavenly King" and the rest with the Trisagion and "Our Father" up to "O come, let us worship" inclusive. Deacons, if there be [any], go out with the Priest before the Holy Doors and the right one of them exclaims: "Bless, Master", and the Priest: "Blessed is our God"[^323]
 876: 
 877: ##### 3.4.8.1.18 During the introductory Psalm the Priest, standing before the Holy Doors, says the evening prayers, as usual, and the deacons stand beside him and, at the end of the Psalm, one of them (the right) sings the Great Litany, and the Priest - its exclamation, and then, all bow low and withdraw to the sanctuary. If there be no deacons, then the Priest himself sings the litany
 878: 3.	"Blessed is the man" and the Small Litany, for which the second deacon goes out before the Holy Doors, and the Priest - the exclamation from his place. If there be no deacon, then the Priest himself, according to local custom, reads the litany quietly, sitting in his place, and the Choir sings its responses.
 879: 
 880: ##### 3.4.8.1.19 At "Lord, I have cried" - usual censing, which the Priest or deacons, if there be [any], perform; stichera on 8, "Glory, Both now" from the Heirmologion or according to the tone of the idiomesa
 881: 
 882: ##### 3.4.8.1.20 At "Glory, Both now" - Entrance with the Gospel, which the first deacon carries, if there be one, and the second precedes him with the censer; the Priest says the usual Prayer of the Entrance, as at Vespers, and blesses the Entrance, as at the Liturgy
 883: 
 884: ##### 3.4.8.1.21 At the end of the stichera the Deacon exclaims, if there be one, if - not, then the Priest himself: "Wisdom, attend", lifting up the Gospel, and while "O Gladsome Light" is sung, the Priest or deacon carrying the Gospel goes out, and behind them the Priest, through the middle doors to the sanctuary and, having placed the Gospel on the Holy Table, censes everything as usual and stands before the steps of the Holy Table
 885: 
 886: ##### 3.4.8.1.22 After the singing of "O Gladsome Light" the Priest exclaims with the deacons, if there be [any]: "Let us attend! Peace be unto all!", "Wisdom", "Let us attend" and, while the Prokeimenon of the day is sung, the Priest withdraws behind the Holy Table, and the deacons remain near the Holy Doors, exclaiming "Wisdom" and "Let us attend" to all the readings, of which on the Nativity of Christ there will be 8, and on Theophany - 11, with a separate troparion and its verses after the first three and after the second three readings
 887: 
 888: ##### 3.4.8.1.23 At the end of the readings the Priest returns before the steps of the Holy Table or the first deacon, if there be one, enters before the Holy Doors, where he sings the Small Litany; the Priest - the exclamation of the Trisagion, but the Trisagion is not sung, but immediately after the exclamation there will be "Let us attend! Peace be unto all!", "Wisdom", "Let us attend" and the Prokeimenon of the Feast is sung; after "Wisdom" and "Let us attend" - Apostle to the Galatians, zaspiv 201 "I speak after the manner of men"; Gospel according to Matthew, zaspiv 83 "The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed"[^324]  (on Theophany: to the Corinthians, zaspiv 143 from the half "Brethren, I would not have you ignorant"; Gospel according to Luke, zaspiv 9 "Now in the fifteenth year"). The Gospel is read by the Priest himself[^325]  from the Holy Doors, and the first of the deacons, if there be [any], exclaims: "Wisdom, attend! Let us hear the Holy Gospel"; priest: "The reading from the Holy Gospel according to (Name)"; and the second: "Let us attend"
 889: 
 890: ##### 3.4.8.1.24 After the singing of the Gospel the Priest, having kissed the beginning of the Gospel reading and having given [it] to the first deacon to kiss, also to the second, approaches the Holy Table, on which he places the Holy Gospel, which remains there. The deacons, having bowed low before the steps of the Holy Table, go out, each through HIS doors, before the Holy Doors and, having bowed low, first the second Deacon exclaims "Let us all say", and also the first after "Vouchsafe" - the litany "Let us complete". If there be no deacons, then the Priest himself sings the litanies from the Holy Table and immediately after the second exclamation of the litany "Let us complete" gives the Great Dismissal of the Feast itself. (On Theophany there is no dismissal here, but it will be after the Blessing of Water)
 891: 
 892: ##### 3.4.8.1.25 After the Dismissal both choirs gather together in the middle of the church and sing the Troparion, Glory, Both now: Kontakion of the Feast, and at the end the sacred ministers close the Holy Doors and, having bowed low, withdraw to the sacristy
 893: All-Night Vigil WITH Great Compline
 894: 
 895: ##### 3.4.8.1.26 At the usual time of the All-Night Vigil the Priest puts on an epitrachelion, and the deacons, if there be [any], - dalmatics with an orarion and go before the steps of the Holy Table and, having bowed low to the Holy Mysteries, open the Holy Doors and the deacons cense everything exactly as at the All-Night Vigil with Vespers[^326]
 896: 
 897: ##### 3.4.8.1.27 After the censing the Priest (after the Deacon, if there be one, exclaims: "Bless, Master") begins: "Blessed is our God"; the choirs sing "Amen", and the sacred ministers, having closed the Holy Doors, stand before the steps of the Holy Table. The choirs continue: "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee", "O Heavenly King" and the rest with the Trisagion and "Our Father" up to "O come, let us worship". Then the sacred ministers, having bowed low, withdraw behind the Holy Table and sit there in their places
 898: 
 899: ##### 3.4.8.1.28 After the end of the second tripalm the choirs sing alternatingly "God is with us", that is selected verses of the eighth ode of the prophecies of Isaiah. They sing thus: 1st choir: "God is with us, understand ye nations,... for God is with us", afterwards the second choir sings the same. Also other verses the choirs sing alternatingly, ending each verse with the words "For God is with us". After the end of all verses they sing "God is with us" three times[^327]. The custom of singing the whole first verse after each of the following ones as is usually done here, we do not find in any typikon[^328]. The Lviv Synod also adds that the Priest should not go out before the Holy Doors and sing these verses alternatingly with the choirs, but only there/, where there will be only one choir, for then the Priest replaces one of the choirs. Similarly he should not go out for the moleben verses "O Most Holy Lady", which the choirs say twice, that is once one, and once the other choir, but only, if there be one choir[^329]
 900: 
 901: ##### 3.4.8.1.29 Instead of the troparia of the day, given after the moleben verses "O Most Holy Lady", the Troparion of the Feast is sung; and instead of the troparia "Have mercy on us, O Lord", given after the Trisagion, which is after the Prayer of Manasses, the Kontakion of the Feast is sung
 902: 
 903: ##### 3.4.8.1.30 The Priest goes out before the Holy Doors for three prayers: of Basil, of Manasses and the second of Basil
 904: 
 905: ##### 3.4.8.1.31 After "Glory to God in the highest" the Priest, having put on a phelonion, opens the Holy Doors and there will be Litya and everything else until the end of Matins exactly as at the All-Night Vigil with Vespers
 906: 
 907: AT THE HOURS AND AT THE LITURGY
 908: Everything - to the Feast. Instead of the Trisagion, we sing at the Liturgy "As many as have been baptized into Christ".
 909: Note: "It will be reasonable also that from the Nativity of Christ until Theophany there will be no fast whatsoever nor kneeling either in church, or in cells" (Menaion at the end of 24 December)[^330]. However, our people adhere to the custom of keeping the fast on the ### 3.5.3 Eve of Theophany, as another rule of the Menaion on the ### 3.5.3 Eve of Theophany gives, and also on these days to kneel in church, just as throughout the whole year.
 910:  
 911: ### 3.4.9 December: Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos
 912: and of St. Joseph the Betrothed
 913: and of the Holy Hieromartyr Euthymius
 914: Notes
 915: 
 916: ##### 3.4.9.1 The Service of the Hieromartyr is sung at Compline on another day
 917: 
 918: ##### 3.4.9.2 St. Joseph has nothing in the divine service, except one troparion and kontakion, and this only in our horologia and service books. And the Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos also has almost nothing. Vespers of this feast has an entrance not for the sake of the Synaxis, but for the sake of the Great Prokeimenon of the Feast. Matins from the beginning to the canon - of small type, from the canon to the end - of great type
 919: 
 920: ##### 3.4.9.3 Although the divine service of this day, as also of the following, does not have All-Night Vigil, as also Polyeleos, however, our custom, approved by the Synod of Zamość (Titolo de Jeiuniis et Festis) /On fast and feasts/ and Lviv (Title IV, chap. 6) orders during the first three days of this feast to abstain from heavy work and to participate in the divine service; to these days belong: 25, 26 and 27 December
 921: 
 922: ##### 3.4.9.4 The Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos has three cases; it can fall: 1) on a weekday, except Monday; 2) on Monday; 3) on Sunday. The reason that the Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos has a separate rule for Monday is that in this case the service of the Synaxis is combined with the service of the Sunday after the Nativity, namely of the Holy Kinsmen of God, King David, Joseph the Betrothed and James, the Brother of the Lord. If, therefore, the Synaxis falls on Monday, then the Sunday after the Nativity would fall on 1 January, that is already after the Apodosis of the Feast, which will be 31 December; therefore, according to the typikon, it is transferred back, to 26 December. We will give the rule for all three above-mentioned cases
 923: 
 924: #### 3.4.9.1 RULE
 925: SYNAXIS OF THE MOST HOLY THEOTOKOS ON WEEKDAYS,
 926: except Monday
 927: 
 928: AT VESPERS
 929: 
 930: ##### 3.4.9.1.1 There will be no Kathisma
 931: 
 932: ##### 3.4.9.1.2 At "Lord, I have cried" - 7 stichera of the Feast, Glory, Both now: of the Feast
 933: 
 934: ##### 3.4.9.1.3 After the Entrance - Great Prokeimenon of the Feast "Who is so great a God as our God"
 935: 
 936: ##### 3.4.9.1.4 Aposticha of the Feast
 937: 
 938: ##### 3.4.9.1.5 At the end: Troparion to St. Joseph, Glory, Both now: to the Feast
 939: 
 940: ##### 3.4.9.1.6 Great Dismissal of the Feast with commemorations of the Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos, of the Betrothed and of the Holy Hieromartyr[^331]
 941: 
 942: #### 3.4.9.2 AT COMPLINE
 943: There will be no Canon to the Theotokos until the Apodosis of Theophany (14 January). After "It is truly meet" - Kontakion of the Betrothed, Glory, Both now: Kontakion of the Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos.
 944: #### 3.4.9.3 AT Midnight Office
 945: After the 1st Trisagion, instead of "Behold the Bridegroom", we say the Troparion of the Feast "Thy Nativity"; after the 2nd Trisagion - Kontakion of the Theotokos "He Who was before the morning star", also "Lord, have mercy" (12) and dismissal. We do not say the prayer "Remember, O Lord"[^332].

 1025: ##### 3.4.9.9.4 SYNAXIS OF THE MOST HOLY THEOTOKOS ON SUNDAY
 1026: The Service of the Synaxis and the Troparion and Kontakion of St. the Betrothed, prescribed for 26 December are not taken, but the Service of the Sunday after the Nativity is sung, according to the rule, which we will give here, first of the ### 3.4.10 Saturday after the Nativity.
 1027:  
 1028: ### 3.4.10 Saturday after the Nativity
 1029: Note: This Saturday has three cases: it can fall either on the first, or on the last day of the Afterfeast of the Nativity of Christ, or on others. When it falls on the first day, that is 26 December, then it is taken with the Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos and has a separate rule; when - on the last, that is 31 December, then it is taken with the Apodosis of the feast of the Nativity and has a separate rule; if on others, that is 27, 28, 29 and 30 December, then it also has a separate rule. We will give consistently all three rules.
 1030: 
 1031: #### 3.4.10.1 RULE
 1032: 
 1033: ##### 3.4.10.1.1 SATURDAY AFTER THE NATIVITY 26 DECEMBER
 1034: with the Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos
 1035: 
 1036: #### 3.4.10.2 AT THE LITURGY
 1037: Prokeimenon and Apostle-Gospel - first of the ### 3.4.10 Saturday after the Nativity, and then - of the Synaxis. Alleluia of the Saturday and of the Synaxis - common.
 1038: Antiphons, troparia and the rest see 26 December, here on p. 177-178.
 1039: 
 1040: ##### 3.4.10.2.1 SATURDAY AFTER THE NATIVITY 27, 28, 29 OR 30 DECEMBER AT THE LITURGY
 1041: Prokeimenon, Apostle, Gospel and Communion Hymn - of the ### 3.4.10 Saturday after the Nativity. Only, if the Saturday falls on 30 December, then the Apostle-Gospel of the Saturday before Theophany is also taken in the second place[^334].
 1042: 
 1043: ##### 3.4.10.2.2 SATURDAY AFTER THE NATIVITY 30 DECEMBER
 1044: with the Apodosis of the feast of the Nativity
 1045: 
 1046: #### 3.4.10.3 AT THE LITURGY
 1047: Prokeimenon, Alleluia and Communion Hymn - only of the Feast, and Apostle and Gospel - first of the ### 3.4.10 Saturday after the Nativity, also of the Saturday before Theophany[^335]. Everything else - only to the Feast, according to the general rule of the Apodosis of a Feast of the Lord on a weekday.
 1048: ### 3.4.11 Sunday after the Nativity of Christ
 1049: of the Holy and Righteous Kinsmen of God Joseph the Betrothed,
 1050: King David and James, Brother of the Lord

The Communion Hymn will be "Praise the Lord" and of the Saints[^336].

 1102: ### 3.4.12 Rule Concerning Saturdays and Sundays between the Nativity and Theophany
 1103: Between the Nativity and Theophany there can be:
 1104: 
 1105: ##### 3.4.12.1 One Saturday and one Sunday
 1106: 
 1107: ##### 3.4.12.2 Two Saturdays and one Sunday
 1108: 
 1109: ##### 3.4.12.3 One Saturday and two Sundays
 1110: 
 1111: ##### 3.4.12.4 Two Saturdays and two Sundays
 1112: This discrepancy regarding the number of Saturdays depends on the day of the week on which the Nativity of Christ falls, as follows from the following table:
 1113: 
 1114: TABLE OF SATURDAYS AND SUNDAYS
 1115: between the Nativity and Theophany
 1116: 
 1117: DECEMBER							JANUARY					
 1118: NATIVITY	Afterfeast of the NATIVITY	APODOSIS	THEOPHANY	Forefeast	THEOPHANY							
 1119: 25	26	27	28	29	30	31	1	2	3	4	5	6
 1120: 
 1121: ##### 3.4.12.5 Su	Mo	Tu	We	Th	Fr	Sa	Su	Mo	Tu	We	Th	Fr
 1122: 
 1123: ##### 3.4.12.6 Mo	Tu	We	Th	Mo	Sa	Su	Mo	Tu	We	Th	Mo	Sa
 1124: 
 1125: ##### 3.4.12.7 Tu	We	Th	Mo	Sa	Su	Mo	Tu	We	Th	Mo	Sa	Su
 1126: 
 1127: ##### 3.4.12.8 We	Th	Mo	Sa	Su	Mo	Tu	We	Th	Mo	Sa	Su	Mo
 1128: 
 1129: ##### 3.4.12.9 Th	Mo	Sa	Su	Mo	Tu	We	Th	Mo	Sa	Su	Mo	Tu
 1130: 
 1131: ##### 3.4.12.10 Fr	Sa	Su	Mo	Tu	We	Th	Fr	Sa	Su	Mo	Tu	We
 1132: 
 1133: ##### 3.4.12.11 Sa	Su	Mo	Tu	We	Th	Fr	Sa	Su	Mo	Tu	We	Th
 1134: If the Nativity of Christ falls on Sunday or Monday, then between the Nativity and Theophany there will be one Saturday and one Sunday, as you will see in the 1st and 3rd transverse rows of weekly letters.
 1135: If the Nativity of Christ falls on Tuesday, then there will be two Saturdays and one Sunday, as you will see in the 3rd row.
 1136: If the Nativity of Christ on Wednesday, Thursday or Friday, then there will be two Saturdays and two Sundays, as you will see in the 4th, 5th and 6th rows.
 1137: If the Nativity of Christ on Saturday, then there will be one Saturday and two Sundays, as you will see in the 7th row.
 1138: Now, if you wish to know how many Saturdays and Sundays there will be in a given year between the Nativity and Theophany, then first of all you must find out on which day of the week the Nativity of Christ falls, afterwards, going along the transverse line from that day of the week to Theophany, you will find the number of Saturdays and Sundays between the Nativity and Theophany. Regarding the rule which will be for these Saturdays and Sundays in the case when there will be two Saturdays and two Sundays (as in the 4th, 5th and 6th rows), there will be no inconsistency, as there will be no inconsistency in the case when either two Saturdays, or two Sundays (as in the 3rd and 7th rows), for these two Saturdays and two Sundays have their unchangeable rule. But all inconsistencies are limited to the case of only one Saturday or Sunday (as in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 7th rows). In this case two questions arise:
 1139: 
 1140: ##### 3.4.12.12 Which of the two Saturdays or Sundays to take? after the Nativity or before Theophany?
 1141: 
 1142: ##### 3.4.12.13 What to do with the second Saturday or Sunday, which then has no place?
 1143: To the first question we answer: if this Saturday or Sunday is in the middle of the feast of the Nativity, that is within December, then the Saturday or Sunday after the Nativity is taken; if - outside the feast of the Nativity, that is within January, then the Saturday or Sunday before Theophany is taken. Regarding the second question, that is what to do with one Saturday or Sunday which sometimes has no place, we answer: Greek books give no rule for this and therefore this Saturday or Sunday should not have been taken. However, the Slavs do not wish to discard anything and give the following rules for this case.
 1144: 
 1145: #### 3.4.12.1 RULE FOR SATURDAYS AND SUNDAYS
 1146: between the Nativity of Christ and Theophany
 1147: 
 1148: SATURDAY
 1149: The Saturday, which will be the one between the Nativity and Theophany can fall either in the middle, or outside the feast of the Nativity: in the middle, namely 30 or 31 December so, as in the first and second rows; outside the feast, namely 1 January, as in the 7th row. If, therefore, it falls in the middle of the feast, then the Apostle-Gospel will be first of the ### 3.4.10 Saturday after the Nativity, and after - of the Saturday before Theophany. Prokeimenon, Alleluia and Communion Hymn on 30 December will be only of the ### 3.4.10 Saturday after the Nativity; on 31 December, that is on the Apodosis of the feast - will be only of the Feast. If, therefore, it falls outside the feast, as in the 6th row, that is 1 January, then the Apostle-Gospel will be first to the Circumcision, for the Saturday does not have them. On ### 3.4.10 Saturday after the Nativity the Apostle-Gospel is taken on the Apodosis of the feast, 31 December. Prokeimenon, Alleluia and Communion Hymn - only of the Feast.
 1150: 
 1151: SUNDAY
 1152: If there be one Sunday between the Nativity and Theophany, then, similarly as for Saturday, it falls either in the middle of the feast, that is 30 or 31 December, as in the 3rd and 2nd rows, or outside the feast, that is 1 January with the Circumcision, as in the 1st row. And if it falls in the middle of the feast, then the Sunday after the Nativity is taken on 30 or 31 December according to the rule given here on p. 182-183. And the Sunday before Theophany is taken on 1 January in the first place, also the Circumcision and everything else according to the rule which is given for 1 January, when it falls on a Sunday. If the Sunday is one and falls on 1 January, as in the 1st row, then the Sunday after the Nativity is taken on 26 December with the Synaxis of the Most Holy Theotokos according to the rule given here on p. 181[^337].
 1153: 
 1154:  
 1155: ### 3.4.13 December: Holy First-Martyr Stephen
 1156: and Venerable Theodore
 1157: The Service of these Saints - without Polyeleos, according to the general rule of two saints on 4 in the Afterfeast, although in the Pochaiv Anthologion the Service of St. Stephen is given with Polyeleos. One peculiarity of this day - at Matins, for St. Protomartyr (according to others also the Feast) has both Stichera of the Praises, and afterwards - Small Doxology, and Aposticha in its place. Finally our people even on this day abstain from work and take part in the divine service.

 1205: ## 3.5 January
 1206: ### 3.5.1 January: Circumcision of the Lord and memory of St. Basil the Great
 1207: Note
 1208: In general typikons the divine service of this day is not given with All-Night Vigil, but only with Polyeleos. However, probably for the sake of the beginning of the civil year, or also for Basil the Great, for many years All-Night Vigil has been served with us, because it is already given in the Pochaiv Anthologion of 1777. We will present the rule first for weekdays, and then for Sunday.
 1209:

 1228:

 1320: ### 3.5.3 Eve of Theophany
 1321: Everything according to the rule of the Eve of the Nativity of Christ, here on p. 161-167.
 1322: Note: We adhere to the fast exactly as on the Eve of the Nativity of Christ, that is with dairy; but the simple people - without dairy, with one meal, as even the Lviv Synod allows (Title XII[^346], part 4, a. c.).
 1323: ### 3.5.4 January: Holy Theophany
 1324: Everything according to the rule of the feast of the Nativity of Christ, here on p. 168-175, with the exception of the Blessing of Water, which here takes place after Vespers or after the Prayer behind the Ambo, if Vespers be with the Service of Basil, and on the next day - after the Prayer behind the Ambo, as is given below.
 1325: 
 1326: RITE OF THE GREAT BLESSING OF WATER
 1327: 
 1328: #### 3.5.4.1 RULE
 1329: After the Prayer behind the Ambo, if Saturday or Sunday, then after the dismissal of Vespers, the church cross-bearer stands between two candle-bearers in the middle of the church, and before Him - a church server with three candlesticks, with a censer and with a vessel for incense. The Deacon takes the Holy Gospel from the table, the Priest takes the cross with his right hand and, having bowed low to the Holy Mysteries, they go out through the Holy Doors: first the Deacon with the Gospel, behind him - the Priest with the cross, vested in all sacred vestments of his rank, and the Choir sings the Troparion "The voice of the Lord"[^347]; all proceed to the narthex of the church. When all have gone out there, the Deacon places the Holy Gospel, and the Priest - the cross on a table covered with a tablecloth or a clean cloth, on which there will be also a wide vessel with water; and immediately the Priest censes the table from four sides and all present, according to the order.
 1330: After the end of the troparia follow three readings of prophecies; also the Apostle with its Prokeimenon and Alleluia, during the singing of which the deacons cense the water from four sides of the tetrapod, the Priest and all present, according to the order. Then the Priest reads the Gospel, before which the first Deacon exclaims: "Wisdom, attend" and the rest, and the second: "Let us attend".
 1331: After the singing of the Gospel the Deacon says the litany "In peace let us pray to the Lord", during which the Priest reads quietly the prayer "O Lord Jesus Christ"; and after the prayer He does not exclaim, but says to Himself: "Amen". And when "For the precipitous, pure" is said, the Priest begins loudly this prayer: "Great Art Thou, O Lord"[^348]. The prayer "O Trinity beyond all being", since it is given only in some editions, may be omitted; this is allowed by the Euchologion of Benedict, although our typikons do not allow this[^349].
 1332: In the prayer "Great Art Thou, O Lord" three members are exclaimed three times, namely the first member "Great Art Thou, O Lord", at which the Priest three times crosswise signs the water with three lit candles[^350]; the second "Thou Thyself, therefore", at which He blesses the water with His hand, immersing His fingers crosswise; the third "Thou Thyself and now", at which He breathes three times crosswise on the water. When He exclaims: "And save, O Lord, Thy servants, the Most Holy Ecumenical Primate (Name) the Pope of Rome[^351]  and our faithful Emperor (Name)" the Choir sings "Many Years".
 1333: At the end of this prayer the Choir: "Amen"; priest: "Peace be unto all" and, after the prayer at the bowing of heads, which he says quietly, he exclaims: "For Thou Art the sanctification" and immediately blesses with the cross: immerses it simply into the water, holding with both hands, and sings this troparion: "When in Jordan"[^352], and all the people sing with Him. "And the second time singing the same troparion"[^353], and all the people sing with Him. Then the server pours holy water onto a tray or into a sprinkler. The Priest turns his face to the west, holding the precious cross with his left hand, and with the right - the sprinkler, and sprinkles all the people with holy water. After this the choirs sing Glory, Both now: Stichera "Let us praise, O faithful", the procession returns to the church in the same way, and the Priest sprinkles on all sides[^354], and thus they enter the sanctuary through the Holy Doors: the Deacon with the Gospel, and after him the Priest with the cross. And when the Priest has sprinkled the entire sanctuary, the Deacon places the Gospel, and the Priest the cross on the Holy Table, in its place, and the Choir sings "Blessed be the name of the Lord", if there be Vespers with the Service of Basil; if Vespers - separate from the Holy Liturgy, then immediately the Great Dismissal of the Feast; at the end: Troparion, Glory, Both now: Kontakion of the Feast, which both choirs sing together in the middle of the church, as at Vespers with the Service of Basil on 25 December.
 1334: Note: The Lviv Synod orders pastors to perform this blessing of water in their churches both on the Eve, and, more solemnly, on the very day of the Feast (Title IV, Chapter IV, part 2).

 1341: ### 3.5.5 January: Synaxis of Saint John the Forerunner
 1342: This Synaxis can fall either on weekdays, or on a Sunday. Its service has the appearance of a Saint on 6 without Polyeleos, but with the Great Doxology. Vespers will be with an Entrance, in view of the Great Prokeimenon of the Feast. Matins from the beginning to the canon - of small type, from the canon to the end - of great type. Here is the rule for both cases.

 1508: Note
 1509: In January fall five saints, whose memory we honor with Polyeleos without All-Night Vigil, that is 11 January - Ven. Theodosius, 17 January - Anthony the Great, 20 January - Euthymius the Great, 25 January - Gregory the Theologian, 27 January - Translation of the relics of Chrysostom, and since the Triodion can begin within the limits of 35 days, from 11 January to 14 February, therefore these saints can fall either outside, or in the middle of the Triodion: in the middle of the Triodion, if the beginning of the Triodion falls on one of the days from 11 to 27 January; outside the Triodion, if the beginning of the Triodion falls on one of the days from 28 January to 14 February. And if they fall outside the Triodion, then their services are subject to the general rule of a Saint with Polyeleos; if they fall in the middle of the Triodion, they should have a separate rule, and since church books do not give it, we will give it.
 1510: 
 1511: VARIOUS CASES REGARDING THESE SAINTS
 1512: Of the above-mentioned five saints, St. Theodosius can fall only with one service of the Triodion, that is with the service of the Sunday of the Publican; and since in this case at the Liturgy it would be necessary to take three Apostles and three Gospels: of the ### 3.5.7 Sunday after Theophany, of the Sunday of the Publican and of the Saint, then, to avoid this, Slavic typikons transfer the service of the venerable one to another day.
 1513: St. Anthony can fall only with the service of the Sunday of the Publican, but is not transferred, for he does not coincide with the ### 3.5.7 Sunday after Theophany.
 1514: St. Euthymius can fall not only with the Sunday of the Publican, but also with the Sunday of the Prodigal [Son]. If the Sunday of the Publican falls on 13 January, then the Sunday of the Prodigal [Son] will be on 20 January, that is together with St. Euthymius.
 1515: St. Gregory and Chrysostom can fall not only with the Sunday of the Publican and of the Prodigal [Son], but also with the Meatfare, for when the Triodion begins on 18 or 20 January, then the Sunday of the Prodigal [Son] will be 25 or 27 January, and when the Triodion begins on 11 or 13 January, then 25 or 27 January will be Meatfare Sunday. These saints can fall also on the Saturday of Souls, that is Meatfare, which precedes Meatfare Sunday. If the Triodion begins on 12 or 14 January, then 25 or 27 falls on Meatfare Saturday. Chrysostom can fall also on Cheesefare Tuesday, which will be after Meatfare Sunday, for if 25 January falls on Meatfare Sunday, then 27 January will be Cheesefare Tuesday.
 1516: 
 1517: #### 3.5.27.1 RULE
 1518: If one of these saints falls outside the Triodion, one should adhere to the general rule of a Saint with Polyeleos. If he falls in the middle of the Triodion, as e. g. St. Theodosius can fall on the Sunday of the Publican, he must be transferred to another day. If one of the four other saints falls on the Sunday of the Publican, of the Prodigal [Son], Meatfare, on Meatfare Saturday or on Cheesefare Tuesday, then one must adhere to the rule of the Three Hierarchs, given in the Menaion on 30 January, which we will give immediately, with the exception of the All-Night Vigil, which will not be here, but there will be it at Great Vespers, at the end. Resurrectional Troparion, Glory: of the Saint, Both now: Resurrectional Theotokion according to the tone of the Saint. At Compline, after "It is truly meet" - Kontakion of the Saint, Glory, Both now: Kontakion of the Triodion[^361].
 1519: ### 3.5.10 January: The Three Hierarchs
 1520: Basil the Great, Gregory the Theologian and John Chrysostom,
 1521: and the Holy Hieromartyr Hippolytus
 1522: Note
 1523: The Service of the Hieromartyr is sung on another day at Compline; the service of the Hierarchs is sung on this day, according to the general rule of a Saint with All-Night Vigil; it departs from the general rule of a Saint with All-Night Vigil only in that at Matins, instead of "More honorable", it has separate refrains, as on feasts of the Theotokos. However, if their service falls within the limits of the Triodion, then it is combined with the service of the Triodion, and therefore has separate rules.

 1579: III. THREE HIERARCHS
 1580: ON CHEESEFARE MONDAY, TUESDAY OR THURSDAY
 1581: Note
 1582: Our and Russian church rules do not give for this case All-Night Vigil, and consequently neither Small Vespers, but only one Great, without blessing of loaves; afterwards also Compline, at which after "It is truly meet" - Kontakion of the Saints. All this according to the rule of the Forerunner on 24 February[^365]. However, since with us even in this case All-Night Vigil is served, although there is no rule for it, we will give the rule of the All-Night Vigil also for this case, similarly to the rule of the Meeting on 2 February, if it falls on Monday, Tuesday and Thursday of Cheesefare week.

 1584: #### 3.5.10.6 RULE AT SMALL VESPERS
 1585: Everything - as outside the Triodion, only at the Aposticha - stichera idiomesa of the day of the Triodion twice and to the Martyrs, Glory: of the Saints, Both now: their Theotokion.
 1586: AT Great Vespers, AT MATINS,
 1587: 
 1588: AT THE HOURS AND AT THE LITURGY
 1589: Everything, as outside the Triodion, only at Matins, at the Praises there will be Glory: of the Triodion, Both now: of the Triodion.
 1590: Note
 1591: If the Three Hierarchs fall on one of the days of Cheesefare week, then the three-ode canon of Matins we sing at Compline, namely: if the Feast is on Monday, then at Compline on Sunday; if on Tuesday, then on Wednesday; if on Wednesday, then on Thursday; if on Thursday, then on Tuesday; if on Friday, then on Wednesday. Thus give our and Russian typikons for the Feast of the Meeting on these days. Only, if the Feast falls on Monday, let the three-ode canon be sung on Tuesday, for when there is All-Night Vigil - Compline does not happen.

 1600: ## 3.6 February
 1601: Meeting of the Lord
 1602: Note
 1603: This feast falls on 2 February and therefore can fall either in the middle, or outside the Triodion. And since the first boundary of the Triodion is 11 January, and the last - 14 February, therefore it can fall at most 22 days from the beginning of the Triodion and 12 days before the beginning of the Triodion. When there is the earliest boundary of the Triodion, that is 11 January, then the feast reaches Monday of the first week of Lent, the next - immediately after the fourth Sunday of the Triodion, that is after Cheesefare Sunday. And if it falls outside the Triodion, then its order is celebrated according to the general rule of a feast of the Theotokos, although partly it is of the Lord. It differs from a feast of the Theotokos only by a separate dismissal and at the Liturgy - by a separate entrance verse, and on the Apodosis there will not be the Apostle-Gospel of the Feast and of the day, as for the Theotokos, but only of the day, as for the Lord. And if it falls on a Sunday, its service is combined with the Resurrectional, according to the rule of a feast of the Theotokos. It has one day of Forefeast and seven days of Afterfeast, for it is given up on 9 February.
 1604: If it falls in the middle of the Triodion and coincides in this way with the services of the Triodion, then it has a separate rule for the Forefeast, for the Feast and for the Afterfeast, as we present.

 1658: II. FOREFEAST OF THE MEETING ON MEATFARE SATURDAY
 1659: When the Forefeast of the Meeting falls on Meatfare Saturday, then the service of the Forefeast we sing on the previous Friday with Saints Cyrus, John and Tryphon[^367], according to the general rule of two saints on 4 in the Forefeast, only at "Lord, I have cried" there will be stichera: of the Forefeast - 3 and to the Holy Unmercenaries - 3, and the stichera of Tryphon are taken in the morning at the Praises on 4; Glory, Both now: of the Forefeast[^368]. After them, at the Aposticha, - stichera of the Forefeast with their refrains. On Meatfare Saturday we sing the general order for the deceased.
 1660: 
 1661: III. FOREFEAST OF THE MEETING
 1662: ON CHEESEFARE MONDAY, TUESDAY AND THURSDAY
 1663: Everything according to the general rule of a Saint on 4 in the Forefeast, only at the Aposticha of Vespers, and also at Matins, there will not be stichera of the Forefeast, but idiomesa of the Triodion of the day twice and to the Martyr with general refrains; also Glory, Both now: of the Forefeast. And at Matins, after the 2nd Kathisma there will not be the Sessional hymn of the Forefeast, but of the Triodion. The canon, where the three-ode canon comes, will be of the Forefeast with heirmos on 4, three troparia of the Saint on 2 and of the Triodion on 8[^369]; katavasia at the 3rd, 6th, 8th and 9th - heirmos of the canon of the Saint. Generally, in those odes where the three-ode canon comes, there will be the Katavasia of the Triodion.
