```text
 783: #### 3.4.7.1 RULE
 784: At the appointed time the Priest enters the temple and, having approached the Holy Table and having bowed low, kisses the Gospel, marks four Gospel readings and, having bowed again, goes out to the sacristy; puts on an epitrachelion, goes out before the closed Holy Doors, makes a low bow to the Holy Mysteries and begins the usual: "Blessed is our God". Choir: "Amen", also "Glory to Thee, our God, glory to Thee", "O Heavenly King" and everything else, as usual, up to "O come, let us worship" inclusive[^320][^313]. At the second "O come, let us worship" the Priest, having bowed low, enters the sanctuary and, while the choirs sing the tripalm, reads it sitting in his place.
 785: When, after the Troparion of the Forefeast "Once Mary was registered", the Theotokion is also read, the choirs sing three stichera idiomesa[^314]  on 6, that is twice each. The first stichera both the first and the second time is sung without a refrain; the second - the first time with a separate refrain, and the second - with another separate refrain; the third - the first time with the refrain "Glory", and the second - with the refrain "Both now". All four above-mentioned refrains at all Hours - are the same. At the 9th Hour the third stichera is taken three times, that is the first time it is read loudly and piously by the canonarch in the middle of the church, without a refrain, then the second time - by one choir with the refrain "Glory", and the third - by the other with the refrain "Both now"[^315].
 786: After the singing of the three stichera there will be three readings: the first - of the Prophecy with a Prokeimenon, the second - of the Apostle without a Prokeimenon and without Alleluia, the third - of the Gospel, beginning it from "Wisdom, attend!", "Let us hear". All this is accompanied by the following actions: when the stichera end, the Priest puts on a phelonion and, having gone out before the steps of the altar and having bowed, opens the Holy Doors and exclaims: "Let us attend! Peace be unto all!" (blessing the people), "Wisdom! Let us attend!". The choirs sing the Prokeimenon. After its conclusion the Priest, having exclaimed before the title of the Prophecy "Wisdom!" and before the reading "Let us attend!", waits before the steps of the altar for the end of the reading of the Prophecy and, after its conclusion, having exclaimed "Wisdom!" and "Let us attend!" before the reading of the Apostle, as usual, puts incense into the censer with the short prayer "Incense we offer to Thee" and, having blessed the incense with the words "Blessed is our God", censes everything as usual, that is the Holy Table from four sides, the iconostasis, the choirs and the people[^316]. At the end of the Apostle, and together with it the censing, the candle-bearers go out before the analogion, and the Priest approaches the Holy Table and, having bowed, takes the Holy Gospel and, having placed it on the analogion, begins to sing the Gospel from "Wisdom, attend". After the singing of the Gospel the Priest, having kissed the beginning of the reading, leaves it there, closes the Holy Doors and, having bowed low to the Holy Mysteries, goes out to the sacristy, takes off the phelonion, goes out through the side doors before the Holy Doors for "Thou Who at all times" and remains there until the end of the Hour.
 787: Note: Since we sing all the Hours together, the prayer of blessing the incense should be said only at the 1st Hour, at the others - only "Blessed is our God" just as at Great Vespers with All-Night Vigil.
 788: If there be deacons, they put on dalmatics with an orarion before the beginning of the 1st Hour and remain vested until the end of the Typika. At the Prokeimenon, together with the Priest, they go before the steps of the altar and, having bowed low all together to the Holy Mysteries, open the Holy Doors. The right Deacon exclaims: "Let us attend!", and the left, after the giving of peace by the Priest: "Wisdom! Let us attend!". Also before the first and second reading - the right: "Wisdom!", and the left: "Let us attend!" and they cense everything as usual, as at the beginning of the Liturgy. At the end of the Apostle, and together with it the censing, both deacons stand with the Priest before the steps of the altar and, having bowed all three together to the Holy Mysteries, go out from the sanctuary: the Priest with the Gospel through the middle [doors], and the deacons, having swapped their sides, through the side doors to the analogion. The right Deacon exclaims: "Wisdom, attend!", "Let us hear", the Priest: "The reading from the Holy Gospel according to (Name)", and the left deacon: "Let us attend!". The Priest sings the Gospel. Having finished, the Priest kisses the beginning of the reading, also the right deacon, and after him the left. Having bowed low, the deacons return through their doors to the sanctuary and, together with the Priest, close the Holy Doors. Having bowed low all three together to the Holy Mysteries, they withdraw: the deacons to their places, and the Priest before the iconostasis for "Thou Who at all times".
 789: If the hierarch or other sacred dignitaries be present in the church, the deacons should cense them before the choirs, and neither the Priest nor the deacons should kiss the Gospel before the hierarch and sacred dignitaries, and therefore both deacons together carry the open Gospel to them for kissing, also to the Priest standing in the Holy Doors and, when he kisses it, the deacons themselves kiss [it], after which they place it on the analogion and, having bowed low to the Holy Mysteries, return, each through his doors, to the sanctuary.
 790: Question: When the Royal Hours are transferred from Sunday or Saturday back, to Friday, should one take on them the Troparion of the Eve or of the Forefeast, 22 or 23 December?
 791: Answer: The Typikon mentions the Troparion and Kontakion of the Eve, therefore we think that one should take [those] of the Eve. If someone thinks that this will not be good and takes one Troparion for two days, that is on the Eve and before the Eve, let him consider that the Troparion of the Forefeast is also taken the same on two different days of the Forefeast.
 792: THE TYPIKA (Typika)
 793: After the concluding prayer of the 9th Hour we immediately read the Typika just as in the Horologion, however, without the introductory verse that is before the first psalm, without the stichera on the "Beatitudes", without the Apostle-Gospel; also, if there be Liturgy, then also without the "Creed" and without "Blessed be the name of the Lord", and without the following 33rd Psalm, for all this will be taken at the Liturgy. When the Royal Hours are transferred back, to Friday, then since then there will be no Liturgy, here both the "Creed" and "Blessed be the name of the Lord" with the 33rd Psalm is read. Instead of the kontakia of the temple, of the day and others, one Kontakion of the Eve is taken. Here is the detailed rule for you.
 794: 
 795: DETAILED RULE
 796: 
 797: ##### 3.4.7.1.1 After the concluding prayer of the 9th Hour the Priest, having bowed before the Holy Doors, enters the sanctuary and sits in his place
 798: 
 799: ##### 3.4.7.1.2 The choirs read: Psalm 102 "Bless the Lord, O my soul" and Psalm 145 "Praise the Lord, O my soul", "Glory, Both now", "Only-begotten Son"
 800:

 802: 4.	"Remember us, O Lord" (3).
 803: 5.	"The heavenly choir", verse "Come unto Him", "The heavenly choir", Glory: "The Choir of holy angels", Both now: "Remit, pardon" (when there is no Liturgy, then Both now: "The Creed", also "Remit, forgive").
 804: 6.	"Our Father", Kontakion of the Eve once and "Lord, have mercy" (12).
```

```text
 807: Diagram: At the High Throne** [Left] 2 ... 4 ... 6 [Center] D (High Place) [Right] 1 ... 3 ... 5 **196.** During the reading of the Gospel all remain in their places, looking towards the ambo or the place from which the Gospel is read. **197.** At the Cherubic Hymn all lift their hands, if this can be done conveniently, but all recite the Cherubic Hymn and make the prescribed bows. During the censing of the holy table by the deacon all step away from it slightly so that the deacon can easily go around it. **198.** From the table of oblation each takes one of the things used in the Divine Sacrifice, namely: the spear, the spoon, holding them on their chests. All go out^[784] through the northern doors, in front -- the deacon, who exclaims: "All of you" and stands in the holy doors in the sanctuary, behind him other concelebrating priests, beginning from the youngest, exclaiming each: "All of you," one or even several, if there is a custom, and stand facing one another outside the sanctuary before the holy doors as at the Little Entrance. The principal priest exclaims: "Our most holy [Pontiff]" and stands exactly before the holy doors, turns to the west when he exclaims "All of you," after which he enters the sanctuary, and behind him go the concelebrants and each stands at the holy table at his place. **199.** Having made the Great Entrance, if there is no deacon, one of the concelebrants sings the first part of the litany "Let us complete," and another -- the second part, so that each has time to read the Prayer of the Offering. **200.** When the principal priest kisses the Holy Gifts, the concelebrants one by one approach the holy table, according to the order of their dignity. The principal priest, having stepped back slightly from the holy table, turns to the right side and looks to the north, and each concelebrant kisses first the Holy Gifts, and then the left and right shoulder of the principal priest and stands to his left, slightly behind. The second concelebrant kisses first the Holy Gifts, then -- the principal celebrant, and at the end -- the first concelebrant and stands on his right side. All others do likewise. The principal priest says: "Christ is in our midst," and the concelebrant responds: "He is and shall be." Likewise do also the others, who kiss one another. After the kiss of peace the celebrant returns before the holy table; the 1st concelebrant takes one edge of the *aer*, and the 2nd -- the second edge and fan with it over the Gifts. All others stand in their places and quietly recite the Symbol of Faith. **201.** The concelebrants offering the sacrifice point with their hand to the holy diskos, and then to the holy chalice, just as the principal celebrant, simultaneously, slowly and attentively, sing the words of consecration, recite together "Thine own of Thine own," but only the principal celebrant blesses the Gifts. The same applies also to the Epiclesis. One must ensure, especially in the Liturgy of St. Basil, that after the reading of the prayer which immediately precedes the consecration, all together with the serving priest exclaim from the beginning to the end the words of consecration. It will also be good if the principal celebrant pronounces the last words of this prayer louder so that the concelebrants can hear them, and watches that all are ready already for the simultaneous exclamation of the words of consecration (see no. 134). **202.** The first part of the litany "Having commemorated all the saints" is sung by one of the concelebrants, if there is no deacon, and the second part -- by another, so that all have time to read the prayer "To Thee we entrust all our life." **203.** After the breaking [of the Lamb], the principal celebrant calls the deacon and gives him a particle of the Holy Bread, as prescribed. Then all recite the prayer "I believe, O Lord" and the principal priest communicates of the Body of Christ. All concelebrants, in turn, according to their dignity, approach the holy table from the side of the oblation table, and the principal celebrant stands on the opposite side of it. After the communion of the Body of Christ, each goes to the north of the holy table and washes, if necessary, his fingers in the vessel standing on the table of oblation, and, according to the prescribed sequence, they go behind the 1st concelebrant, who stands at his place at the holy table. The deacon consumes the particle of Bread after the priests. The principal celebrant, having returned to the center, communicates of the Most Precious Blood and moves away from the holy table; after this the concelebrants, according to the prescribed order, approach the holy table, this time from the southern side, and each after the communion of the Blood departs by the table of oblation and stands at his place at the holy table. At the end the deacon receives, according to the prescription, the communion of the Most Precious Blood from the principal celebrant. 
 808: 
 809: [INSERT DIAGRAM/TABLE HERE FROM ORIGINAL PDF]
 810: 
 811: [Diagram: Communion of the Body / Communion of the Blood] [Table of Oblation] 4 3 | 4 3 2 1 | 2 1 [Holy Table] [Principal Celebrant] [Principal Celebrant] **204.** Each, having just communicated, wipes his lips with the purificator at the edge of the chalice. **205.** The Prayer behind the Ambo is exclaimed, standing between the two choirs, by the principal celebrant. Only after the dismissal and after the holy doors are closed does each take off the sacred vestments. **6) In the Ordinary, or Private Form** **206.** There is no non-actual celebrant, or assistant, at the ordinary or private service. **207.** Everything that was said about concelebration in the solemn form is valid also for concelebration in the ordinary or private form, with the following exceptions: **208.** In seminaries and houses of religious education it will be good if the deacon participates in the celebration of the Divine Liturgy also when serving with the simple rite and if ordinary singing is used. Here, however, it is recommended to observe the rules which are binding for simple concelebration without a deacon. **209.** If there is no time for the recitation of the preparatory prayers before the iconostasis, which all concelebrants recite together or each separately, it is never permitted to omit the prayer "O Lord, stretch forth Thy hand." Having entered the sanctuary, they recite the psalm "I will enter into Thy house" and, having kissed the holy table, the Gospel and, if there exists a custom, -- the altar cross, they put on the priestly vestments (see no. 178). **210.** The members of the litanies are distributed among the concelebrants and are sung so that the one who does not sing the litanies has time to recite the corresponding prayer without haste. If there be two concelebrants, they sing the liturgical litanies alternately, having recited first quietly the corresponding prayer of each litany, but the prayer of the Great Litany and the Prayer of Thanksgiving after communion they recite quietly after the litany, but before the exclamation. It should also be noted that the first part of the litany after the Great Entrance and the litanies after the Anaphora are said by the second priest, who after that recites quietly the prayer; and the second part with the exclamation is recited by the first. If there be three concelebrants, then the 1st says the Great Litany, the 2nd -- the first Small Litany, the 3rd -- the second Small Litany; the 1st -- again the Litany after the Gospel; the 2nd -- the Litany of the Catechumens; the 3rd -- the first Small Litany of the Faithful, and the 1st -- the second; the 2nd -- the first part of the litany after the Entrance and after the Anaphora, and the 3rd -- the second part of those litanies; at the end the 1st -- the Thanksgiving Litany after communion. Such a method of distribution of various litanies among individual concelebrants is not prescribed absolutely, but only recommended to be used for greater convenience. **211.** It is not required that all concelebrants go out for the Little Entrance, but if they go out, then the one who is the 1st among them carries the Gospel, he himself recites the Prayer of the Entrance and imparts the blessing. But it is always required that those standing before the holy table or on its right side, before they go out, go around the holy table and go out behind the holy doors. **212.** There will be no blessing of the High Throne and all must remain near the throne during the reading of the Apostle. **213.** For the Great Entrance not all have to go out. If only the 1st makes the Entrance, he himself places the *aer* on his left shoulder and himself exclaims: "Our most holy [Pontiff]." If all go out, then each does not have to take some object used for the Divine Sacrifice, only the 2nd concelebrant takes the holy diskos, which he holds on his head, and the 1st -- the holy chalice; the 2nd exclaims: "All of you, Orthodox Christians," and the 1st: "Our most holy [Pontiff]." Others exclaim nothing (see no. 200). **215.** Everything else that the deacon is supposed to say or do, according to what was said about the celebration of the Liturgy without a deacon (comp. nos. 164-174), the concelebrant says and does. The one who serves the Proskomedia also cleanses the holy vessels after communion.
 812: [^781]: Here neither the deacon nor the priest (when serving alone) makes the sign of the cross with the book of the Holy Gospel, but only lifts it up (a sign for attention).
 813: [^782]: In the shortened form this part is not taken. Deacon exclaims: "Only the faithful, again and again in peace let us pray to the Lord".
 814: [^783]: No participation of all in the exit is required (see nos. 211 and 213).
 815: [^784]: Form of current diskoses does not allow to fulfill this requirement, therefore the deacon holds the diskos in his hands. **Chunk 78** **VI. Rubric of the Liturgy of Presanctified Gifts** **216.** On the Holy and Great Forty Days [Lent] at the Proskomedia of the Divine Liturgy on Sunday or on the last day before the Liturgy of Presanctified Gifts, besides the Lamb that is to be consecrated on that day, other Lambs are also prepared for those Liturgies of Presanctified Gifts that are to be celebrated on the following days. Having cut, sacrificed and pierced the first Lamb, the priest performs the same rites also over the other Lambs, reciting at each of them: "In remembrance," "As a sheep," "Sacrificed," "One of the soldiers" and places them one near another on the diskos. Then he pours wine and water into the holy chalice, having recited what is prescribed and, according to custom, finishes the Proskomedia. **217.** When the Lamb is to be blessed at the invocation of the Holy Spirit, he says: "And make this Bread" in the singular, and not in the plural, for Christ is -- only one. **218.** At the elevation he elevates simultaneously all consecrated Lambs; breaks only the first Lamb, places a part into the holy chalice and pours warm water when prescribed. After this he takes the other holy Lambs and places them in the pyx in the tabernacle. **219.** Then, according to custom, the priest recites the prayers, communicates and finishes the sacrifice according to the prescription. **1. In Concelebration of One Deacon** **220.** For the reading of the Hours, the priest in the epitrachelion stands before the holy doors and begins: "Blessed is our God." Reader: "Amen," "O Heavenly King" and the rest. After "Our Father" the priest, having said the exclamation, enters the sanctuary through the southern doors. The 3rd, 6th, 9th Hours are read, as well as the Typika. **221.** At the end of the Typika the priest and deacon vest in the sacred vestments as usual, but putting on each [vestment] they say nothing more, but only "Let us pray to the Lord." **222.** When the reader finishes the Typika, having recited the Trisagion, "Our Father," "Lord, have mercy" (12) and the prayer "Most Holy Trinity," the holy doors are opened. Priest: "Wisdom." Choir: "More honorable than the Cherubim." Priest: "Glory to Thee, O Christ God." Choir: "Glory, Both now," "Lord, have mercy" (3), "Bless." The priest makes the dismissal with the commemoration of the holy temple and the holy day. After this the holy doors are closed again. **223.** The priest accompanied by the deacon makes three small bows before the holy table and recites only: "O God, be merciful to me a sinner." They kiss, as was already noted, the Holy Gospel, the holy table and the altar cross. Then the deacon, having received permission from the priest, goes out through the northern doors and, having stood at the usual place, makes three small bows, saying nothing and says: "Bless, Master." The priest, standing before the holy table and making with the Holy Gospel the sign of the cross over it, exclaims: "Blessed is the kingdom." Choir: "Amen." Immediately the Reader: "Come, let us worship" (3) and reads the opening psalm (see nos. 102, 118, 119, note). **224.** The deacon returns into the sanctuary through the southern doors, and the priest, having stood before the holy doors, reads the Vespers (Lamp-lighting) Prayers from the fourth to the eighth, for the first three he will read later, at the Antiphons. **225.** At the end of the opening psalm the priest returns through the southern doors into the sanctuary, and the deacon, having gone out through the northern and stood at the usual place, sings the Great Litany. After the exclamation, having made a small bow, he returns through the southern doors into the sanctuary. The Reader begins the 18th Kathisma of the Psalter. At "Alleluia" -- they make small bows. When at each of the following Antiphons "Glory" is said, the deacon goes out through the northern doors from the sanctuary and at the designated place sings the Small Litany, and the priest recites quietly the first, second and third Vespers Prayers. After the completion of the Small Litany the deacon returns through the southern doors into the sanctuary, and the priest says the exclamation, as prescribed. **226.** At the beginning of the reading of the psalms [stichologia], if the Presanctified Lamb is kept in the tabernacle (artophorion) of the holy table, the transfer to the table of oblation takes place thus^[785]: the deacon brings to the holy table the holy diskos, the star-cover and the small veil. The priest kisses the Holy Gospel and places it on the right side of the holy table. After this he places the diskos on the unfolded antimension [*iliton*], on its left side, and, having opened the tabernacle, makes a small bow. He takes the chalice with the lid, in which the Lamb is kept, places it on the middle of the antimension [*iliton*] and, having taken from it the Presanctified Bread, places it with great piety on the holy diskos, as also the particles needed for the communion of the faithful. Having placed the pyx back into the tabernacle, he closes it and, having placed the holy diskos on the middle of the antimension [*iliton*], censes the star-cover and the small veil and covers the diskos with it. Having taken the censer, he censes around the holy table, preceded by the deacon with a lighted candle. Having returned before the holy table and given the censer to the deacon, he makes a low (prostrate) bow, making the sign of the cross on himself, after which he takes with both hands the covered holy diskos and, holding it on his head (see no. 129, note) crosses by the right side of the holy table to the table of oblation (altar of preparation), preceded by the deacon with a lighted candle and censer. **227.** At the table of oblation the priest places the diskos on the unfolded antimension [*iliton*], after which he pours wine and water into the chalice, as is the custom, saying nothing at this. After censing the veil of the chalice over the censer he covers the chalice with it. Then with the large veil, which he likewise censes, he covers the diskos and chalice, saying nothing at this, but only: "Through the prayers of our holy fathers, Lord Jesus Christ our God, have mercy on us." Having made a prostrate bow, the priest and deacon return to the holy table. There the priest places the Book of the Holy Gospels on the folded antimension [*iliton*]. **228.** If the Presanctified Lamb is kept in the tabernacle which is located on the table of oblation, then at the beginning of the reading of the psalms [stichologia] the priest and deacon go to the table of oblation. Both make a small bow before it, the priest opens the tabernacle and, having made again a small bow, censes with three swings the Presanctified Gifts. Then he takes the Presanctified Bread from the pyx and places it with great piety on the diskos, and pours into the holy chalice, according to custom, wine and water, saying nothing. He takes the censer, censes the star-cover and veils, covers the diskos and chalice, each -- with its own veil and both -- with the large veil (aer), saying nothing, but only: "Through the prayers of the holy fathers." Having made a prostrate bow, he returns to the holy table. **229.** If the priest deems it appropriate, he finishes the rite of placing the Lamb on the diskos during the reading of the first Antiphon, the censing -- during the second, and the transfer of the Presanctified Gifts -- during the reading of the third Antiphon. **230.** If a larger number of faithful is expected for communion, so that the Presanctified Bread alone will not suffice, the priest places the appropriate number of already consecrated particles on the diskos, and on top of them -- the Lamb Itself (see no. 114). **231.** After the completion of the reading of the psalms [stichologia] the choir begins the psalm "Lord, I have cried," and the deacon censes according to the prescription (see no. 33), at this he censes the Presanctified Gifts -- three times, each time -- with three swings. **232.** During the singing of "Glory, Both now" the holy doors are opened and the Entrance takes place in the usual manner. The deacon censes, if there be an Entrance with the Gospel, and makes the Entrance with the Gospel. **233.** When the deacon says in a low voice: "Let us pray to the Lord," the priest recites quietly the Prayer of the Entrance with its exclamation and, after the completion of the stichera, the deacon exclaims: "Wisdom, arise." Choir: "O Gladsome Light." They enter the sanctuary, then the deacon, turned to the holy doors, says: "Let us be attentive." The priest, having turned to the people, blesses: "Peace be to all." Deacon: "Wisdom, let us be attentive." The choir sings the Prokeimenon of the first Paremia. Deacon: "Wisdom." Reader, having stood in the middle between the two choirs and looking to the east: "The reading from the Book of Genesis." Deacon: "Let us be attentive." The Reader reads the first Paremia. After this the choir sings the second Prokeimenon. **234.** Immediately after the second Prokeimenon the deacon says to the priest: "Command," and the priest takes with both hands the lighted candle and simultaneously the censer, stands before the holy table, looking to the east and, making the sign of the cross, exclaims: "Wisdom, arise." After this he turns to the west, towards the people, makes again the sign of the cross and says in a raised voice: "The Light of Christ illumines all." At these words all who are in the sanctuary and in the church make three great prostrations. The priest turns again to the east and gives the candle and censer to the server. Reader: "The reading from the Book of Proverbs." Deacon: "Let us be attentive." The holy doors are closed and the second Paremia is read. **235.** After the completion of the second Paremia the priest says to the reader: "Peace be to thee," and the deacon: "Wisdom, let us be attentive." After this the deacon, having taken a lighted candle, approaches the priest. The Reader, who stands in the middle between the two choirs, or rather the priest, who stands in the sanctuary before the holy table and censes, sings: "Let my prayer be set forth." After the singing of this verse by the reader or priest, the choir sings it once more. Then again the reader or priest, who now, accompanied by the deacon going in front, stands on the southern side of the holy table and censes there, sings the first verse of the 140th Psalm: "Lord, I have cried," and the choir repeats: "Let my prayer be set forth." And again the reader or priest, accompanied by the deacon, stands at the east of the holy table, censes there and sings the second verse of the psalm: "Set, O Lord, a watch before my mouth," and the choir sings: "Let my prayer be set forth." After this the reader or priest, preceded by the deacon, stands on the northern side of the holy table, censes there and sings the third verse of the psalm: "Incline not my heart," and the choir sings: "Let my prayer be set forth." And once more the reader or priest accompanied by the deacon, again stands before the throne, censes there and sings: "Let my prayer be set forth as incense before Thee," and the choir finishes: "the lifting up of my hands as an evening sacrifice." **236.** It should be noted that during the singing by the reader or priest of "Let my prayer be set forth" or the verse, the priest censes the holy table with three swings at the beginning and at the end of each verse which he sings. At this time the choir and the faithful pray on their knees. When the choir sings the priest, having given the censer to the server, and all who are in the sanctuary, pray likewise on their knees. After the completion all bow three times. **237.** If on these days of Lent falls the memory of a certain saint or a temple feast, having opened the holy doors, the deacon exclaims: "Let us be attentive," and the reader reads the Prokeimenon of the Apostle, after which the Apostle and Gospel are read, as prescribed. **238.** The holy doors are closed and the deacon, having received permission from the priest, goes out through the northern doors and, having stood at the designated place, sings the litany "Let us all say." Everything else takes place according to the prescription until the very exclamation of the prayer for the catechumens, after which the priest, having laid aside the Gospel, unfolds the antimension [*iliton*] on the holy table. **239.** From Wednesday of the fourth week of Great Lent, which is the midpoint of the Forty Days, after the exclamation "That with us they also," the deacon dismisses the catechumens, and having invited to prayer those preparing for holy baptism: "All catechumens, depart. Catechumens, depart. All who are for illumination, approach" and so it is sung at all services of the Presanctified, even if a feast day fell, with the exception of Saturday and Sunday. After this follow the prayers of the faithful, according to the prescription. **240.** After the exclamation "According to the gift of Thy Christ" Choir: "Amen" and sings the hymn "Now the Powers of Heaven." The deacon, having returned through the northern doors into the sanctuary, opens the holy doors and, having taken the censer, censes with three swings only the front of the throne, then -- the table of oblation and the priest. Then he stands before the throne to the right of the priest and holds the censer on the ring finger of his left hand. The priest and deacon, with hands raised up, recite together "Now the Powers of Heaven" three times, each time making a small bow. **241.** Then they go directly to the table of oblation. There the priest, having taken the censer, censes with three swings the Presanctified Gifts, saying nothing at this, takes the large veil (aer) and places it on the left shoulder of the deacon, then takes the covered holy diskos with his right hand and holds it on his head, and the chalice with wine -- with his left hand at his chest (see no. 129, note). **242.** If, however, the diskos should not have a foot, the priest places it on the covered chalice, which he holds with his left hand, and with his right hand holds the veil over the holy diskos and carries the chalice like a diskos to his forehead. **243.** They go out of the sanctuary through the northern doors, in front walks the deacon, who frequently censes the Holy Gifts. During the procession no one says anything. When they enter through the holy doors into the sanctuary, the priest places the holy diskos on the throne on the left, and the holy chalice -- on the right side, removes the small veils from the diskos and chalice and places them on the holy table, and with the *aer*, which he takes from the shoulder of the deacon and censes over the censer, covers the Holy Gifts, saying nothing, but only censing the Holy Gifts thrice. After the completion of the hymn "Now the Powers of Heaven" all make three great prostrations, after which the holy doors are closed and the curtain is drawn shut. **244.** The deacon, having bowed to the priest, goes out through the northern doors and, having stood at the usual place, exclaims: "Let us complete," "Help us, save us, have mercy." The priest exclaims: "And vouchsafe us, O Master," and the people: "Our Father." The deacon girds himself with the orarion crosswise, as at the Liturgy of Chrysostom. **245.** According to the prescription follows the bowing of heads, and after the prayer "Look down, O Lord Jesus Christ" the priest and deacon make three small bows, after which the priest does not uncover the Holy Gifts, but, placing his right hand under the *aer*, touches the Life-giving Bread piously and with fear, and at the words of the deacon "Let us be attentive" exclaims: "The Presanctified Holy Things to the holy." Then the priest removes the *aer* and, having folded it, places it aside, as also the star-cover. The deacon enters through the southern doors into the sanctuary, stands to the right of the priest and, having made a small bow, says: "Break, Master, the Holy Bread," and the priest breaks it and places the four parts on the diskos just as it takes place at the Liturgy of Chrysostom, and the particle with the inscription "IC" he places into the holy chalice, saying nothing. The deacon pours a little warm water into the chalice, if there exists a custom, saying nothing and stands somewhat to the side. The choir sings the Communion Hymn "Taste and see," and also a second one, if the Apostle and Gospel of some saint or temple saint were read. **246.** The priest and deacon communicate according to custom of the Holy Bread. Then the priest wipes his fingers with a sponge, if there is a custom to use it, and, having kissed it, places it on its place. The deacon wipes the holy chalice, saying nothing and, having made three small bows, after the curtain of the iconostasis has been drawn open, opens the holy doors. Having received the chalice from the priest, he approaches the holy doors and, lifting it, shows it to the people, saying: "Draw near." Choir: "I will bless the Lord at all times. Alleluia." The communion of the faithful takes place just as at the Liturgy of Chrysostom, and the priest, giving the Holy Bread, says the words of this Liturgy "The precious and most holy." The transfer of the holy diskos takes place just as at the Liturgy of Chrysostom. The priest makes a small bow, takes the holy chalice, turns to the holy doors, looking at the people, says quietly: "Blessed is God," and then exclaims: "Always, now and ever." **247.** Everything else takes place just as at the Liturgy of Chrysostom. However, it should be noted that: 1) at the dismissal of this Liturgy the author is not mentioned; 2) in the three first days of Passion Week one must say the dismissal of Palm Sunday at Vespers: "Christ, our true God, Who came to His voluntary Passion." After the completion of the Liturgy of Presanctified Gifts the priest and deacon take off the holy vestments, saying nothing. **2. In Concelebration of Two Deacons** **248.** After the completion of the Hours and after the dismissal at the end of the Typika the holy doors are closed, the priest and deacons make before the holy table three small bows each, saying: "O God, be merciful to me a sinner" and kiss the Holy Gospel, the edge of the holy table and the altar cross, as usual. After this the 1st deacon, having paid respect to the priest, goes out through the northern doors and, having stood at his place before the holy doors, makes three small bows, saying nothing, after which he exclaims: "Bless, Master." Priest: "Blessed is the kingdom." Choir: "Amen" and the reader reads the opening psalm. The priest, having gone out through the northern doors, reads the Vespers Prayers, from the fourth to the eighth. At the end of the opening psalm the 1st deacon goes out through the northern doors and sings the Great Litany. After the exclamation "For to Thee belongs" the deacon returns into the sanctuary. **249.** The first deacon assists the priest during the placing of the Presanctified Lamb on the diskos and its transfer to the table of oblation, and the 2nd deacon goes out through the northern doors and sings the first Small Litany. The 1st deacon sings -- the second and finally the 2nd deacon -- the third. **250.** The censing on the psalm "Lord, I have cried" and the entrance take place just as at Vespers in concelebration with two deacons (see no. 39). Having returned into the sanctuary, the 1st deacon exclaims from the holy doors: "Let us be attentive." The priest, turned to the people: "Peace be to all." 2nd deacon: "Wisdom, let us be attentive." The choir sings the Prokeimenon of the first Paremia. 1st deacon: "Wisdom." Reader: "The reading from the Book of Genesis." 2nd deacon: "Let us be attentive." The Reader reads the first Paremia, after which the choir sings the second Prokeimenon. **251.** After the second Prokeimenon the 1st deacon, turning to the priest, says: "Command." The priest takes the candle and censer and makes the sign of the holy cross, as was said above. Reader: "The reading from the Book of Proverbs." 2nd deacon: "Let us be attentive." **252.** After the second reading of the Old Testament both deacons go before the priest when he censes the holy table and sings: "Let my prayer be set forth" with the verses of the 140th Psalm. **253.** If the memory of some saint or a temple feast falls, the 2nd deacon exclaims: "Let us be attentive." After the Prokeimenon of the Apostle the 1st deacon: "Wisdom." After the reading by the reader of the title of the Apostle the 2nd deacon: "Let us be attentive." After the completion of the reading of the Apostle the priest says: "Peace be to thee." 1st deacon: "Wisdom, let us be attentive." Choir sings "Alleluia". The censing before the Gospel takes place just as at the Liturgy of Chrysostom in concelebration of two deacons (see no. 155). Then the 1st deacon: "Bless, Master, the proclaimer." Priest: "May God, through the prayers" and gives him the Gospel. 2nd deacon: "Wisdom, arise, let us hear the Holy Gospel." Priest: "Peace be to all." 1st deacon, having stood on the ambo or somewhat before the holy doors: "The reading from the Holy Gospel according to (Name)." 2nd deacon: "Let us be attentive" and everything else, as is customary. **254.** After the reading of the Gospel the deacons, having gone out through their doors, stand at the designated places. 1st deacon begins: "Let us all say." Then 2nd deacon: "Pray, ye catechumens." 1st deacon: "All catechumens." 2nd deacon: "Catechumens, depart" and again 1st deacon: "Only the faithful." From the Wednesday of the fourth week of Lent they sing thus, as is given further. 1st deacon: "All catechumens." 2nd deacon: "Catechumens, depart." Again 1st deacon: "All who are for illumination, approach. Pray, ye who are for illumination." Choir: "Lord, have mercy," and the 1st deacon: "Ye faithful, for the brethren who are preparing for holy illumination." Priest -- exclamation: "For Thou art our enlightenment." 1st deacon: "All who are for illumination, depart." Again 1st deacon: "Only the faithful." Then 1st deacon: "Help us, save us, have mercy," "Wisdom." 2nd deacon: "Again and again," "Help us, save us, have mercy," "Wisdom." The deacons enter through their doors into the sanctuary. **255.** During the singing of the hymn "Now the Powers of Heaven" the holy doors are opened and the deacons, having taken censers, cense with three swings (thrice) only the front of the holy table, then -- the table of oblation and the priest. After this they stand to the right and left of the priest, holding the censers on one of the fingers of the left hand, and recite with the priest three times the hymn "Now the Powers of Heaven." Then they go straight to the table of oblation. There the priest censes the Presanctified [Gifts] and, having taken the *aer*, places it on the left shoulder of the 1st deacon, and all go out in the usual manner. In front go both deacons and frequently cense the Holy Gifts. **256.** After the holy diskos and the holy chalice are placed on the holy table, the deacons go out through their doors and stand at the usual places. 1st deacon exclaims: "Let us complete." At "Our Father" the deacons gird themselves with the oraria crosswise. 2nd deacon: "Bow our heads unto the Lord." After three small bows the 1st deacon exclaims "Let us be attentive" and after the exclamation of the priest "The Presanctified Holy Things to the holy" both deacons return through their doors into the sanctuary. 1st deacon: "Break, Master, the Holy Bread." The deacons communicate of the Holy Bread, according to custom. After the communion of the priest and deacons, the 1st deacon wipes the holy diskos over the holy chalice and calls: "Draw near." The rest takes place just as at the Liturgy of Chrysostom. **3. Without a Deacon** **257.** If this Liturgy is celebrated without a deacon, the priest exclaims everything that belongs to the deacon, as has already been said in the rubric of Vespers and the Divine Liturgy of John Chrysostom. **258.** When the priest censes the holy table and transfers the Holy Gifts to the table of oblation, the server, holding a lighted candle, walks before him. Small litanies and exclamations the priest says, if possible, before the holy table. **259.** During the singing of "Let my prayer be set forth" the server walks with a lighted candle before the priest. **260.** At the Great Entrance candle-bearers, if there be such, turned to the northern doors and arranged in order, accompany the Presanctified Lamb. After they arrive before the holy doors they stand together on both sides, and then return to their places. **4. In Concelebration of Priests** **261.** The rules of concelebration of the Liturgy of Presanctified Gifts -- are the same as of Vespers and the Liturgy of Chrysostom. Only one must keep in mind that: -- At the end of the Typika concelebrants vest in sacred vestments, saying when putting on each only: "Let us pray to the Lord." -- The principal celebrant exclaims: "For to Thee belongs," "For a merciful," "According to the gift of Thy Christ," "For Thou art our sanctification." Other exclamations are exclaimed by concelebrants in turn. -- At "Let my prayer be set forth" concelebrants remain in their places, stepping back slightly from the holy table when the principal celebrant needs to pass, together with the principal [celebrant] they bend their knees and rise. -- At the Great Entrance the celebrants carry nothing, however the 1st concelebrant may carry the chalice before the principal celebrant.
 816: [^785]: I corrected it (Dutka Ivan), because here it was written "does not happen", but this is an incorrect translation.
```

```text
 192: Note: The *Octoechos* is not used.
 193: #### 2.5.1 AT Great Vespers
 194: ##### 2.5.1.1 Kathisma *“Blessed is the man”* (according to the Typikon - only the 1st antiphon)
 195: ##### 2.5.1.2 On *“Lord, I have cried”* - 6 stichera[^130] or 8[^131], all to the saint. Glory: to the saint, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the current tone, in view of its Apodosis. Prokeimenon of the day from the *Horologion* and three readings to the saint
 196: ##### 2.5.1.3 Aposticha whole to the saint, with his refrains. To the Doxastikon of the saint the Theotokion is selected from the Sunday Aposticha in the tone of the Doxastikon[^132]
 197: ##### 2.5.1.4 At the end: Troparion of the saint, Glory, Both now: Theotokion from the Sunday ones in the tone of the saint's troparion[^133]

 199: #### 2.5.2 AT COMPLINE
 200: Canon of the Theotokos from the *Octoechos* of the current tone[^134]. After *“It is truly meet”* with the Trisagion - Kontakion to the saint alone[^135].
 201: #### 2.5.3 AT Great Matins

 203: ##### 2.5.3.2 Kathismata - two current with Sessional Hymns of the saint, also Kathisma 19, that is Polyeleos with Magnifications and the Post-Polyeleos Sessional Hymn of the saint
 204: ##### 2.5.3.3 Gradual of Tone 4, first antiphon
 205: ##### 2.5.3.4 Prokeimenon, Gospel and Sticheron to the saint
 206:   * The Typikon of the Pochaiv *Anthologion*, instead of "Through the prayers of the holy Apostles" gives: "Through the prayers of the saint (name), whose memory is celebrated (See the service of a prophet). So gives also the Greek-Venetian *Menaion* (See e. g. January 11, 25, 27, 30). However, general editions do not give this.
 207: ##### 2.5.3.5 Canons two: 1st - of the Theotokos, one of the two usual ones ("Having traversed the moisture", Tone 2 of Sunday Matins, or "Having crossed the water", Tone 8 of Compline on Tuesday) with the Heirmos on 6, then to the saint one or two canons on 8[^136]
 208:   * On Saturday, if the temple is of the Lord or of the Theotokos, the canon of the temple is taken with the Heirmos on 6, Heirmos - twice, and to the saint on 8[^137].

 211: ##### 2.5.3.7 After the Great Doxology with the Trisagion - Troparion to the saint, Glory, Both now: Theotokion from the Sunday ones in the tone of the saint's troparion

 215: ## 2.6 Saint with an All-Night Vigil on a Sunday
 216: AT SMALL VESPERS
 217: ##### 2.6.1 On *“Lord, I have cried”*: stichera - 4, all Sunday of the current tone of the *Octoechos*; also Glory: sticheron to the saint, Both now: Theotokion of the tone of Small Vespers[^138] that is 1st Theotokion of the tone[^139], which is called Dogmatikon[^140]
 218: ##### 2.6.2 On the Aposticha stichera - 4, that is: one Sunday, which is in the first place in the *Octoechos* of the current tone and 3 to the saint with two of his refrains, which are on the Aposticha of Great Vespers[^141], also Glory: to the saint from his Small Vespers, Both now: Theotokion from the Aposticha of Small Vespers[^142]
 219: ##### 2.6.3 At the end: Sunday Troparion, Glory: to the saint, Both now: Theotokion from the Sunday ones in the tone of the saint's troparion
 220: ##### 2.6.4 Dismissal with the commemoration of the Sunday and of the saint
 221: #### 2.6.1 AT Great Vespers
 222: ##### 2.6.1.1 Kathisma 1 *“Blessed is the man”* (according to the Typikon - whole, according to our custom today - only certain selected verses)
 223: ##### 2.6.1.2 On *“Lord, I have cried”* stichera - 10, that is 4 from the *Octoechos* and 6 to the saint, Glory: to the saint, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the current tone
 224: ##### 2.6.1.3 Prokeimenon of the day from the *Horologion* and 3 readings to the saint
 225: ##### 2.6.1.4 On the Litiya: according to the Slavonic Typikon, first sticheron - of the temple (which today we usually do not take), also stichera to the saint. Glory: to the saint, Both now: Theotokion from the Sunday Aposticha of Great Vespers, in the tone of the Doxastikon[^153][^144][^143]
 226: ##### 2.6.1.5 On the Aposticha: stichera of the Sunday tone, Glory: to the saint, Both now: Theotokion from the Sunday Aposticha of Great Vespers, in the tone of the Doxastikon
 227: ##### 2.6.1.6 At the Blessing of Loaves: Troparion "O Virgin Theotokos" twice and to the saint once[^227][^145]
 228: #### 2.6.2 AT Great Matins
 229: ##### 2.6.2.1 On *“God is the Lord”*: Sunday Troparion twice, Glory: to the saint, Both now: Theotokion from the Sunday ones in the tone of the saint's troparion
 230: ##### 2.6.2.2 Two current kathismata with their Sunday Sessional Hymns of the *Octoechos*; also Kathisma 19 (Polyeleos) with Magnifications and "The Angelic Host", and Hypakoe of the tone, and immediately all three Sessional Hymns of the saint, that is 1st and 2nd without Theotokion, then Glory: 2nd Sessional Hymn, which is called the Polyeleos one, Both now: its Theotokion[^147]
 231: ##### 2.6.2.3 Gradual, Prokeimenon, Gospel and Sticheron, all only Resurrection Sunday
 232:   * During the singing of the canon, by our custom, the Priest anoints the people with oil blessed at Vespers.
 233: ##### 2.6.2.4 Canons three or four on 14, namely: Sunday with Heirmos on 4 and of the Theotokos on 2, and to the saint on 8, there will be two or only one canon; for usually the saint has two canons[^148]
 234: Katavasia current after every Ode. After the 3rd Ode - Kontakion-Ikos, and Sessional Hymn to the saint. After the 6th - Kontakion-Ikos Sunday, after the 9th - Sunday Exapostilarion, Glory: to the saint, Both now: Theotokion of the Sunday Exapostilarion
 235: Everything else at Matins, at the Hours and at the Liturgy so, as with a Polyeleos saint, here on page 73.

 237: ## 2.7 Saint with an All-Night Vigil on Weekdays and Saturday
 238: AT SMALL VESPERS
 239: ##### 2.7.1 On *“Lord, I have cried”* and on the Aposticha all stichera - to the saint, on the Aposticha there will be separate refrains to the saint. Only regarding the Theotokia on *“Lord, I have cried”* and on the Aposticha let it be known, that they sometimes will be special[^150], sometimes only general, designated only by the first words; sometimes even without indication of the first words. And in this last case, we think that they should be selected from the *Octoechos* on Daily Vespers in the tone of the Doxastikon and of the day of the week, which are given at the end of every volume of the *Menaion* and of the Lviv *Anthologion*; if - not, then in the tone of one of the three Doxastika, given at the end of the Pochaiv *Anthologion*[^151]
 240: ##### 2.7.2 At the end: Troparion of the saint, Glory, Both now: Theotokion from the Sunday ones in the tone of the saint's troparion
 241: #### 2.7.1 AT Great Vespers
 242: 1.	*“Blessed is the man”* (according to the Typikon - only the 1st antiphon).
 243: ##### 2.7.1.1 On *“Lord, I have cried”*: stichera of the saint on 8, Glory: His Doxastikon, Both now: 1st Theotokion (Dogmatikon), in the tone of the Doxastikon; on Friday for Saturday - Dogmatikon of the current tone[^152], in view of the Apodosis of the tone
 244: ##### 2.7.1.2 Prokeimenon of the day from the *Horologion* and 3 readings to the saint
 245: ##### 2.7.1.3 On the Litiya: first sticheron - of the temple, which today we usually do not take, all the rest - to the saint and Glory: to the saint, Both now: Theotokion or special, if there be, or general from the Aposticha of Sunday Great Vespers, in the tone of the Doxastikon[^153]
 246: ##### 2.7.1.4 On the Aposticha all stichera - to the saint, with his two refrains; Theotokion to the Doxastikon, if there be no special one, is taken from the Sunday Aposticha in the tone of the Doxastikon[^154]
 247: ##### 2.7.1.5 At the Blessing of Loaves: Troparion of the saint twice and "O Virgin Theotokos" once
 248: AT Great Matins, AT THE HOURS AND AT THE LITURGY
 249: Everything so, as in the case of a Polyeleos saint without All-Night (see page 75-76); only Matins begins from "Glory to the Holy", and there will be anointing with oil during the canon, according to custom.
 250: Note
 251: Three feasts, namely: The Nativity and Beheading of St. John the Baptist on June 24 and August 29 and of the Chief Apostles Peter and Paul on June 29 surpass other saints with All-Night Vigil in that at Matins their canons are taken alone, without the Theotokion canon, and at the Liturgy their Apostle-Gospels are taken alone[^155], without the daily ones, which are read on the previous day under the refrain, except for Sundays, for these always precede. According to today's general custom, except for cathedral churches, on other saints too the daily Apostle-Gospels are not read. To these three feasts the Moscow Typikon adds also the feast of John the Theologian and the Feast of the temple[^156].
 252: CASES OF FEASTS
 253: ## 2.8 Forefeast with a Saint without a Polyeleos on a Sunday
 254: Note: If two saints with a Forefeast fall on a Sunday, then the service of the first (second) is transferred to another day, according to the decision of the Ecclesiarch[^157].
 255: #### 2.8.1 AT Great Vespers
 256: 1.	*“Blessed is the man”* (according to the Typikon - all three antiphons).
 257: ##### 2.8.1.1 On *“Lord, I have cried”* - 10 stichera, that is: of the *Octoechos* of the current tone - 4, of the Forefeast - 3 and to the saint - 3. Glory: of the Forefeast, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the tone. If there be a Doxastikon to the saint, then having discarded the Doxastikon of the Forefeast, Glory: Doxastikon to the saint is taken, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the tone[^158]
 258:   * **If the saint be on 6**, then there will be of the Sunday - 3, of the Forefeast - 3 and to the saint - 4, Glory: to the saint, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the tone[^159].
 259: ##### 2.8.1.2 On the Aposticha: stichera Sunday, Glory, Both now: of the Forefeast. If there be a Doxastikon to the saint, then after it at "Both now" is taken of the Forefeast
 260: ##### 2.8.1.3 At the end: Sunday Troparion, Glory: of the saint, Both now: of the Forefeast
 261: 5.	the Great Dismissal with the commemoration of the Sunday service and of the saint[^160].
 262: AT COMPLINE: After *“It is truly meet”* - Kontakion of the Forefeast alone[^161].
 263: AT THE Midnight Office: Trinitarian Canon of the current tone and everything else, as usual.
 264: #### 2.8.2 AT Great Matins
 265: ##### 2.8.2.1 On *“God is the Lord”*: Sunday Troparion twice, Glory: to the saint, Both now: of the Forefeast
 266: ##### 2.8.2.2 Everything else up to the canon - Sunday, as usual
 267: ##### 2.8.2.3 Canons 4 on 14, that is: first - Sunday of the *Octoechos* with Heirmos on 4 and second - of the *Octoechos* of the Theotokos on 2, also of the Forefeast on 4 and of the saint on 4[^162]. (If the saint - on 6, then here is taken only on 4). Katavasia after every Ode - current. After the 3rd Ode - Kontakion-Ikos of the Forefeast and of the saint, Glory: Sessional Hymn of the saint, Both now: of the Forefeast. After the 6th Ode - Kontakion-Ikos Sunday. After the 9th - "Holy is the Lord our God" thrice and Sunday Exapostilarion, Glory: of the saint, Both now: of the Forefeast[^163]
 268: ##### 2.8.2.4 Praises stichera - 8, that is: of the *Octoechos* - 4 and to the saint - 4, if he has, with two separate refrains of his; if the saint does not have, then of the feast on 4 (from the Aposticha with their refrains); also Glory: sticheron of the feast, Both now: "Most Blessed Art Thou"[^164]
 269: ##### 2.8.2.5 After the Doxology - Sunday Troparion, one of two usual ones
 270: 6.	the Great Dismissal, as at Vespers.
 271: #### 2.8.3 AT THE HOURS
 272: At all: Sunday Troparion, also Glory: at the 1st and 3rd - also of the Forefeast, at the 6th and 9th - also to the saint. Kontakion, Sunday and of the feast, we say alternatingly, that is at the 1st and at the 6th - of the Forefeast, and at the 3rd and 9th - Sunday[^165].
 273: #### 2.8.4 AT THE LITURGY
 274: All service - only of the Sunday, except Troparia, for they are taken also of the Forefeast with the Sunday ones, that is Sunday and of the Forefeast, Glory: Sunday Kontakion, Both now: of the Forefeast[^166].

 277: ## 2.9 Forefeast with a Saint without a Polyeleos on Weekdays and Saturday
 278: Notes
 279: ##### 2.9.1 Beginning from the very Forefeast until the Apodosis of the feast, the service of the *Octoechos*, with the exception of Sunday, is not taken and, instead of it, the service of the feast is taken in the first place, likewise also on Saturday; it is combined together with the service of the current saint, except for the Apodosis, for then the service of the saint is transferred to another day. Only at Compline is the Canon of the Theotokos of the *Octoechos* taken
 280: ##### 2.9.2 The Divine Service is celebrated in a lesser form, that is Vespers and Matins - daily
 281: ##### 2.9.3 The sequence of stichera and troparia does not end with usual *Octoechos* Theotokia, but festal ones; with the exception of Friday evening for Saturday, in view of the Apodosis of the tone, usually the 1st Theotokion of the tone is taken
 282: AT VESPERS
 283: ##### 2.9.4 Kathisma current
 284: ##### 2.9.5 On *“Lord, I have cried”* - 6 stichera, that is: of the Forefeast - 3 and to the saint - 3, Glory, Both now: of the Forefeast, or Glory: to the saint, if he has, Both now: of the Forefeast
 285:   * **If two saints occur**, then there will be to the first - 3, to the second - 3, also Glory, Both now: of the Forefeast. Stichera of the Forefeast then are none[^167].
 286:   * **If a saint on 6 occurs**, then also there will be stichera of the Forefeast - 3 and to the saint - 3, as with a saint on 4[^168].
 287: On Friday evening for Saturday: Dogmatikon of the tone, which is being taken leave of.
 288: ##### 2.9.6 On the Aposticha: stichera of the Forefeast; if Glory be to the saint, then Both now: of the Forefeast
 289: ##### 2.9.7 At the end: Troparion to the saint, Glory, Both now: of the Forefeast
 290:   * **If two saints occur**, then first the troparion of the first saint, Glory: of the second, Both now: of the Forefeast.
 291: ##### 2.9.8 Dismissal medium with the commemoration of the service of the day and of the saint[^169]
 292: #### 2.9.1 AT COMPLINE
 293: Canon of the Theotokos of the current week in the *Octoechos*. After *“It is truly meet”* with the Trisagion - Kontakion of the Forefeast alone[^170].
 294: AT THE Midnight Office: Everything exactly so, as in the *Horologion*, to the saint - nothing.
 295: AT MATINS
 296: ##### 2.9.1.1 On *“God is the Lord”*: Troparion of the Forefeast twice, Glory: to the saint, Both now: of the Forefeast
 297:   * **If two saints occur**, then there will be the Troparion of the Forefeast once, also to the first saint once, Glory: to the second once, Both now: of the Forefeast[^171].
 298: ##### 2.9.1.2 Kathismata two current with Sessional Hymns of the Forefeast
 299: ##### 2.9.1.3 Canons 2 on 12, that is: of the Forefeast with Heirmos on 8 and of the saint on 4[^172]. Katavasia after the 3rd, 6th, 8th and 9th Ode - Heirmos of the last canon, that is of the saint[^173]. After the 3rd Ode - Kontakion-Ikos and Sessional Hymn of the saint, Glory, Both now: of the Forefeast, after the 6th - Kontakion-Ikos of the Forefeast, after the 9th - Exapostilarion of the saint, if the saint has one, if - not, then only of the Forefeast (December 29, January 2), Glory, Both now: of the Forefeast[^174]
 300:   * **If two saints occur**, then there will be 3 canons on 14, that is: of the Forefeast with Heirmos on 6, also of the first saint on 4[^175] and of the second on 4. Katavasia - after the 3rd, 6th, 8th and 9th Ode - Heirmos of the last canon, that is of the second saint[^176]. After the 3rd Ode - Kontakion-Ikos of the first and second saint[^177], also Sessional Hymn of the first, Glory, Both now: of the Forefeast; after the 6th - Kontakion-Ikos of the Forefeast; after the 9th - Exapostilarion of the first saint, Glory: of the second, if he has, Both now: of the Forefeast (e. g. November 2).
 301:   * **If the saint be on 6**, then the Canon of the Forefeast on 6 and to the saint on 6 (December 20)[^178].
 302: ##### 2.9.1.4 On the Aposticha: stichera of the Forefeast, Glory: to the saint, if he has, Both now: of the Forefeast, if - not, then Glory, Both now: of the Forefeast
 303: ##### 2.9.1.5 At the end: Troparion of the saint, Glory, Both now: of the Forefeast
 304:   * If there be two saints, then the troparion of the first, Glory: of the second, Both now: of the Forefeast.
 305: #### 2.9.2 AT THE HOURS
 306: At all: Troparion of the Forefeast, also at the 3rd and 9th also Glory: to the saint, Kontakia - alternating, that is: at the 1st and 6th - of the Forefeast, at the 3rd and 9th - to the saint.
 307:   * If there be two saints, then at the 3rd after Glory - Troparion to the first saint, and at the 9th - to the second; Kontakia: at the 3rd - to the first, at the 9th - to the second saint[^179].
 308: #### 2.9.3 AT THE LITURGY
 309: By our custom today: Troparion, Glory, Both now: Kontakion of the Forefeast, everything else - of the day[^180].
 310: ## 2.10 Feast of the Lord on a Sunday and Weekdays
 311: All service - only of the feast, of the great type with All-Night Vigil.
 312: AT SMALL VESPERS
 313: On *“Lord, I have cried”*: stichera of the feast on 4 and Aposticha of the feast with two refrains of the feast, and At the end - Troparion of the feast one.
 314: #### 2.10.1 AT Great Vespers
 315: ##### 2.10.1.1 Kathismata usually none; only on Saturday for Sunday - Kathisma *“Blessed is the man”*, according to the Typikon - all three antiphons; on Sunday for Monday - only the first antiphon
 316: ##### 2.10.1.2 On *“Lord, I have cried”*: stichera of the feast on 8
 317: ##### 2.10.1.3 Prokeimenon of the day; only, if the feast falls on a Saturday, then, instead of the daily Prokeimenon, the Great Prokeimenon of the feast is taken, given on Vespers of the next day. In this case, Vespers of the next day will be on Saturday for Sunday, which has the Great Prokeimenon *“The Lord is King”*, which does not yield to the Prokeimenon of the feast. This Vespers, therefore, is already not of the feast itself, but of the Afterfeast and therefore it cannot exclude the Sunday service, which occupies the first place. In order not to discard the Prokeimenon of the feast, it is taken before that on Great Vespers of the feast itself, namely on Friday[^181]
 318: ##### 2.10.1.4 Three readings of the feast
 319: ##### 2.10.1.5 On the Litiya and on the Aposticha - stichera of the feast
 320: ##### 2.10.1.6 At the Blessing of Loaves - Troparion of the feast thrice
 321: #### 2.10.2 AT Great Matins
 322: ##### 2.10.2.1 On *“God is the Lord”*: Troparion of the feast twice, Glory, Both now: once more
 323: ##### 2.10.2.2 Kathismata two current with Sessional Hymns of the feast, also Kathisma 19 (Polyeleos) and Magnifications, and the Post-Polyeleos Sessional Hymn of the feast
 324: ##### 2.10.2.3 Gradual of Tone 4, 1st antiphon. Prokeimenon, Gospel and Sticheron of the feast
 325: ##### 2.10.2.4 Canons one or two. Troparia on 12, Heirmoi - twice. Katavasia current after every Ode. After the 3rd Ode - Sessional Hymn, after the 6th - Kontakion-Ikos, after the 9th - Exapostilarion of the feast. At the 9th Ode *“More honorable”* is not sung, but festal refrains to the Heirmoi and Troparia of the canon
 326: ##### 2.10.2.5 Praises stichera of the feast - 4, Glory, Both now: of the feast
 327: ##### 2.10.2.6 After the Great Doxology - Troparion of the feast
 328: 7.	the Great Dismissal with the commemoration of the feast.
 329: AT THE HOURS: At all hours - Troparion and Kontakion of the feast. Dismissal with the commemoration of the feast.
 330: #### 2.10.3 AT THE LITURGY
 331: Antiphons, Entrance and everything else - to the feast[^182]. Instead of the Trisagion, on the Exaltation of the Holy Cross and on the Sunday of the Adoration of the Cross we sing "Before Thy Cross"; on the Nativity of Christ, on Theophany, on Lazarus Saturday, on Great Saturday, during Bright Week and on Pentecost Sunday is sung "As many as have been baptized into Christ"[^183]. Instead of *“It is truly meet”*, according to our later Typikon, is taken the Heirmos of the 9th Ode of the Festal Canon with the festal refrain.
 332: 
 333: 
 334: ## 2.11 Feast of the Theotokos on a Sunday
 335: The service of the feast is combined with the Sunday *Octoechos*, which takes the first place.
 336: AT SMALL VESPERS
 337: ##### 2.11.1 On *“Lord, I have cried”*: 4 Sunday stichera of the current tone, Glory, Both now: of the feast
 338: ##### 2.11.2 On the Aposticha: one Sunday sticheron of the current tone, which is in the first place, also 3 stichera of the feast from the Aposticha of Great Vespers with their refrains[^184]; Glory, Both now: of the feast, from Small Vespers[^185]
 339: ##### 2.11.3 At the end: Sunday Troparion; Glory, Both now: of the feast
 340: ##### 2.11.4 Dismissal small with the commemoration Sunday and festal
 341: #### 2.11.1 AT Great Vespers
 342: ##### 2.11.1.1 Kathisma 1 (*“Blessed is the man”*), according to the Typikon - all three antiphons, by our custom today - only selected verses
 343: ##### 2.11.1.2 On *“Lord, I have cried”* - 10 stichera, namely: of the Sunday *Octoechos* - 4, which is in the first place, also of the feast - 6, Glory, Both now: of the feast[^186]
 344: ##### 2.11.1.3 Prokeimenon of the day from the *Horologion
 345: ##### 2.11.1.4 Three readings of the feast
 346: ##### 2.11.1.5 On the Litiya all stichera - of the feast
 347: ##### 2.11.1.6 On the Aposticha: stichera Sunday, Glory, Both now: of the feast
 348: ##### 2.11.1.7 At the Blessing of Loaves: Troparion of the feast thrice
 349: #### 2.11.2 AT Great Matins
 350: ##### 2.11.2.1 On *“God is the Lord”*: Sunday Troparion twice, Glory, Both now: of the feast
 351: ##### 2.11.2.2 Kathismata two current with Sunday Sessional Hymns and with their Theotokia, also Polyeleos with Magnifications, "The Angelic Host" and Hypakoe of the tone. All three Sessional Hymns of the feast, that is: 1st Sessional Hymn once, 2nd Sessional Hymn once, then Glory, Both now: 3rd Sessional Hymn, if it is double, then there will be Glory: first, Both now: second[^187]
 352: ##### 2.11.2.3 Gradual of the current tone, afterwards - "Resurrection of Christ"; everything else up to the canon - to the feast[^188]
 353: ##### 2.11.2.4 Canons 3 on 14, that is: Sunday from the *Octoechos*, with Heirmos on 4, Theotokion from the *Octoechos*, without Heirmos, on 2 and both canons of the feast, without Heirmos, on 8; if to the saint there be only one, then one is taken on 8[^189]. Katavasia current after every Ode. After the 3rd Ode - Sunday Kontakion-Ikos and Sessional Hymn of the feast (on the Dormition of the Most Holy Theotokos, instead of the Sessional Hymn, - Hypakoe of the feast); after the 6th - Kontakion-Ikos of the feast, after the 9th - Sunday Exapostilarion sequential, one of 11, then Glory, Both now: of the feast. At the 9th Ode - *“More honorable”*, festal refrains, according to the Typikon, are not taken; however, we think, that it would be better to coordinate the festal refrains with the troparion of the canon of the feast, than with the general refrain "Most Holy Theotokos, save us"[^190]
 354: ##### 2.11.2.5 Praises stichera - 8, that is: 4 Sunday and 4 of the feast with two festal refrains; Glory: of the feast, Both now: "Most Blessed Art Thou"
 355: ##### 2.11.2.6 After the Great Doxology with the Trisagion - Sunday Troparion, one of two usual ones
 356: 7.	the Great Dismissal with the commemoration Sunday and of the feast.
 357: ##### 2.11.2.7 Glory, Both now: Gospel Sticheron
 358: #### 2.11.3 AT THE HOURS
 359: At all: Sunday Troparion, Glory, Both now: of the feast. Kontakia - alternating, that is at the 1st and 6th - Sunday, at the 3rd and 9th - of the feast[^191].
 360: #### 2.11.4 AT THE LITURGY
 361: Antiphons Sunday. On "Come, let us worship", if you wish, to "Save us, O Son of God" add the refrain: "Through the prayers of the Theotokos, who sing to Thee, Alleluia"[^192]. Sunday Troparion and of the feast, Glory: Sunday Kontakion, Both now: Kontakion of the feast. Trisagion, Prokeimenon, Apostle, Alleluia, Gospel and Communion Hymn - first of the Sunday, afterwards - of the feast. Instead of *“It is truly meet”*, according to our later Slavonic custom, we sing the Heirmos of the 9th Ode of the festal canon (with its refrain)[^193].

 363: ## 2.12 Feast of the Theotokos on Weekdays
 364: Everything - according to the Typikon of a Feast of the Lord (see page 87-89), except for the Antiphons, which will be daily, and the Entrance, which will be "Come, let us worship", and the Trisagion, which always is on Theotokion feasts.
 365: 
 366: Note about the Afterfeast
 367: Everything is performed according to the Typikon of the Forefeast, given here before on page 81-83. However, in the Afterfeast there will be:
 368: ##### 2.12.1 Troparion and Kontakion of the feast itself
 369: ##### 2.12.2 At the Dismissal is commemorated also the service of the feast
 370: ##### 2.12.3 At the Liturgy, in the Afterfeast of the Lord, first two antiphons - of the feast[^194], third - usual with the refrain of the feast, also and the usual Entrance "Come, let us worship" with the same refrain of the feast[^195]
 371: ##### 2.12.4 Prokeimenon, Alleluia and Communion Hymn on Sunday - of the day (that is of the Sunday) and of the feast, on weekdays - only of the feast; Apostle and Gospel - of the day[^196]. When on Sunday the service of a saint is also taken, then the Prokeimenon, Alleluia and Communion Hymn of the feast are discarded, and only of the Sunday and of the saint are taken. On weekdays, if the service of a saint is combined with the festal service, then all this is taken in the first place - to the feast, afterwards - to the saint. But because among us to a saint without Polyeleos at the Liturgy usually nothing is taken, all this is taken only to the feast
 372: ##### 2.12.5 Instead of *“It is truly meet”* - Heirmos of the 9th Ode of the canon of the feast. However, we will present separate and full models

 374: ## 2.13 Afterfeast with a Saint without a Polyeleos on a Sunday
 375: Note: If two saints fall on a Sunday, then the service of the second saint is transferred to another day, according to the decision of the Ecclesiarch.
 376: #### 2.13.1 AT Great Vespers
 377: ##### 2.13.1.1 Kathisma usual *“Blessed is the man”* (according to the Typikon - all three antiphons)
 378: ##### 2.13.1.2 On *“Lord, I have cried”* - 10 stichera, that is: 4 from the *Octoechos* of the current tone, 3 of the Afterfeast and 3 to the saint, Glory: of the Afterfeast, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the current tone. If there be a Doxastikon to the saint, then, having discarded the Doxastikon of the feast, the Doxastikon to Him is taken, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the current tone
 379:   * If the saint falls on 6, then there will be stichera of the Sunday - 3, of the Afterfeast - 3 and to the saint - 4, Glory: to the saint, Both now: 1st Theotokion of the current tone.
 380: ##### 2.13.1.3 On the Aposticha: Sunday stichera of the *Octoechos*, Glory, Both now: of the Afterfeast
 381: ##### 2.13.1.4 At the end: Sunday Troparion, Glory: of the saint, Both now: of the Afterfeast
 382: 5.	the Great Dismissal with the commemoration of Sunday and of the saint[^197].
 383: AT COMPLINE: After *“It is truly meet”* with the Trisagion - Hypakoe of the tone, Glory, Both now: Kontakion of the feast.
 384: AT THE Midnight Office: Trinitarian Canon of the *Octoechos* of the current tone and other things, as usual.
 385: #### 2.13.2 AT Great Matins
 386: ##### 2.13.2.1 On *“God is the Lord”*: Sunday Troparion twice, Glory: to the saint, Both now: of the feast; everything else up to the Sunday Canon - as usual
 387: ##### 2.13.2.2 Canons 4 on 14: Sunday *Octoechos* with Heirmos on 4, of the Theotokos *Octoechos* on 2, of the feast on 4 and of the saint on 4
 388:   * **If the saint be on 6**, then also - on 4. Katavasia after every Ode - current. After the 3rd Ode - Kontakion-Ikos of the feast and of the saint, Glory: Sessional Hymn of the saint, Both now: of the feast. After the 6th - Kontakion-Ikos Sunday, after the 9th - *“More honorable”*, after the 9th - "Holy is the Lord our God", Sunday Exapostilarion, Glory: of the saint, Both now: of the feast.
 389: ##### 2.13.2.3 Praises stichera - 8, that is: 4 Sunday from the *Octoechos* and 4 of the feast with two of its refrains. Glory: Gospel Sticheron, Both now: "Most Blessed Art Thou"
 390:   * If the saint has Praises stichera, then stichera of the feast are not taken and, instead of them, 4 stichera are taken to the saint with two of His refrains, that is: 3 prosomia and one idiomelon, which is on Glory[^198], then Glory: Gospel Sticheron, Both now: "Most Blessed Art Thou".
 391: ##### 2.13.2.4 After the Doxology - Sunday Troparion, one of two usual ones
 392: 5.	the Great Dismissal, as at Vespers.
 393: #### 2.13.3 AT THE HOURS
 394: At all: Sunday Troparion, also Glory: at the 1st and 6th - also of the feast, at the 3rd and 9th - also to the saint. Kontakion, only Sunday and of the feast, we say alternatingly, that is: at the 1st and 6th - of the feast, at the 3rd and 9th - Sunday[^199].
 395: #### 2.13.4 AT THE LITURGY
 396: Antiphons, in the Afterfeast of a feast of the Lord, we take: two first - of the feast, third - usual with the refrain of the feast, also "Come"[^200]. In the Afterfeast of the Theotokos - Antiphons usual on all Sundays. Sunday Troparion and of the feast, Glory: Sunday Kontakion, Both now: of the feast and the Trisagion[^201]. Prokeimenon, Apostle, Alleluia, Gospel and Communion Hymn - only Sunday[^202].

 398: ## 2.14 Afterfeast with a Saint without a Polyeleos on Weekdays and Saturday
 399: AT VESPERS
 400: ##### 2.14.1 Kathisma current
 401: ##### 2.14.2 On *“Lord, I have cried”* - 6 stichera, that is: 3 of the feast and 3 to the saint, Glory, Both now: to the feast, or Glory: to the saint, if he has, Both now: of the feast
 402:   * **If two saints occur**, then there will be to the first - 3 and to the second - 3, Glory, Both now: of the feast.
 403:   * **If a saint on 6 occurs**, then the stichera to him will be only 3[^203], as also to the saint on 4.
 404: On Friday evening for Saturday - 1st Theotokion of the tone, which is being taken leave of (Dogmatikon)[^204].
 405: ##### 2.14.3 On the Aposticha: stichera of the feast, Glory: to the saint, if there be, Both now: of the feast, if - not, then Glory, Both now: of the feast
 406: ##### 2.14.4 At the end: Troparion to the saint, Glory, Both now: of the feast
 407:   * **If two saints occur**, then the troparion of the first saint, Glory: of the second, Both now: of the feast.
 408: ##### 2.14.5 Dismissal medium with the commemoration of the feast and of the saint, without commemoration of the service of the weekday, because it is not taken
 409: #### 2.14.1 AT COMPLINE
 410: Canon of the Most Holy Theotokos, according to the sequence of the *Octoechos*. After *“It is truly meet”* - Kontakion of the feast alone.
 411: AT THE Midnight Office: Everything exactly so, as in the *Horologion*.
 412: AT MATINS
 413: ##### 2.14.1.1 On *“God is the Lord”*: Troparion of the feast twice, Glory: to the saint, Both now: of the feast
 414:   * **If two saints occur**, then the troparion of the feast once and of the first saint once, Glory: of the second, Both now: again of the feast.
 415: ##### 2.14.1.2 Kathismata two current with Sessional Hymns of the feast
 416: ##### 2.14.1.3 Canons 2 on 12, that is: of the feast with Heirmos on 8 and of the saint on 4. Katavasia after the 3rd, 6th, 8th and 9th Ode - Heirmos of the last canon, that is of the saint. After the 3rd Ode - Kontakion-Ikos and Sessional Hymn of the saint; after the 6th - Kontakion-Ikos of the feast; after the 9th - Exapostilarion of the saint twice, Glory, Both now: of the feast[^205]
 417:   * **If two saints occur**, then 3 canons on 14, that is: Canon of the feast with Heirmos on 6, to the first saint on 4 and to the second on 4. Katavasia after the 3rd, 6th, 8th and 9th Ode - Heirmos of the last canon, that is of the second saint. After the 3rd Ode - Kontakion-Ikos of the first and of the second saint, also Sessional Hymn of the first saint, Glory: of the second, Both now: of the feast; after the 6th - Kontakion-Ikos of the feast; after the 9th - Exapostilarion of the first saint, Glory: of the second, Both now: of the feast.
 418:   * **If a saint on 6 occurs**, then the Canon of the feast with Heirmos on 6 and to the saint on 6[^206], everything else, as above with one saint.
 419: ##### 2.14.1.4 On the Aposticha: stichera of the feast, Glory: to the saint, if there be, Both now: of the feast, if - not, then Glory, Both now: of the feast
 420:   * If the saint on 6 will have Praises stichera with the Small Doxology, then they are taken on 4 and Glory: his, and Both now: of the feast. After the Litany "Let us complete" will be on the Aposticha stichera of the feast, Glory: to the saint, Both now: of the feast[^207]. If this saint will have also the Great Doxology, then the Praises stichera are taken: of the feast - 3 and to the saint - 3, Glory: to the saint, and Both now: of the feast. And after the Doxology with the Trisagion - his Troparion, Glory, Both now: of the feast, and everything else, as at Great Matins.
 421: ##### 2.14.1.5 At the end: Troparion of the saint, Glory, Both now: of the feast
 422:   * If there be two saints, then the troparion of the first saint, Glory: of the second, Both now: of the feast.
 423: #### 2.14.2 AT THE HOURS
 424: At all: Troparion of the feast, Glory: at the 3rd and 9th - also to the saint. Kontakia - alternating, that is: at the 1st and 6th - of the feast, at the 3rd and 9th - to the saint.
 425:   * If two saints, then Glory: at the 3rd - to the first, and at the 9th - to the second saint. Kontakia: at the 3rd - to the first, at the 9th - to the second saint[^208].
 426: #### 2.14.3 AT THE LITURGY
 427: ##### 2.14.3.1 Antiphons in the Afterfeast of the Lord we take: two first - from the feast itself, third - general with the refrain of the feast, also and "Come, let us worship"; in the Afterfeast of the Theotokos antiphons so, as also on all days
 428: ##### 2.14.3.2 At the Entrance - Troparion, Glory, Both now: Kontakion of the feast, Trisagion
 429: ##### 2.14.3.3 Prokeimenon, Alleluia and Communion Hymn - of the feast, Apostle and Gospel - of the day. Instead of *“It is truly meet”* - Heirmos of the 9th Ode of the Canon of the feast with its refrain. Dismissal with the commemoration of the feast and of the saint[^209]
```
